resp.text:
Hi Laura, thank you for your review and star rating. Here at Best Buy, we aim to deliver top-notch service to our customers during their visit, and your three-star rating informs us there’s an opportunity to improve on this. Whenever you feel you aren’t receiving five-star service, we’d love to hear about it. I invite you to reach out to me at ReviewSupport@bestbuy.com if you’d like to share more about your experience. Thanks for shopping at Best Buy, Laura, and we hope to see you again soon.

Alex
Best Buy Support

Overall, burger tasted pretty good, could def use bigger helpings of the 5 toppings they offer (ketchup, mustard, pickles, relish, and onions).

Definitely not worth the money, as I could go to any other burger joint, and get a burger at least three times the size for that money.

Heck, I could go to McDonald’s and get 3 McDoubles for $5.97. It would be about 4 times the size of their burger and only cost an extra dollar.

name: Derrick Glander
text:
I'm not sure what all the fuss is about with these burgers. They have a major pro.. the bread is fresh baked and the burgers are high quality real beef. However they are expensive for what they are, and maybe it's because I like a lot of flavors on my burgers, but I've eaten at other burger places (not in Brookings) that I thought were better... for example Black Hills Burger and Bun in Custer, Texas Roadhouse in Rapid City, Bob's Carryout in Sioux Falls (they changed their name and don't sell the burgers anymore :( ) and if Culvers had better buns, I'd vote for them as well.

They're fine if you are in them for the nostalgia, or enjoy a simple burger with not a lot on them, but if you live in Rapid City, Sioux Falls, or somewhere else, in my opinion there's no major reason to drive out of your way to visit here to taste one. Ultimately it's your choice. :) They are very small and expensive for what they are. Good, but not great.

As I start traveling more outside the state I hope to sample some of the "best places" in other states and compare. If you're looking for a "best place" in this state I'd recommend going to Custer to Black Hills Burger and Bun and enjoy the hills. There's a number of other great burger establishments west river as well. Look em up.

name: Murry Smith
text:
Very clean and relaxing!
This place has to be South Dakota's best kept secret!
The staff are extremely friendly and helpful, they manictre the grounds as if it were a mansion, most of the camp sites are very spacious and give you a beautiful view of the lake.
The park rangers are also very nice and patrol quite often.
The views, serenity and peace of this park really does make a relaxing and enjoyable stay!
They have boat ramps on both sides of the lake with easy access in and out.
The bathrooms and showers are super clean and always well stocked.
This is our first time visiting and it won't be our last!
If you're looking for peace, quiet, scenery and extreme cleanliness, you'll find it all here!

text:
One of our favorites state parks on this 5 year journey RV’ing the US. Very clean park. Check-in was smooth and staff was friendly. Campground includes boat ramp, tent camping, cabins, kids playground and dedicated swimming area off the lake. Our campsite was level and site clean. Verizon phones got weak 4g. DirecTV (free standing satellite) had no issue getting signal. Campground is about 10mins from freeway (i90) and 30mins from a decent grocery store. Our only issue is the late checkout time, which is 4pm… so don’t arrive too early.  Reservations available online for this state park. While at this campground we visited Falls Park in Sioux Falls and the Corn Palace (disappointment).

Our family is currently traveling this beautiful country via RV style, and have been RV'ing for many years. Therefore, we have an idea between high-standard qualities and poor quality. We utilize Trip Advisor and Google to assist us on locating top attractions, tasty restaurants and exciting locations within our wonderful country. Follow our adventure via Facebook/Instagram; “Happy Campers 227”.

Is it good? Really, that depends on what you're searching for. Basic pet equipment is available and most of the major brands are stocked so if that's what you want, this is the place for it. If you want to buy something living, especially if that living thing is intended to be a pet, you might try a smaller pet store that's more likely to tend to the needs of their stock.

Was told they were full on appointments for awhile but they did walk-ins for nails and face trims and it was no problem when I came in.  This was okay which is what I  needed.   Came into tonight and was told no, and I overheard the lady in the back whining that tomorrow was better. The first lady then told me not now, but they could get me tomorrow morning maybe. I said tomorrow maybe was not better for me and said no thanks and left. This was a horrible first impression and I doubt that I will try again.  This also makes me question whether to continue shopping there at all, even though up to now I was a regular.

text: I love this mall and this part of town!  About 10 to 15 years ago the Western Mall was kind of on life support.  there wasn't much going on in there and it seemed like the hallways were filled with "walkers" who were trying to stay in shape and stay out of the weather.  Since then there has been a ton of really fun stores added and a giant makeover for the entire Mall has been applied.  Of course Scheels is awesome especially being an athlete.  but there are also some new fun restaurants there including some favorites like HuHot and Potbelly's.  I would highly recommend you take another look at this mall if you haven't been there lately!  You may find your Christmas shopping to be much more enjoyable and not come home with the same thing everybody else found at the other Mall.

resp.text:
Thanks for stopping by and supporting the light show! Typically the inside located businesses (where access is only in the indoor of the mall verses other stores like Best Buy, Scheels, Furniture Mart, Eileens Cookies, Hu Hot, AR workshop, etc with outside access), are closed evenings. These are typically businesses that are non-retail and hours are 8-5 pm, so during the light show they would all be dark and look empty.

It turns out she never wrote the number down so we were never going to get a bus without me saying something... And while she did Apologize the point is how did you not write us down when we arrived I'm a little confused here because there was nobody else there other than her talking to her little friends at the hostess counter... Once we were seated the drinks and the food came out relatively fast... The food was okay I guess I was expecting something different but overall not a bad experience but the first impression going in with the mess up at the hostess table just kind of set the tone for the evening....

Everything was hot and fresh and this was completely unbeatable for the price. We've eaten at a few more expensive brunch buffets with cold food, food shortages, and limited options, so we will definitely be back for the Chevys brunch.

name: Miranda Sullenger
text: Service was great. Very friendly.

name: Dave Kosters
text: Chevys was awesome and no masks required!! Double awesome

name: Mariah Rus
text: Delicious food + fast, friendly service! The chips + salsa are always a hit. Kass was a great waitress, especially with our large group - thanks!

name: William Bonner
text: Food needs to be flavored salsa was blah, wet burrito was more wrapped with flour tortilla than chicken stuffing I had go use a knife to cut the burrito

name: E.M. Olsen
text: I have eaten here for years and have always had excellent service and food. Unique salsa and the best flautas you will ever have! Try the jalapeno margarita, it is a great twist!

name: Terry Snow
text: Way over crowded. No social distancing. Felt uncomfortable.

name: tammi strong
text: Awesome service

name: Todd McKissick
text: Very expensive. Horrible 'extra flavor' in steak fajita. No shrimp enchiladas, closest was with crab and disgusting green sauce, touted as alfredo with a kick. Refried beans have burnt flavor by design. Even the Pepsi was very flat. $37 to fill up on rice and chips.

name: Kelly Hornsby
text: Arrived about 7, 7:30? Told wait was 40 minutes, ok figured there'd be a wait on a Saturday night. Except then what we presumed was a manager came out & told the three "hostesses" standing at the podium to tell people the wait would be 45 minutes to an hour!! In the maybe 15 minutes or so we waited we overheard someone else we assumed was a manager tell new people arriving that the kitchen was backed up. This person also stood there talking to the three at the podium telling them people were getting upset & made it sound like it was getting to be a bad & perhaps somewhat out of control situation. It soon became clear that we didn't know WHEN we'd be seated OR eating so we left!! Had a very nice meal with immediate seating at Puerto Vallarta on East 10th Street.

name: Marty Hogan
text: I always like eating here.  Big helpings of food and not too expensive.  Drink specials always make my wife happy.  Serving staff is friendly and quick.  I have never had bed service here.  The chips and salsa ruin the meal for me cause I gorge on them.  Warm chips are always good.

name: Mike Loween
text: Smothered burrito is really good.

name: Bev Chase
text: Great food, great service, and the best chips and salsa.

name: michael sharp
text: Overall 4/5!!! How you guys handled COVID 19 precautions 2/5!!! Food was good and had chicken fajitas. I was here on July 18th, 2020 and sat on the patio when it was 95 degrees but felt good and shaded.  It felt weird because I sat on the patio like I always do when eating out during this pandemic and I am from Omaha Nebraska by the way and I was travelling to the Black Hills of South Dakota. There was no social distancing and only 2 employees (both servers) were wearing a mask. None of the 2 managers that I saw wore a mask and there was no communication on who had the patio for service and ended up seeing 3 servers serving the patio hmmm. In Omaha, tables are spread out at least 6 feet apart or people being sat at every other table and most places people are wearing masks.  I definitely felt like an outsider when it came to this.

name: jeremy michaelson
text: First time there. Good food and service

name: Marty Westra
text: Had a great dinner tonight with friends.  It was pretty busy, but it didn't seem to affect the wait staff or kitchen.

name: Kimberly Puhrmann
text:
Oh where do I begin with this place....well as you can see from my picture, my drink was served to me with dried lettuce stuck to the glass. When looking at the menu, wow! I guess not everyone knows what true Mexican food is. Everything was smothered in at least 2 different types of peppers, not one source of meat did not have it. When we asked our waitress if that could be an options, she informed us no. I explained I was born and raised on the border of Mexico. This was not true Mexican food. She then rolled her eyes and told me it was Tex-Mex! I told her sorry, try again, I was from Texas and trust me, it's not tex-mex. She rolled her eyes again and walked off. My husband paid for our two drinks which came to $6.20. We left and will never go back
I'm sorry to say but this place is a huge joke!

name: Jocelyn Lewis
text: Chevys was amazing!  The shrimp and crab enchiladas are seriously so delicious!

name: Moe Jonathan
text: Amazing Mexican restaurant! The food is terrific and the staff is extremely kind.

name: James Halterman
text: Great service and food. Thank you Steven.

name: Lizzy Reck
text: Chevys NEVER disappoints! One of my favorites is the flautas which are always crispy and always cooked to perfection, not to mention that jalapeno jelly that goes with it (to die for). Add a margarita with it and your meal is perfect.

name: Dee Farnham
text: Loved it!!!!!!!!!! Margarita great like always. (Half off Tuesday ) ! grill fajitas mix  , Great!  Fresh avocados mix at the table. Loved it. Fried ice cream. For 2 on the house. Priceless. For my daughter and son-in-law Anniversary. Mexico gave us wonderful memories and so did Chevys. Thanks

name: Jacob Carsten

name: Jon Morrill

name: jeremy salonen
text:
The food is the best mexican in Sioux Falls.  Perfectly seasoned and prepared.  Perfect texture in the tamales.  Guacamole was seasoned just to accent the avocado.  Their corporate chefs know mexican food.  And local managers are able to hire chefs to prepare on the best price.
Unmatched quality in Sioux Falls.

They have a buffet on Sundays and it’s a pretty good deal and value. Parking was a struggle as I made the wrong turn into Sams Club. I was unable to get a free WiFi which is why they don’t have 5 stars.

name: Ben J

We asked another waitress but were told "I'm not your server" so we never got it.  Food, service, and basic facilities were all well below average.  Don't waste your time

text:
Sub par. If you know how microwaving food gives it a sort of mishmash of blah flavor then you know what the food here tastes like.

I ordered the from the specials menu. I had the Mango Mama-sita and the fajitas combo.

The Mango Mama-sita was weakly alcoholic and very sweet. Which may be a selling point for some but lacking any taste of mango is does not sell it for me.

The fajitas combo managed to ruin fajitas. I could not taste the beef or the beans and the texture was like something out of the microwave. The rice tastes like catsup. The onions and peppers are clearly baked, not sauteed.

It's like the management doesn't care whether I like the food.

The service was prompt and courteous and the only thing about this place better than standing outside in the rain.

text: My wife purchased something for my Father's Day gift on a Friday after work. She needed my truck to haul it home, so we loaded up the entire family to go pick it up the following Saturday. She called 30 minutes before they got there and let them know we are coming, as we have younger kids and kids don't like to sit in a truck in a parking lot. She goes inside and proceeded to stand at customer service for over 20 minutes while she waits for someone to bring the item out. After 30 minutes she asked for a return. We left empty handed while having wasted over an hour of time on a weekend. We won't be going back. Customer service is literally the easiest thing to get right, as it doesn't cost anything. Unless you can answer your own questions and physically pull the item yourself, I would never go there. Even then, the prices are nothing special.

So I just ordered it online for in store pickup. 4 hours later I call the store after not getting anything but an order confirmation wondering where my stuff is, I was very polite the woman who finally answered after it rang for 5 minutes was extremely rude. She said they are busy and I should get an email soon. Another 3 hours later still nothing. The website now says this item is no longer sold. Ive cancelled the order as clearly they were trying to bait and switch me. I'll buy the same thing from another store for less money and have it shipped. Will not be giving this place another dime, I buy a tool from a hardware store chances are pretty good I need it right now. Im lucky my old drill still works. Anticonsumer to the core.

Had no problems finding what I wanted. The help was there and very helpful and friendly.

New posting: May 2019, had several problems this time. Enough to make me mad and decide not to go there again. Salesman ordered the wrong item I wanted. When it was delivered I got 1 of 3 items that was correct. I called the store and that was when the problems really started. Since the salesman ordered the wrong item, they were telling me that I was wrong. Finally they said they will fix the order and get me what I wanted. However, when the next delivery came, instead of the items that were missing I got 4 items. 1 was one that was missing. The others had nothing to do with the order. I called again and now it was just a continuous circle with customer service. I was told the store manager would call me, but that never happened. After talking to the store manager several days later, I believe no one even talked to him about my problem. I'm really sure that no one in that store knows what is going on.
I'm still waiting for the third part of my order, which I have been informed it will be delivered this next Thursday. This is the third delivery for the three items in my order. At 90 miles away that becomes a 540 mile trip to make what should have been a 180 mile round trip.

text: Initially an excellent place to eat.  Food prices were reasonable.  Portions great.  Now prices have sky rocketed. Portions are small.  Service is poor. Chicken strips and shrimp were over cooked bordering on burned.  When brought to the attention of our server we were comped $2 total. Linch for 3 adults and a child with no alcohol and 2 waters was $74

resp.text:
Good evening Michele,

Thank you for taking the time to leave us a review. After looking through tickets and speaking with our staff over past weekend I am not able to locate your ticket.

We appreciate your feedback on the shrimp and chicken strips. I will discuss this with our kitchen manager to follow up with proper cooking times. And I hope you give us another chance as they are two of our most popular items.

As to the portion sizes, with umpires menu, we have actually increased the portion size of our more popular items. But unfortunately We have had to increase the price of a few items on our menu too (Mainly our Jumbo Shimp, Steak and a few select appetizers) These prices were increased to cover the increased cost from our supplier.

Good news though when we released our new menu, we actually lowered the cost on several items, added several new and unique food choices bringing our menu up to 6 total pages of options for the whole family. So please try some of the new amazing dishes. Especially our new Pretzel Style Cheeseballs! (Yum)

If you have any other concerns please contact us during the day and ask for Tony. He would be happy to assist you and help with any of your concerns.

Bailey (our waitress) was very friendly and that was the only enjoyable part of the meal. Then upon looking at reviews here, I see the owner has reviewed his own company. Pretty unethical. While I won't be back for food, hopefully they can get the event center up and running in a more professional manner than their restaurant. The attached photo is of the owners review.

text: We shop at this Walmart quite often since it is the closest one to us. Right now it is under construction and it is really hard to find what you are looking for. Hopefully when they are done it will be a better shopping experience. Most of the time, they are stocked with items. The cleaner section is pretty bare and has been since Covid started. They have a bakery, pharmacy, order pick up, and an auto center. There is some staff that is really friendly and others are not. They do seem to keep closing doors. As of today, you can only enter and exit through the door by the produce. Makes the parking lot a nightmare over there. I went through the self check out and the lady working was really nice and pleasant and she washed down each station after they were used. When college is in, the store is a lot more packed and seems busier since it is right across the street. We try and do all of our shopping early to miss more crowds if we can. There is a Runnings, Lowes, car dealership, Perkins, Culvers, Taco Bell, and a hotel all in the same area where you pull in and out so it does get quite congested sometimes trying to get around.

I think the staff that helped during the event also did an wonderful job making us feel welcome and well provided for. We had a great selection of speakers and an incredibly well received keynote speaker that really brought a new light into the teaching profession. I think if Sioux Falls continues to offer spectacular venues such as the Sioux Falls Convention center, the city will continue to grow and prosper. Thank you Sioux Falls and Denny Sanford for providing such an incredible convention center that teachers such as myself can visit and feel welcome and well taken care of. name: Steve Buysman
text: Many of the tools are great at a nearly unbeatable price. I have and will continue to buy many tools here. Stay away from the hand tools (sockets, ratchets, box wrenches, etc.) as the quality lacks. Instead gravitate toward the power tools and more exotic tools. Air compressors, electric grinders, drills, etc. Are all of high quality and have comparisons so you can find the right one for your budget. Higher end or more exotic tools (English wheels, electric or pneumatic planishing hammers, sheet metal benders/brakes may not live up to a higher quality American made product but also reflect a good entry level tool. Start here to build your skills and try new things. Then if/when a high end tool breaks buy an American made product to replace it.

text:
This store has your staples and I am definently thankful for Sunshine when we cannot or do not want to travel for groceries. Their quality of their produce, although not equal to Hyvee in Sioux Falls but equal to Brookings Hyvee, is by far superior to Walmart. The fact some of you buy meats and produce at Walmart is beyond me. Yuck. Sunshine does a good job and I've lived in many different states and towns. This is a good store. Prices aren't really any higher than Hyvee and I love their discount days when they mark down their spinach and meats for quick sale! Those are my favorites and sure does help on a budget.

We have a lot of people here that are not Hispanic or white, we could really use more ethnic choices. Seriously there are six types of boring white rice but nothing fun to make a Biryani with? I would have given five stars if only you take into consideration your ethnic population in Madison. Although I think they have a fairly nice selection of Hispanic foods.

Bring your own bags and they give you a discount and dont be lazy, walk your own cart back into the store. I'd laugh to see you whine about Aldi's. Murica'!

This is the type of small town, off the beaten path bar and grill you always hope you are going to find.
The menu had plenty of options and they all sounded good. I went with my bar and grill standard - a burger with a side of cheese curds.  The burger was fresh, perfectly cooked and served on a quality bun. As for the side, I only have one criteria for good cheese curds; they need to be cooked in a clean fryer with good oil - they hit both marks and served up a tasty basket of curds.
Great food, great service and fair prices.  If you're in the area, drive a few extra miles to experience this back road gem.

name: T Maxson
text:
There has been a noticeable shift over the last two years in the lack of inventory on the shelves. This goes beyond the "Toilet Paper Covid" rush. This is across the board and seems to affect every department. I spoke to some department managers as well as some CSM's about this on different occasions and they also notice that there is a significant change in the way Walmart is stocking. I would love to say this is for the better but it's not. I am a huge fan of JIT and LEAN but this particular store just doesn't seem to understand principles of supply, demand, safety stock , etc inside the supply chain galaxy. Other Walmart's in Sioux Falls seem to be fairly well stocked albeit the occasional mainstay may go missing but this Walmart on 85th and Minnesota is plainly missing the boat. Here are some specifics. 1) On any given day you would think you could pop into your local WM and find name brand Diet Coke, Bread, Milk, or any number of regular sundries that Mr. and Mrs. America tend to buy on a regular basis. After finding these items out of stock repeatedly and I being a retired nerd with some time on my hands decided to see if what I perceived was actually a reality. Was WM really out of basic, name brand items most of the time or was it just when I happened to be looking for them? I began my nerd fest by charting 12 trips over 3 months and arrived randomly at 7am, 2pm, 6pm and 10pm. I found that out of those twelve trips this Walmart was repeatedly out of at least 3 and sometimes up to 5 name brand items I had on my list. By the way I'm talking common items like 2% milk, Krispy Kreme K Cup Coffee, Kraft Single Slice Cheese, Hormel Microwave Bacon,  Cottage White Bread, Popsicle brand pop sickles, Strawberry Poptarts, Minute Maid orang juice, International Delight Hershey's Chocolate Creamer, Gatorade Cool Blue, JIF Peanut Butter.......I think you get the point. Name brand items;  repeatedly OUT OF STOCK. Now one could be asking themselves why would a $426 Billion dollar corporation not have a better inventory system than this or was there some other reason these items are always out of stock? Could it be a strategy to sell their own Walmart branded items which by the way have an incredibly larger margin than traditional name branded items? I think not. Many retail stores have tried to be single suited and carry primarily their own branded merchandise and many have failed because they ignored the cries of Mrs. Homemaker and her buying power! (Remember: SEARS, Steinmart, Levits, Kids R Us, 365, A&B...?) The list goes on and on of chains that tried the "one and done" approach to selling their own brands and eventually all failed miserably.
I believe that this WM is just not paying good attention to the demand cycle and needs of it's customer base. During random talks with department heads it was clear that they are equally frustrated by being repeatedly "out" of some of their most popular items. It's not just once or twice here folks, it's systemic and prolific throughout the store! I did have a chance to speak with "Dan" who was supposedly one of the store managers to vent my belief and he of course was extremely nice, professional but eventually gave me the party line of acting shocked and in utter disbelief that his store could be out of so many items at one time. He promised to look into this at once and get back to me! He asked for specifics; of which I gladly provided. I never heard from Dan again even after leaving a few messages. Disappointed that this little experience has taken 6 months to complete from( July 2019 to December 2019 ) and nothing has improved even before the Covid train ran everything off the tracks! I gave up and wrote this review. Again, just to qualify this, they are NOT out of all items all the time. Just a disproportionate amount of NAME BRAND items that people expect you to have! Summary; shopping at Walmart on 85th and Minnesota is like going to Vegas and always expecting to win more often than you lose. Vegas was built to fool you into giving them money and apparently so is this store.

text:
I am totally done with Madison's McDonald's!
Just ordered a double quarter pounder with cheese meal, waited in the parking lot for fries, drive 3 blocks home, fries were cold!
I hadn't eaten all day and as I ate my burger, I thought it tasted odd. Then I looked at it and it was raw!!!
I call the store and I'm getting a refund but the excuse was the cold temperatures froze the "fresh, never frozen" meat!
I drive truck and haul a refrigerated trailer hauling everything from me cream to produce and rest assured, the excuse I was given was a BS lie!
In subzero temps in the -30's, I've NEVER had a load freeze that wasn't supposed to freeze!
$11.44 for cold fries and a raw burger is NOT a value and being told a BS excuse then get a snotty attitude from the night manager when I catch her in a bold face lie is also NOT a value!
Considering past issues with Madison McDonald's, I have no desire to spend my money here anymore!
It used to be a decent and reasonably priced place to grab some food but over the past few months, it's turned into an overpriced not too good place.
Too bad for them that they'll lose business in a small town!

text: This Starbucks is located inside of Hyvee and does NOT have a drive through. Once you get inside the store, it is right in the front through the doors. Also keep in mind that this location gets a lot of traffic being located in a strip mall and the parking lot gets quite packed. Would be nice if they were able to move to a bigger location. I have gotten a coffee from here a few times while I went shopping and haven't had any issues with their service or the quality of the drinks. Because I am treating myself, I normally get a fancier type of coffee than just a regular cup of joe. I have also had the baristas make my girls a non caffenated drink similar to what I get and they are always super helpful in picking that out for them. I do feel that Starbucks is quite expensive so I save up gift cards and such from Verizon or other sources before deciding to stop in. This location always has some little tables and shelves set up with Starbucks items that are for sale as well. I think they have a decent menu. A little smaller than ones I have been to that are a stand alone shops, but enough options to find something tasty.

text: I really enjoy shopping here because of all the products they have and their sales. No matter what part of town you live in, there's a Hy-Vee not far away. A couple of years ago, they added Aisles Online. You pick out your groceries online, pay for them, pick out the day and time you want to pick up your groceries and go to their pick-up spot and call them. All for a low fee. text: Hyvee has a reasonable and ever expanding selection of grocery and general household needs. Their pharmacy is fantastic and they are very polite and friendly. Every employee there seems to be perfectly happy to go out of their way to help you and determined to get you an answer. I have even had employees take the initiative to check with other hyvee locations to find where the product I wanted was. I didn't ask them to do that they chose to. I also love their international sections and that they are bringing in lots of new items and cultures food's for people to broaden their horizons with. The store is always clean and the meats and deli always have beautiful looking products and the gourmet cheese is fantastic and they will help you find one that you want. They have really good deals on different meals there each week at their hot food counters and their produce tends to be fresher than most other stores. I also really like that their managers care when you have comments or suggestions and will go out of their way to help customers including running, not walking, to get replacement products if an egg is broken or a milk started leaking or a tear in a bag and also I have had cashiers notice and point out to me that something is damaged and call for replacements. I appreciate their honesty and caring.

text:
I enjoy going to this hyvee.  It is conveniently placed in Sioux Falls.  The customer service is excellent with employees willing to drop what they are doing and assisting you in trying to find that last item that you can't find.  The will also summon all available people to man the registers when the lines get more then two deep.  It makes it easy to get out of there in a timely fashion.

There are a couple of downsides to this hyvee.  The first is that it is not very large.  They usually have the ingredient I am looking for but the selection is pretty thin with usually just one or two brands as an option.   I will point out that they do have a lot of food you wouldn't normally think to find in a Hy-Vee.  For example, they have crocodile.  It's in the frozen section.  The second downside the kitchen (not the market restaurant they have.). If you go to the counter that contains all of the no Chinese, Italian food, it is dried out and nasty looking.  It's sad because I really enjoy Hy-Vee's meatloaf but haven't had it since I started shopping here.

text:
Waited over 1 hour today to ask a few questions about upgrading phones. It'd be beneficial if Verizon hired some process engineers for customer flow. There's no reason for the consistent wastes seen while waiting. Is there really only 1 tape dispenser? Wouldn't think it'd be too expensive to get one at every desk, especially since they're charging me over 800 for a new phone. They have all of this "advanced technology" to help speed up the process, but rather brings it to a halt when it doesn't work, or dies. If you believe so much in technology, why are we using paper and phone calculators to estimate the changes in the bill? There's a wired computer right in front of you. Are there no programmers that could create a real simple program that generates the bill change cost? Maybe if the plans weren't so complicated, training, flow, and customer turnover would be easier. One last comment, you should speed up your WiFi. There's absolutely no reason a customer and employee should wait over 10 min while a phone updates over a measly 20 Mbps.

I used to get a new phone every 2 years on the old plans. Waited over over 3 years this time, and will continue to wait, because of the new new new plans. Seems like every time i go to Verizon, they have this brand new plan that's "cheaper" than the one your on, but always has a little fine print. Paying over 800 for a phone is absurd. Paying it by month is not only unethical for the american public, it's greedy.

The employees here didnt fail me, the management, training, and scope of the company did. Get a grip Verizon, or get out of the game.

text:
I had run out of overripe bananas with which to make cakes for Christmas gifts. I called a hometown grocer, but they didn't have any. I knew it would do me no good to call the warehouse or big discount stores. I thought, "Who else is a old-fashioned hometown grocer" and Sunshine came to mind.

I called and asked if they had any overripe bananas they would sell me. He said they had a pound or two and said they would put them in a box for me at the service desk. Yes! Mission accomplished! And, I get to look at their meat!

Ordinarily I don't get to shop this store because I live on the W side of the city, but I was close that day. I bought their meat before, and, if they were closer, I would buy more.

I put my box of bananas in my cart, found another overripe batch with the other bananas, and I grabbed them, too. I bought some pretty sweet potatoes and made my way to the meat.

They had good prices on several cuts. I bought chicken thighs and split breasts and a pretty roast I plan to cut into stew meat.

I enjoyed my trip through the aisles. I hope it won't be long before I get to go back.

I called the store and was told customer service would have my name and next time I could get a free one. Tonight I thought I would give them another shot and get my free chicken and get the rest of my groceries. I planned on spending about $50 but ended up spending nothing! After them going through 2 books of people who were owed replacement products they didn't find my name. The manager who let 2 men yell at each other said I needed my receipt. What??!! I was never told I would need it! I walked out without buying anything! It worked out for me though because I went to Hyvee and bought my chicken, sides and the rest of my groceries for $35 without listening to customers yelling at each other. I have no plans on ever going back to this store ever.

text: I was absolutely disgusted going into this store. There was stuff everywhere. Nothing was in it's place and there was stuff in carts, boxes, and just laying all over including on the floor creating a trip hazard and making it super hard to move around and get to product. Looked like maybe it was clearence stuff. A lot of it was in carts, boxes, and tubs lining the path to the register and there was so much stuff around the pop, I couldn't even get to it so I went elsewhere for that. On the way out I stopped to use the restroom and it was filthy. There was poop in and on the toilet, I didn't even sit all the way to pee. The floors were covered in filth and there was no where to hang a purse or bags so either risk setting things on the dirty floor or use the sink. I chose the sink. There really needs to be some new management in that store, I went during the week, during the day when you would expect a manager to be there taking care of their store and making sure things look presentable but just a young girl and guy in there. I will never go back to this store. I've never seen anything like it and as a former conveinence store manager, if this were my store, I would be embarrassed.

name: Beverly White
text: My first experience at Terrace Park I had not too long moved to Sioux Falls, South Dakota from Los Angeles, California, big change in life style.  While looking at the J,,apanese Garden me and my son found a beautiful garden snake.  The snake blended in with the rest of the garden.  For a moment I didn't know what I was looking at.  Five days ago I came upon another garden snake, this time I knew what to do.  I jumped into the air as high as I could and made a B-Line straight to my car and didn't look back.  This may seem strange but in Los Angeles the only place to see snakes was in the zoo.  It was like the snake and I were running in a marathon trying to see who could get to Sunshine Market the fastest.  Of course, I won.  My reward was a ice cold coke.

name: Scott McVicker
text: The food and service, always consistently great.  Their unwavering connection to local schools and sports is incredible.  For me and my family, that is #1.  I moved here in 2004, and we have kept my wife's connection to TC's all the way through, even when we lived in the Twin Cities, Georgia, Iowa, Florida, and Wisconsin.  The best booth, in my humble opinion, is the southeastern most booth with the greatest teams in South Dakota history on display.  Every seat in the house is great.  If you have the chance, try that booth (and the cajun chicken, wrap, soups, salads, specials,...any and all of the menu) and find your own unique experience with a great local restaurant, rooted in the past and promoting the future.  Second to none.

name: Dori Spring

name: Brett Tedmon
text:
Talk about a diamond in the rough! This is a fantastic, friendly little sports bar. The staff is excellent! The drinks are excellent! The food is outstanding from simple sandwiches to delicious seafood and fine meats. I stumbled upon the place by coincidence because my auto insurance company happened to be next door and I'm sure glad I did.
It's a great experience to watch some sports, have a couple really good cocktails or beers and enjoy some awesome food!
I highly recommend T.C.'s Referee!!

text: I am so glad someone local told us about this hidden gem. The service is fast, accurate, and friendly, the interior is fun with wood paneling and TVs everywhere for sports. The soups are great, I don’t know what day they serve jalapeño cheese soup is served but it alone is worth a trip, wow, pleasantly spicy, tangy cheesiness, and a generous size bowl. The hot wings are also very good, always well cooked, meaty and great sauces. Great burgers and a variety of other dishes too. The hot hamburger is a standout too, burger on toast smothered with mash potatoes and gravy.

text: I had a lot of recommendations to go here. Honestly, I was a little disappointed with some of the food. There was A LOT of pink for a medium well burger, and the portion sizes seemed small, but the wings and service were indeed amazing. name: mrsmel269
text: Frankman Motor Company is a bit off the beaten path in Sioux Falls. However, if you know Sioux Falls it really doesn't take long to get to different ends of the city. It is in a  very nice area that is expanding, but isn't overrun with businesses. They have a nice sized lot with the vehicles and they have separate buildings for the sales part and for the service part. We called to check availability on a vehicle and they gave us the information, but were not pushy about coming in. We decided to go in and check it out. The first thing that was nice is we went and checked the car out first, it was easy to find in the lot and we didn't have anyone stalking us down. Inside, the staff was friendly and showed us to the person we talked to on the phone. The inside is clean and smells like they clean and wipe it down often. The bathrooms were also clean.. They have some nice older model cars inside. We were told to take a nice long test drive to really get a feel for the car, which was awesome. They are very confident with the cars they put on the lot and that is great. All the cars look like they are in great condition and they seem to pay attention to detail in cleaning them up and putting them on the lot. Also, they have so many pictures on their website of their inventory, it is amazing. I don't know about you, but I hate going to a website and seeing 3 pictures of a vehicle. Makes me think they are hiding something. Not this place. You will get over 50 pictures! They did not push us on the sale, they were open to seeing what they could do to benefit both us and them as well. All in all, we were very pleased with them and would do business with again. It is definitely worth the drive to check out their inventory if you are in the market for a new car.

text:
Had been out to the vintage car section four times.  Settled on a truck and after test driving, discovered it needed work done to be stopped safely.
First the owners son acted as if he had studied at the "sleazy car salesman" school and graduated with honors.  Seriously, this guy tried to tell me that a. The brakes were fine and b. he wasn't going to lose money to me by fixing the brakes... seriously. Told him to have his dad contact me. Dad did and we agreed with Xmas season in full swing and me going out of town, he would get the brakes fixed (surprise, they were broken) and then upon return, we would seal the deal.  I come back and call with money in pocket to pick up my new classic truck.  Dad comes on the phone to say they had sold it while I was away.  They didn't even bother to call me to tell me that the purchase was in jeopardy.  I guess the fruit doesn't fall far from the tree. Avoid at all costs.

name: Thomas Sigler
text:
Well since I got a phone call, asking me about this review.  I will update it..

YES! I got 400 off for a new top, the guy in the finance department says, Oh I tired 4 banks for a loan for this jeep. Well after checking my credit report. He flat out lied, unless they do it without pulling a credit report........  credit karma is great..........So I paid them $11,044.00 cash, to get my jeep.

It's now at a shop getting the front end redone and brakes done. Had great tires on it, but they no longer make that tire in that size. Had to swap all of them off for new tires, at a cost of $1,400.00, because the spare is a 31×10.50r15. The tires on the jeep are 32×12.50r15

So let's recap, needed a new top got 400 off for the top, supposedly ran 4 banks to get the finance on it. That was a lie. Almost 5 grand later the front end will finally be right. Also had to change the tires on it, due to the spare and the tires being on the jeep not matching. So, yes I gave it a 1 star rating, but in my defense. Anyone else would've given it a 0 star rating.

name: george peters
text: Frankman Motor Company, "The home of buyers remorse".I bought a used car from Frankman Motor Company several years ago. Within two weeks, I had nothing but problems with it. It would die at stoplights, something would go wrong with it every month. The transmission went out. When I took the car in to Frankman to ask if they would stand by it, they told me I bought it as-is and would not stand by it. Not even a repair discount! They gave me only 200 dollars for my trade-in which was a much more reliable car. What a waste of several thousand dollars! Will never go back there again! I've had better luck from cars I bought from the salvage yards for three or four hundred dollars! Back in those days there was no lemon law on used cars so it was buyer beware. South Dakota generally has honest, trustworthy; friendly people, however not this place! I dont know how they stay in business! P.S. I wonder how much these people got paid for their recent, positive reviews? Huh?

name: Christine Bofenkamp
text:
I just purchased an Infiniti FX35 (2011) from Jim Swanson at Frankman Motor Company.

Jim was great to work with and was honest with us all the way. From trading in our old car to signing on the dotted line for a new car Jim was open, honest and completely trustworthy. While purchasing the vehicle we worked it out so they could do some minor fixes for us.  Did they have to do this? No. Did they? Yes.

They made sure that we would leave happy and with a great vehicle.

From the perspective of someone who has run businesses for years, I want to remind everyone that for every bad review there are hundreds of happy customers that don’t even think about reviewing a company.

So, if you need a new car and you want to work with someone who will treat you like family, contact Jim Swanson.  He, the owners and staff will do their absolute best to make you and your family happy. They have been fantastic and I recommend them.

Thank you for everything Jim!

He found a car for less than our price, with less miles on it and was still willing to negotiate.
Our salesman was Sean Speth. He was fast, friendly, knowledgeable, and patient. He answered our questions and called us when he said he would.
He now has a lifetime customer with us.

name: Drew S.
text: I took my ‘14 Taurus to Frankman Motors and am only disappointed and upset from the service I received a couple weeks ago. Three weeks prior, I had my battery tested elsewhere and found out it was slowly beginning to read a low amperage. Frankman's performed an inspection with an oil change and tire rotation and told me in person and recorded on paper that the battery was currently reading the full 650 amps. This was impossible. When I replaced the old battery today (shortly after visiting Frankman's) I realized the battery had a hole in it and it was leaking battery acid. Frankman's very obviously did not check the battery amperage, and I had no idea my battery was going bad so quickly. Not a good experience.

name: Hugo Hackenbush
text: $11 admission.  Plan on 45 minutes. Absolute maximum 3 hours if you read every word on every sign and study every object. Strongly recommend downloading the app: "Mammoth Site Tour" for an explanation of bones - there's no signage or explanation when you're looking at them - you don't even know what you're looking at or for. There's a 10 minute introductory film, 3000 square foot+- dig, a dozen general overview/ geology signs, a 1000 square foot+- area with more interesting items, and the gift shop.  (I'd also recommend the impressive local museum in town filling all rooms in a 3 story 1893 school.)

resp.text: Dear Hugo, Thank you for taking the time to review The Mammoth Site. We appreciate your feedback and your input about our signage. The Mammoth Site works hard to provide the best experience possible for all of our visitors. If you would like to discuss more about our signage and how we could have improved your experience, please call us at 605-745-6017 and ask for our Public Relations Coordinator. We look forward to hearing from you.

name: Ty Walsh
text: I've lived in a lot of places and love museums. This is possibly one of the COOLEST things I've ever seen. The display and background information is phenomenal. The fact that you're looking at a current dig site is even more impressive. The preservation and active scientific research/content/discovery is beyond anything a museum could offer. Im so thankful for this place and what they're doing. They could of just dug everything up, sent it to a museum and built houses over the site. How fortunate we are ❤

resp.text: Greetings Ty, We are so happy that you found The Mammoth Site to be "one of the coolest things you have ever seen." We appreciate your feedback and your five-star review. We hope you will visit us again someday!

We do offer programs in the summer called The Mammoth Site Excavation and Preservation Program where individuals can sign up to come and dig at The Mammoth Site. name: Deborah Barron Brown
text: Maybe 3.5.   I do think the find is extraordinary and the story of how all these prehistoric animals came to be found in one place is amazing. The viewing was great but I think better lighting could have been used.  You are allowed to take pics. It is a current dig site so it is nice they even have tours. It was not a challenging walk. The tour guy was a young high school senior/college kid and his delivery was amateurish.  He was nice and he did engage the younger kids.  We came in June and had a 15 minute wait.  I guess I wanted a more _?__ experience .  I left feeling meh.  Something is missing from it.

resp.text: Dear Deborah, Thank you for taking the time to review The Mammoth Site. We appreciate your feedback about your recent visit. We are sorry to hear that something was missing from your experience. The Mammoth Site works very hard to make sure that our visitors have the best experience as possible. We take our reviews seriously and use them as training tools for our staff. We would like to hear more from you about what we could have done differently to have improved your experience at The Mammoth Site. If you would like to discuss this matter further please feel free to contact The Mammoth Site at 605-745-6017 and ask for the Public Relations Coordinator. We look forward to hearing from you.

name: David Clark
text: I had to be talked into coming here, but I was pleasantly surprised at how cool this place is. The tour guide was very informative. They provided headsets so you could wander off a little and take pictures during the tour without missing anything. They built a building over an excavation site. 60 mammoth remains have been discovered over the last 30 years. About one third of the excavation has been completed. If you go earlier in the day during the summer field season you should see the excavation in progress. Parking is free. Well worth the price of admission. The gift shop is very reasonably priced. A must see.

resp.text:

Greetings Sie Sar,
Thank you for taking the time to review The Mammoth Site and provide feedback from your recent visit. We are sorry to hear that you were disappointed with your visit to the Site. Our Summer Educational Programs typically end on August 15th. This year due to COVID-19 and limiting the number of participants in the classes, we had decided to extend for another two weeks, making the classes available Monday-Friday at two different times, until August 28th. Our sluice is still operating daily where visitors can purchase bags in our Gift Shop or Bonebed Bistro to use at the sluice to search for fossils or gems. We also have our Kids Cave and different exhibits throughout the museum. We are always looking for ways to improve our visitor experience and we appreciate your feedback.

resp.text:
Dear Veronica, Thank you for taking the time to review The Mammoth Site. The Mammoth Site is truly unique that it is an indoor active paleontological dig site and the only accredited museum in the Black Hills. The Mammoth Site boasts the largest concentration of Columbian mammoths in the world.
We understand that this Site may not be for everyone and we do appreciate the feedback provided by all our visitors. We take our reviews very seriously and use them as training tools for our staff. The Mammoth Site works very hard to provide the best experience possible for our guests. We would love to hear from you of what we could have done differently to have improved your experience. Please feel free to contact our Public Relations Coordinator at 605-745-6017 if you would like to discuss this matter further. We look forward to hearing from you!

We took the self guided tour around the site, fascinating to see the uncovered fragile fossilized bones of the giant Colombian mammoths. Interesting to learn about how many mammoths are believed to have drowned in the sinkhole.  The people at the register and gift shop were very friendly.

A worker did approach us part way during our guided tour and ask us to donate to a children's program. Normally i dont appreciate being approached but for the kids it was fine (:

resp.text: Greetings James, Thank you for taking the time to review The Mammoth Site. We appreciate your five-star review and feedback. We are glad you enjoyed your visit and found our "staff to be friendly". We apologize that you were approached during your tour to donate to our Educational Fund. We are currently hosting a Quilt Raffle to raise money for our Educational Programs and are asking our visitors in the Exhibit Hall and in our Gift Shop if they would like to purchase tickets. This shouldn't occur during a tour, so we are sorry for the inconvenience. We take our reviews very seriously and use them as training tools for our staff. Please feel free to contact our Public Relations Coordinator at 605-745-6017 if you would like to discuss this matter further. Once again we appreciate your feedback and we look forward to hearing from you.

text: It is the single most horrible costumer service experience of my whole life time!! This happened about a month ago because I couldn't find this store on google maps so I am writing a review now to warn people of the absolute disrespect and lack of customer service here. Anyway, so I walked in and they asked the usual "how may I help you?" I told them "I want to buy the new Galaxy S6, how much will it cost off contract?" then she pulls some random, high number out of her ass.. "that will cost you $900 with out a contract" she said almost frantically as if to intimidate me into signing up for a contract. I tried to tell her "there's no way, I know its not that high! it should be around $607-$647" but before I could even get the words out of my mouth she interrupts me at least 3 times and then appears to be upset now that I have corrected her. so I walked away to see how much it was, as I walked away I was told someone would be with me shortly... it was $647 as I had mentioned. so now I wanted to buy it off contract as I had planned to do in the first place. so I waited and waited for someone to help me as I looked at other phones. by this time I had waited for about half a hour and the store had been completely flushed out with new customers than what It had when I walked in. Now I was so fed up with the lack of customer service plus the initial horrible greeting I received on my way in that I did not even bother to ask anyone else for help, and so I walked out of the store. on my way out I noticed the greater smirking and glaring at me on my way out the door and never said another word to me. at that point I vowed to my self, "I will never come back here ever again!" and so I haven't. don't buy from these people. if they lack in the most basic professional customer service skills imagine the damage they could do to you're pocket book. and there's my two cents.

text: If I could, it would be "0".  I almost never bother with reviews or participate in the Google community, but this felt worth sharing.  I can't speak for how the food tastes because we never even got far enough into the experience to get any. This was hands down the worst service I've ever seen and I work in the food service industry.  There was only one waitress. There were 3 other tables that already had food, 1 other table that didn't.  The waitress was high school or college age with short hair and didn"t have a name tag. She started the experiance by audibly expressing irritation when the first two of our party sat down and told her that there would be two more joining.  After 5-10 minutes she finally took our drink order (4 waters) andy I told her we were ready to order too (she had her notepad).  She told us to "hold on" and walked away.  Several minutes later she came over to take the order, and 3 of our party ordered.  When I attempted to order the "three meat skillet" she told me that "that's not very good" (who does that to their employer?). I opted for the loaded baked potato instead and was told theyre not available.  I asked her what she recommended and she mentioned a couple burgers. I politely declined those and said I would like to have the "parmesan fries" I was in mid-sentence, asking if I could also have two eggs on the side when she cut me off by saying "I'll come back" and walked away....  We waited another five minutes for her to return to finish taking the order, when she didn't we got up and left.  Total experience was 15-20 minutes, she didn't even bother to bring us water.  If she's the person the owners choose to represent them to the public, I can imagine how bad the kitchen area must be.  I go in and out of restaurant kitchens all day for a living and I've learned that the quality of the employees out front seems to almost always have a direct correlation with how clean and well-managed the kitchen and other non-public areas are.  As I said, the worst service ever witnessed.

text: For 56 dollars and a family of four, the buffet missed on a few things. Stuffing was lacking decent flavor, the pasta was limp from soaking in water, ice cream machine was on the fritz, fried chicken was dry and hard.  Good points for corn, potatoes and gravy, diligent staff keeping beverages refilled. For the same price, could have had KFC or taco bell. Last item? Bourbon chicken? Don't try it. Nasty.

text:
To be honest I would just find a different buffet.

Definitely nothing spectacular or wonderful for buffet. There was seven of us who went and not one of us was thrilled. All of us could agree that we were disappointed in the options you had from the salad bar to the dinner section. We were expecting to have a great variety but were let down horribly bad. The food that we did eat was okay but they never had everything full. You had to wait a long time before they would feel things up. My son was waiting for chicken for an extremely long time before he was able to get just a piece. I definitely wasn't happy with the clam chowder and my daughter thought the red jello was gross. My nephew was really bummed out that they did not have any options for fruit. My husband had a hard time finding things to eat because it didn't look very appetizing.

text: Today was my birthday and they made it so special for me here. Even brought two different types of pie to my table and sing Happy Birthday to me. The chef's up at the grill cooking the steaks set me up with a full plate size steak all to myself. Couldn't be more happy, or more stuffed..... I shall return.

name: dave brosk
text:
I love golden corral and usually have a great experience. Unfortunately I had my first bad experience there. My waitress was extremely rude I couldn't believe it! She seemed more interested in talking to co workers than refilling drinks and taking care of my table. The way she talked was condescending and she never smiled. I usually get great service so maybe I caught someone having a rough day. We still tipped her well. Some of the food didn't seem up to temperature. Also I always get steak there and it's usually delicious but it was like trying to chew rubber and I couldn't even cut it with a knife(had it cooked medium). I spent 50  dollars all together for myself and two others and don't feel like I got my money's worth. On a positive note I will say that the desserts were delicious. This was my first time at this location and I feel discouraged to return which is disappointing because it's my favorite buffet style restaurant.

Update: After my visit a manager named Mary reached out to me to address my last visit. She heard my concerns and fixed the issues. I went back tonight and the food and service was great even on a busy saturday night. Its the excellent service I usually get visiting Golden Corral. Thank you for taking good care of your guests. See you next time!

The salad bar and dessert bar are better than many buffets, but you definitely don't get what you pay for unless you're there to behave as a glutton.

name: R. Thomas
text: HORRIBLE!  We ate here at the recommendation of a friend telling us it was much better than other buffets.  We were there on a not so busy night, but you could have fooled me.  Our waitress forgot about our drinks three times so we ended up helping ourselves, then got a scolding from the manager for being in an area only for employees.  They were out of several items of food.  The salad bar and the hot food section needed cleaning badly due to mixed foods and scraps all over.  We could clearly hear the manager yelling at 2 cooks and witnessed one manager picking up food (WITH HER FINGERS) out of the serving trays and eating it on the spot.  The ultimate thing that sent us running from the place... we witnessed the lead cook walking around cleaning up scraps and gathering them in his hand.  This would have been fine but he then threw them over cooked food (mashed potatoes, mac and cheese area).  We were flabbergasted, disgusted and apalled.  Made a beeline for the parking lot and never looked back.  We'll never visit again!

name: Jeannine Szostak
text:
So much history here! If you have the opportunity to come back at night, the laser light show is an unforgettable experience, and one which is free with your ticket from earlier in the day. It can be viewed from inside the memorial itself, or from the upper parking area; there are speakers that will allow you to hear the music from the parking lot.

To be fair, we visited Crazy Horse in July 2020, deliberately avoiding high traffic areas due to Covid. We’d done Mount Rushmore a couple years ago; it was incredibly crowded. This wasn’t that, which made it so much more pleasant, less touristy, more personal.

name: Acacia Willey
text:
When you look up the definition of disappointment in the dictionary you find Crazy Horse. At least that was the case for me. I first visited Crazy Horse in 1996, when I was 8. I was excited to come back and see the progression, but from the looks of it, and after reading other reviews it appears it hasn’t been worked on since the last time I saw it.

Okay, okay... my fault for being too caught up on nostalgia and not researching, but to charge an entrance fee is a bit much. It cost $15 to snap a picture from the parking lot. A closer view would’ve been an additional $125. Thank goodness it was just me in the car. Otherwise it would’ve been $30 for this picture (to enter).

name: David K
text: The history behind this memorial is amazing. It was inspiring to learn the inspiration behind the beginning of this memorial. I hope I am still around in 30 years when it is completed. If you get a chance to go to the top, I would definitely recommend going.

name: Brian Baker
text: Was here 20 years ago and it looks like there's been more attention and progress made on the welcome center area than on the mountain carving itself.  Still cool to visit though when you're in the area!

name: Andrew Weisz
text: Awesome experience! We got to hike to the top of crazy horse and were blown away by the detail of it. Such a cool monument! I'd definitely go to this instead of mount Rushmore. Its bigger, better, and you can see it evolve over time!

name: Robert Mitchell
text: Amazing place to visit. The volksmarch was Fantastic. Highly recommended to visit here. The visitors center packed full of history. A gift shop, food live performances and much more. See you next year.  Thank You.

name: Nyor Mirror
text:
I would hope that most people visit the Crazy Horse Memorial before or after they visit Mount Rushmore to allow themselves to see a different perspective (both literally and figuratively) between the Memorials.

Entrance fee for my son and I was $24. It was an additional $4 to take a bus to the bottom of the mountain for a slightly closer view (that we did not do). I also read that you could take a van to the arm of the mountain for $125 per person donation but it was never offered to us as an option. You have to remember that this project is privately funded, in fact, the original sculptor turned down two grants offered by the federal government.

I would agree with other reviewers that it is difficult to get a good view of Crazy Horse without binoculars or a camera with a telephoto lens. I suppose most get spoiled with all the angles and great photos you can get at Mount Rushmore.

I found that the 30 minute movie that provided the history of how the memorial came to fruition was the most interesting thing that we did. Some of the Lakota tribe did not want this memorial built because it was being built on sacred ground.

The museum is very organized, clean and provides the vision of the memorial and shows items, pictures and artifacts of the Native Americans. There is also live entertainment along with a night laser light show. We weren't able to see either because we were going to Custer State Park.

This will be the the largest sculpture and the 8th wonder of the world if and when it is ever completed which will not be in my or my son's lifetime seeing the progress since 1948. I would recommend visiting though just to further educate yourself and family about the history of our nation and how the memorials came to be.

text: Loved the museum and native dances, especially when they explained the history of the black hills, which was very intriguing. The music was amazing, and the monument was beautiful, although not being even close to completed. It is amazing and should be funded for by the government.

name: Eric Anderson
text: Just go!! Very interesting for sure. Ask for the pass, good for a return visit within the following three days. You can get that at the information desk. Very friendly staff. This mountain is still being carved. Also, there is a laser light show projected on the mountain. It starts around 9:30-10 and lasts quite some time.

name: Carissa Raye Todd
text: I've lived in the Hills for 5 years and never paid the entrance fee for Crazy Horse. Yesterday my friend and I finally bit the bullet and went with the intention of going to the face, I couldn't find any information online about how much it cost. When we get there, they say it's $125 per person (12 years- free), I understand that all the fees fund the project but that's insane.

I would prefer cheaper parking and entrance and an opportunity to donate money after you got to know the history of this place. text:
A must see when in the neighbourhood.
The entrance fee includes entrance to the museum and a nice movie of the story of the crazy horse memorial.
There is a small additional fee for the bustour that brings you too a nice viewing point.
With your entrance fee you also support the completion of this monument, which will be absolutely stunning once complete.
For now the work in progress and the story behind it are more then worth the visit.

text: Crazy Horse Memorial was build as a sign of brave native Americans who seeked for justice in the past. The hiking to the top is fun and there is a museum close by that people can learn about native Americans. It is a must see place in black hills.

text: Spectacular. Will return in 100 years when finished.

There are some scheduled Native American shows inside the cultural center.

text:
An amazing experience just with Mount Rushmore. This one might eventually be more magnificent, albeit at this point continues to be under construction.
As you see in pictures you can already see a lot of the massive monument. There is a great media presentation and artifacts walk. Along with a mirador that will easily have you staring for an hour.
There is a great display about the artist and many historic bits.
Easy parking, I cannot say enough about all the things close to rapid city, mount Rushmore being my top thing but crazy horse not to be missed and so many other things to do in the metro area. Loved it!

name: TW U
text: WOW!!!! I've been here 4 times in my life, 1980, 1990, 1997, 2017. It seems like this project will be going forever. Very noble cause and worth visiting with friends or family. Large museum, gift store, and restaurant. I'll be bringing the kids in the next couple years. It is a shame to see all the poor reviews from a bunch of internet aged spoiled punks who expect instant gratification for free when you consider the scope of this project.  The monument is funded through donations and not government money. That alone makes this a destination worth seeing. Is the place perfect? No. Is it awesome? Yes.

name: Jeff
text:
So, the museum was interesting… Felt a little disconnected. Should the monument ever be finished, I am certain it will look incredible. Yet, from what we read about crazy horse, we question whether he would be happy with this memorial.

I felt the $30 for admittance was overpriced for what was available. Unless you really plan on carefully going through the museum and reading every sign, you can probably see the whole thing in 40 minutes.

text: Awesome experience! It's a lot bigger than it looks. Can't hike up so be sure to do the bus tour.

name: James McIntire
text: Thos place is so amazing! In my opinion it is a better experience than Rushmore. The museum is wonderful and very educational. The gift shop is on point with anything you could possibly want. I highly recommend taking the Face to Face tour! That is the most incredible tour I've ever been on.

name: Joshua MacGregor
text: Expensive, crowded, unimpressive & disappointing to name a few adjectives.  Face of carving faces away from visitor center and is not easily seen.  Nearly everything costs additional 💰.  It has been 70 years since they started this project and yet it looks like it has barely started.  Where had all that money gone?  Mt Rushmore only took 14 years and is much more impressive.  Avoid Crazy Horse Memorial and head to Mt Rushmore.

name: Liz JA
text: I had not been here in about 40 years and it really didn't look much different (or when I had been here 50 years ago). The price to get in was more than we wanted to spend at this time. Would sure be nice if they could get it finished our at least to be able to see a difference. How can it take this long when Mt. Rushmore took only 14 years and this has been going on for about 70 years!

name: Wade Christiansen
text:
Today's visit was my fourth. Each time has been an all new experience. The entire place changes greatly. Always new additions and expanses. The museum is beautiful and I hope it is seen as a great honor to American Indians. Be sure to visit and save a couple of hours during your vacation to the Black Hills. You will need to explore because there a number of doors and hallways where you are welcome. Make sure that you come back again in a year or two because it will have changed.
I see that the a number of people are complaining of the price or lack of info on the website. First, the information is on the site. Second, it is $10 or $12 for everything in the Back Hills. The $30 is per car for more than 2 people so if there are 3 people, it is $10 and so on. Bus rides are $4. Also remember there is no government funding for this endeavor. Please take the time to understand the full scope. This is a National Museum, school, and Memorial.

name: Debra Reddy
text: I think this sculpture is going to be amazing once it's finished but it seems to be taking an awfully long time to complete. I visited 16 years ago and not a lot has changed. I understand the entrance fee pays for everything but $30 is too much. And then you have to pay more to take a bus ride to see it closer and from the front. The restaurant is no good either.

text: I think this place gets a bad rap in some reviews. I took my family and we felt it was completely worth the $30 car entry fee. Then we were able to see two performances - one from Jonah Littlesunday on the Native American Flute (AGT contestant) and the musical group Brulé (with traditional Native dancers). Both of this was included with our admission price. Would totally recommend stopping at Crazy Horse!

name: Robert Snow
text:
A true monument in every sense of the word.  Whether your interests are historical, cultural, or artistic you
can't help but be inspired by the scope of this effort. Considering all the dreams this work represents and the collaboration of entire generations of people and families it is a special place. I visit it frequently to draw on its energy.
I took my son and daughter here 20+ years ago to participate in the Volksmarch and had the opportunity to hike the Spring 2019 Volksmarch with my granddaughter.  She loved it.  A great event for sure.  Hope to be able to do it again with my great grand kids.  A shout-out to the Black Hills Volksmarch Assoc for their efforts.  TY !

text: Terrible! Tourist trap! Avoid! The Foundation is ripping people off in the name of Native American Culture... They collected over $52 million and have only given back $250k back. The whole Ziolkowski family is corrupt. 1) $12 a person as you drive up. Waste of money! Wish they would refund me! 2) There are no Native Americans working. They don't even support the project. 3) Construction progress is so slow. At this rate, it'll take 200 more years to complete! 4) Disorganized collection of fake art.

text:
You cannot do Rushmore and not do Crazyhorse.  I can't wait to take my family there.  I also recommend the Mammoth Site south of here.

The staff in the Visitor's Center were very helpful and friendly.  They gave me a free packet for Teachers.  Not sure if this is still offered.  I didn't take the bus out, but enjoyed the VC and the Fightin Stallions bronze outside, and the African Mahogany version inside.

Only downside was they gave preferential treatment in pricing to cars from neighboring states.

Hope I'm still alive to see it finished!

resp.text:
Dear Adam Harrington,
Thank you for taking the time to visit and write a review of Crazy Horse Memorial. Your contribution through admission assists with the continued progress of the Mountain Carving, Museums & INDIAN UNIVERSITY OF NORTH AMERICA(R). The University offers Native American students the opportunity to earn their first semester college education on scholarship.

For $28 per carload allows you entrance to the Welcome Center, movie about the history and progress of the Carving, access to several museums, Native American dance performances, summer lecture series, hands on activities in the Cultural Center, nightly laser light show and so much more.
We appreciate your support.
Sincerely,
Crazy Horse Memorial Foundation

text: Our first trip to cosmos was this past weekend. We went with a small group, including our two young kids. Its a fun experience, but I am not sure I believe in all of the conspiracy theories. Its a fun house in the woods with some interesting experiences related to gravity. I would not recommend for anyone who gets nauseated easily or has motion sickness. The unlevel cabins and confined spaces can make it a bit difficult to find your bearings. I think its worth one trip, but not sure we would return.

I give this 3 stars only due to my own motion sickness issues...my husband and one of our daughters loved this tour.  Your brain and eyes want you to think and feel something else and it messes with your balance and equilibrium.
I do recommend taking this tour, but you must have a strong stomach, balance and wherewithal.
You will be challenged to stand straight in a couple of cabins/rooms built to work against your innate senses. Definitely a bucket list thing.
I would not take small children, definitely wear good shoes that tie and have great traction. There are a lot of steps and steep inclines, so only do this with stable lower joints. Don’t take purses or bags or anything that would cause you to sway or be weighted down.
Just a few suggestions.

text: Really nice and well maintained park. A bit bummed that the monument itself was no lit after dark.  Odd that other items in park were lit, but the main one was not. It's my fault for lollygagging and not making it during day time. Great, quick stop nonetheless.

name: D Cooper
text: We've visited The Ciudad Mitad del Mundo so why not the Center of the USA! Well maintained grounds and worth the drive out to Belle Fourche to see it, don't forget to hit the little boutique shops on the main street and support local.

name: Jeff
text:
The marker for the geographic center of the United States is about what you expect. A marker. There were a lot of state flags around it. Possibly all 50? We didn’t really count and we don’t know most of the state flags… So let that be a challenge to you!

Now if all you see is the marker, you’re really missing out. Nearby is a cabin… The stairs are very narrow, but otherwise the interior is surprisingly roomy for the first cabin in that area. A very polite staff person in the building and a buffalo horn coat rack.

But the highlight of the whole place is the museum. Go to the museum. Saddles, saddle struck by lightning, saddles a famous people, saddles that were on horses, Saddles that were 100 years old…

Also, antique firearms, the first piano ever, the medical kits that doctors used from 100 years ago with all the pills and drugs and tinctures still inside and on display. Note: These prescriptions are probably past their expiration date.

A whole bunch of other stuff that I forgot now, but I think was really cool. Just lots and lots of stuff. Seriously, see the museum! It’s great! Our friend Sean didn’t come in, and he regrets it. Really really regrets it. And on the way out, throw in a few bucks to the donation box! I mean, come on! Everything else is free. Chip in a little bit, you know? Geez. Have a heart.

name: Ruben Stemple
text: Nice monument, but the accompanying museum is even better. They have kids activities and great information about varied topics from prohibition to western doctors to dinosaurs. Staff is helpful and knowledable.

Excellent, light a
& refreshing sandwiches Vietnamese Chicken sandwich, Curried Cauliflower. Even the fries hit the spot. Others in our group had the hamburger! No wonder Guy Fiere  ❤👍us too!

My kids 9 and 10 had the regular burger and not the kids meal burger, and they were able to polish them off pretty easily showing at the portions are a little bit on the small side. Flavors were good, not outstanding, they could have had a little more cowbell and it would be over the top.

name: Mike Sohm
text: I very much enjoyed  my dining experience at the B&CS.  I was able to walk right up and  order, I got the brisket and my wife had the Italian. The bread is delicious  with a hearty firmness that escapes the abilities of distant sandwich shops like SUBWAY or as I prefer to call them McSub. The bread was toasted with the distinctive flavors of a good brisket without the overdone burnt flavor that the inexperienced are masters of.  The ingredients are fresh and the atmosphere was relaxing.

resp.text: So glad to hear it Mike, thanks!!

resp.text: Thanks for your review Jared! FYI, our online ordering platform is set at 30 minutes to ensure we can meet demand. If you need your food faster, just order in person or via telephone.
