The lunch buffet was about $9(a staff person said $11 for dinner).There is lots of food. Lots. Not only is there plenty of typical cuisine, there is also enough generic choices (chicken nuggets and mac 'n' cheese)  to feed pickier eaters. Additionally there are generous salad, dessert, and fresh fruit sections. Overall this place has efficient (if not particularly happy) staff and the food, though not making any headlines, is good, fresh, plentiful, and in enough varieties that I can't help but give this first time visit 5 stars.

text:
From my previous experience I knew that this is not the place to go with bigger groups of people. They always screw something up. Sure enough, this time wasn't an exception.
As we went in, I ordered sodas for us (parents) and water for kids ( I thought, that was as clear as day, who I'm paying for, and what we drink).
First of all, they brought water for us and somebody else got our drinks.  We had to wait as they try to figure that out, and who can they charge for those 2 drinks (10 mins delay)  (after they brought our drinks, it did not concern me anymore, but still mistake on waitress' part. They should deal with that mistake and not trying to pass that charge onto customer)
Second, (kids were sitting on separate table)  apparently my kid ordered a soda for himself and guess what, with out my permission they bring soda to my kid (there is always a reason when they drink water instead of soda)  so when I try to straighten that charge on my bill all I got from them is "he is our customer and we have to bring him what he asks for".  REALLY? He is only seven years old. Do you think he is gonna pay for his meal? I'm not saying you shouldn't treat him as your customer but YOU should ALWAYS coordinate with his parents if he ordered something different from what we ordered previously. (Another 40 mins delay)
Conclusion:
Was it worth fighting 40mins over $2 charge? NO
But I'm pretty sure it is well worth fighting over the next kid with real health issues. If management of Hibachi Grill & Supreme Buffet would only understand real problem here.
Food is ok.  My wife doesn't like it at all
Customer service - worst out of all restaurants in Sioux Falls

If I could leave zero stars, I would, but least amount of stars Google requires is one, so that's what I'm leaving.

text: Friendly staff and great atmosphere! Tanya W. is an incredible stylist...She took the time to give me exactly what I was looking for.  I will most certainly be back in a few months!

name: Chris Malcomb
text:
Professional courteous service.
They send you a text to remind you of your appointment and ask that you call them from your car when you get there. They will let you know if your stylist is ready for you to come in.

text:
Aldi always has great deals. Be aware that they are a intentionally a small store in order to keep overhead low. Their business model is very unique and allows the prices to remain low all the time.
With that being said, they will not have all the name brands or the multiple variations of every item. The inventory changes frequently based on economics.
This is a great place to add to you grocery run if you food prep or comparison shop. Just don't plan on buying your entire list here. Use this as your first stop and then get whatever they don't have at your next favorite store.
Aldi saves us up to 50% on our grocery bill when we plan ahead and comparison shop.

I highly recommend Aldi and its sister stores Trader Joe's.

Really? I LOVE candy!  And I REALLY love candy stores!!  I wonder what else I'll find in the shadows of the big retailers I think are still closed off from the little guys in between, but I'm not sure anymore. And honestly....who cares?! It's a Target. I don't know what it is exactly that they do that makes you want to buy stuff, but they do it well. I went in for cheap ear buds, and left with a $170 Ninja Specialty coffee maker. What the heck? Now, my coffee maker is, admittedly, starting to die, but I'm really good at squeezing the last droplets of life out of my appliances and making them go as long as possible to save as much money as I can. By that account, I should have been able to hold off buying a new coffee maker for at least 6 months.

Apparently that ability's kryptonite is a Target. Who knew?

name: kevin Trierweiler
text: Buffet never got stocked when we were there. They were out of pepper, yes pepper! My girlfriend asked for some white gravy because the buffet was out, and they acted as if it was the end of the world. When it came back it was like water.

name: Debra Boeding
text: The food was great but the young gentleman forgot to give me my pop. I realized that a few blocks away so went back and waited in the drive thru for another 5 to 7 minutes to get it! I love my soda!

name: Rebecca Tarrell-Weidenbach
text: The regular chicken meal was fine but because they are independently owned, they don't have bowls, potties or popcorn chicken.  Only e 10th still has the popcorn chicken but louise has everything except that.

name: Miranda Sullenger
text: Ordered 2 famous bowls. The kid through the drive threw didnt know how to give correct change back. Also, they usually have popcorn chicken on the top. These had cut up chicken strip pieces on them that werent even crunchy. Not pleased at all.

name: Lori Uecker
text: My order wasn't correct and the drive thru lane is too small.

name: Jarrod Hafner
text: The service was great and the food was prepared very quickly; unfortunately, the chicken was very soggy and chewy.

name: Family Rhoades
text: The food was good they just forgot my sauce and they need a little more gray on the potatoes

name: Kelly Hornsby
text: Ever since the previous owner retired, things just haven't been the same!! This used to be my boyfriend & my's favorite location, but sadly no more. They "streamlined" the buffet, aka took a lot off like their yummy mac 'n cheese, shredded cheese for the salad bar portion, you can no longer request their chicken fried steak if it's not on the buffet & that ain't on there anymore either!! The tables aren't kept clean like before & though it could be my imagination - the whole atmosphere is less welcoming & fun. Probably still occasionally visit since it is closest to the boyfriend, but not like our weekly visits before. I truly hope the previous owner is thoroughly enjoying his retirement, but he IS sincerely missed!!

name: Jenifer Mccoy
text: Easily the worst buffet and service I've ever had. Who charges $10. For a buffet that for 20 minutes had absolutely no chicken? I'm not the only one that complained either. By the time the chicken arrived it was like rubber. Not very many other choices so I had 1 plate. On top of that having a new kid run the register with zero training during dinner time? WOW! 3 people walked out that were behind me. Poor kid tried his very best and he even said that 3 people walked out and she said well maybe they should learn to have more patience. Uh no! Maybe you should be standing with him and teaching him his job. Really, if you're a manager and not taking time to invest knowledge into your team then should you really be a manager? If I ran my own business with this type of poor quality it would be shut down. The world is at a stand still. These poor kids not only get zero education at school the real world teaches them nothing either. Thanks for the $10. Rubber chicken. Comical at best!

name: Brenda Mason
text: Great food, good customer service

name: Zack Allen
text: Went there on the 31st around 6pm. That was the absolute worst service I have ever had at a KFC. They didn't even put ice in our drinks through the drive thru, and were kind of rude. The food tastes old at best, if not bad. I highly do not recommend going here. After eating the famous bowl that I ordered, I almost threw up in my mouth, that's how bad the food was.

name: Laura Lopez
text: Service was great but the food was not. The signature gravy could not mask the distinctive taste that cheap instant mashed potatoes leave in your mouth. The buffet no longer carries Mac and cheese or chicken fried steak. The price went up but the quality went down.

name: toothy hogwartz101
text: I won't be returning. First I got a pop the guy handed it to me and the lid popped off he saw this and didn't offer any napkins or an apology. I asked for coleslaw instead of mashed potatoes never got my side of coleslaw and I also asked for barbecue sauce got home no sauce I will not go here again.

name: Duck Shooter
text: The KFC on Kiwanis has a buffet.  It was well stocked, the food was hot and fresh.  $10 gets you a drink, and decent salad bar with some desserts, and original chicken, extra crispy chicken, BBQ chicken.  Plus mashed potatoes and gravy, biscuits, coleslaw, breaded okra, chicken fried steak and some more...and the restaurant was clean with a worker wiping off tables after people left.

name: Linda Dubois
text: Not the fastest.  Food was fine. I had a chicken  breast, was good potatoes  weren't.

name: Steve Buysman
text: KFC is always a hit. This location will not disappoint!

text: No chicken on buffet. Salad bar & buffet items very limited. Used to be better.

text: Absolutely horrible service. No chicken was out on the buffet and when requested for more the employee then had a major disrespectful attitude. The tables were all messy and no one had wiped down any of them picking up any of the left over food left on them. I dont reccomend going here. Check out the other locations before wasting your time and money here.

text: I am requesting that your casino please begin having the ability to reprint players cards. I don't drive myself but ride with others any chance I can. Half the time the opportunity presents itself after midnight. And three quarters of the times I visit I find my card no longer works. Which means I cannot earn points, access my free play, or swipe at the kiosk. I consider this a great loss. I take great care to keep my players card in my wallet at all times so it isn't accidentally exposed to something that would render it useless yet still it keeps happening.  Other casinos I've visited that have clubs that aren't 24hours give their pit bosses the access to print cards for members. I hope you consider this as a resolution. Thanks.

They have Pepsi products (diet mountain dew)

Other then that it's a small, older casino located in Flandreau, South Dakota. Good RV park and competitively priced hotel rates (not the best rooms)

Since I mostly go to casinos for the food, and secondary a little bit of video keno, this place gets the job done without having to drive very far.  The buffet doesn't need to be large if I spend 80% of the time eating crab legs (as most people who go for crab legs also do)

During Covid-19 the restrooms structure was close unfortunately.

name: Laken Brock
text: Beautiful park with trails and a view. Be careful with the younger kids. It can be very dangerous. There were plaques along the way that educated you about how the falls were created and other fun facts. There are buffalo statues, and other fun things for the kids to do. There is an overlook tower that we skipped due to covid. The park does encourage social distancing. Lots of shaded area to relax or enjoy a picnic.

name: Amber Hendershot-Nordin
text: It's so magical down @ Falls Park during the Holidays & the City of Sioux Falls really knows how to make you feel like a kiddo again w/all the amazing detailed lights & amazing music. Falls Park is already a special place to go visit w/friends or family & even bring your loved ones whom are here visiting from outta town. The Falls Cafe is a great place to grab a bite or get something warm to drink even or if you're freezing to stop in & warm-up.

name: Michael Turner
text:
A beautiful park for families and nature lovers. The falls are beautiful and there's a fun little cafe that is open on the weekends.  There are paved trails throughout and it is very wheelchair friendly. There are also a few historic markers just to make things interesting.  There is also a lookout tower and a cute little gift shop.

It's easy to access and plenty of parking.

The only thing to watch out for is there are very few railings or guardrails. Kids and adults could both walk directly into the water and the falls. It's absolutely stunning but keep an eye on those kiddos.

name: Jason Vaughn
text: I've had memories, within, of the beautiful, loud, very tall and rushing waters of the Big Sioux River, here in my hometown of Sioux Falls, South Dakota, since I was 5 years old. THAT memory of THAT day will be a 4ever one for sure. Now, with my kids, it's  a REexperience! Lol

text: Great park in the middle of Sioux Falls.  Nicely built up pathways and interesting historical info is scattered throughout. The city did a good job blending a natural, geological space into an urban area - not something found in many cities.

text: Great family area and very clean park. Great for the pets.

name: Steve Buysman
text:
This is the namesake park for our city. There are many interesting things to see, lots of open areas to enjoy and history to learn. It is decorated for Christmas and you can drive or walk through to enjoy the atmosphere.
They have multiple public restrooms, a viewing tower and many places to take unique photos or make memories.
Watch your pets and children closely when you are near the water as the rocks have been known to be slippery and the current can and has sucked under and drown even the best swimmers. Practice common sense and good parenting to build the best memories.
It is also within walking distance to the sculpture walk and downtown shopping and eateries.

A beautiful park, and a wonderful place to walk around and see the falls from which the city his named. Must see it if you are in town.

But the sidewalks are not straight and do not all go through, and Sean’s navigation is just terrible, and you will walk for miles to get to something that is only four blocks away somehow. Walk for miles in terrible heat & no shade.

So in summary: beautiful Falls, park close.

name: Landon McCluskey
text: If you're visiting Sioux Falls or you're a lifelong resident, you need to come to Falls Park. You won't find mountains or oceans or roller coasters or the world's largest ball of anything, but you will find a beautiful park that relaxes you and will draw you in time and again. Whether you're looking out from the observation tower, crossing the bridge, climbing the rocks, visiting the bookstore or museum, eating at the cafe, or doing anything else, there's just something about this place that can relax you and relieve stress, making your troubles fade. It's an oasis of natural beauty in the middle of a small city that you wouldn't expect to find. Even more is that there are regular events here that bring the community together and it's close to downtown and right across the street from the farmers market. The park is a great destination year-round, even being lit up all winter. Long story short, please don't miss out on this beautiful Sioux Falls landmark. Do yourself a favor and make time to visit, whether it's your first time or your thousandth.

name: Reece Chambers
text: This place is what Sioux Falls was built on and what it is known for. If I ever have people coming from out of town I tell them they need to check out downtown and Falls Park. But this is where one issue lies--there is downtown AND Falls Park, vs, downtown IS BUILT AROUND Falls Park. These two places are very close, and mostly walking distance, but there needs to be more connection. Falls Park has entirely too much green space for.... mowing? Of course we need green space, but we also need something to attract people to the Falls outside of the river. I've been to places like Greenville, SC where they have a Falls Park (it's actually called Falls Park), and their downtown is built around it. There is so much foot traffic, and their downtown combined with their Falls Park is the absolute place to be. This would be good for businesses and Sioux Falls! But we are getting there, it just takes time.

name: Celeste Ruppelt
text:
Even though we've been through Sioux Falls before, I never actually knew there was such a nice park along the river or that the falls were actually this impressive.
This was just lovely and we were quite impressed.
The park covers 123 acres, and on average, 7,400 gallons of water fall 100-feet over the course of the Falls each second.
The remains of the 7-story Queen Bee Mill, which opened in 1881, are on the east side of the river. The building which is still intact there now, is the old Light and Power Company, which opened in 1908. It now houses the Falls Overlook Café, where you'll find family friendly snacks, ice cream, and such.
There are also picnic ramadas, through-out the park, as well.
A 5-story, 50-foot viewing tower, connected to the Visitor Center, offers a 360-degree panoramic view of the park and parts of Sioux Falls. The observation tower is free to visitors. Access is by elevator, and it does get windy up there. It is open from 9am - 9pm daily, Memorial Day-Labor Day.
There is a large, free, parking lot. Bring a towel, in case you get wet feet playing on the flat rocks near the Upper Falls. If you get lucky, you might even see the military jets flying overhead from the near by base. You will hear them.
Restrooms are near the Visitor Center.
If you smell bacon during your visit, the John Morrell plant is across the way.

text: Well, it's five stars compared to other sites here. They've done an amazing job of developing Falls Park since I first remember going, which seems very appropriate for the namesake of your city! In the summer, it's also well-lit on the lower falls at night, but I look forward to more development of the upper falls. name: Steven Thulin
text: It is a beautiful park, very well kept. There is plenty of grassy area and a lot of tables for picnicing. The falls are awesome! You can see them very well from the tower (free entrance, for those on a budget). There is a nice cafe by the falls and a trolley tour is available from here to see other points of interest in town. There is also the foundation of an old mill, which is often used for concerts and plays (again, often at no cost). My family's favorite thing at this park is the bike tail. Part of the more-than-20-mile loop runs through the park. We usually bike from some other location along the loop to visit the park. There is very good reason the city gets its name from these falls.

text: Admission free. Just remember that crawling around on the rocks can be dangerous if you leave the sidewalks. Convenient observation tower with a deck. Lots of photo opportunities around the Big Sioux River water falls. Geese and ducks at play, watch out for goose poop in the grassy areas next to the water. Light shows after dark in the warm weather months. Great little cafe in the old power station building.  Summer music and plays at the ruins of the Queen Bee Mill every summer. The 4th of July parade ended here and the Mayor had a free picnic to celebrate Independence Day this year. Mile 0 of the paved 18.5 mile bike/walking/skating trail that follows the river around the city is here.

name: Caitlynn Alice
text:
Why isn't there an option for zero stars? This truly was a dinning experience I wish for no one.
NO COVID PROCEDURES. GUEST NOT WEARING MASKS WHILE WALKING IN. SERVERS WERE WEARING MASKS WITH THEIR NOSE OUT. WHAT'S THE POINT OF A MASK THEN?!
After waiting 5 minutes at the host stand, we were finally shown to a table. The place was crowded in the opening room where I could tell the female server was about to seat us. I had then asked the female server if we could be placed in a different room or just a little more spread out from people to which she replied, "this is a restaurant, there's people everywhere". Her unwillingness to simply move us a room over should have been a sign this was NOT going to be a good experience. The server we ended up with was alright, but knew little to nothing about the menu.  Then came the food. This was the poorest excuse of plate presentation I have ever seen. I ordered their signature cracker barrel ham dinner with a side of macaroni and corn. Everything was cold. Everything was flavorless. The biscuits were harder than my critiquing of this restaurant. A guest in our party ordered the chicken tenders and it looks like they opened a bag of Tyson chicken nuggets and threw them on the plate.

By all means save yourself the money and time by never eating here.

text: Now this review hurts because I love Cracker Barrel but I have to be honest! My popular reputation depends on it. I also want to preface this review that if this was lunch or dinner it would be 5 HUGE stars!!! I was on my way back to Rapid City and we stopped for breakfast. I had small pancakes and sausage. The pancakes were slightly burned on the edges and bland. The sausage was like rubber and had an odd taste. Syrup was cracker barrel brand and was delicious. Service was GREAT and friendly so service alone gets 5 stars. I did buy a box of dumplin mix and can't wait to make them. Cracker Barrel chicken and dumplins are the best in the state. Sadly I can't recommend breakfast...yet....maybe it will approve if I'm in the area during breakfast.

name: Patty Storevik
text:
I've been here twice in a month, both times in the evenings and both times the food is not good. Cracker Barrel used to be one of my favorite places to go for breakfast food because their food was consistently good, not anymore. Greasy hashbrowns, over cooked eggs, runny gravy, flat soda, burnt coffee, burnt sausage, and undercooked bacon.

I did email corporate as suggested and didnt hear back yet. It has been a week or so.
I went in for a late breakfast today and the food was good. Apparently the problem is the evenings.

resp.text: Sorry to hear about the poor experience, Patty. Can you please email us some additional information at customercare@crackerbarrel.com? Please use your review username as your subject line, and include: phone number, email address, store location, as well as any other relevant information that could help us understand the situation better.

name: mrsmel269
text: When they opened this walmart, it was our favorite spot. Now, more people have found it and it is busier than we would like, but what can you do. The store is cleand and well stocked. They offer all the normal services like bakery, auto, deli, pharmacy, etc. They have plenty of self check outs and regular. They are also building a BP gas station by the parking lot of the building. Getting in and out is kind of a pain and with the gas station, it will probably be more congested because there are not many other entrances and exits. The parking lot also seems pretty compacted and congested most of the time. As of yesterday, they only allowed you to enter and exit in one door by the produce section. They require masks to enter and say over the speaker that they allow a certain number of customers at a time. Someone is there with a counter, but I haven't had to wait outside before going inside. There is a designated spot on the side of the building for curbside pickup when you order items to be picked up.

text: I was just in there store today utilizing their self checkout. I had only gotten a few things came up to $8.47. I used $5 cash first. Then I selected the option to pay the rest with my card. $3.47 left. I use a chip card so of course I answered it when prompted. It started processing the payment then on the kiosk screen it told me to remove my card and press cancel so it could process the cash. So I did so. It still prompted that I owed $3.47. Still says to insert my card. Did so. IT DECLINES MY CARD! I immediately check my account with my bank app. Sure enough, pending $3.47 from Wal-Mart. I holler for the customer service rep. She just tells me to try it again. Obviously doesn't work. Immediately calls a CSM (which is a customer service manager I think?). That lady proceeds to argue with me, telling me I still owe the amount. I told her what I did, then showed her my bank app. She proceeded to call an acting manager, who proceeded to tell me the same damn thing! They wouldn't let me leave with my items and they would not refund the amount charged to my account or my cash. Somebody from the deli walked over and was nice enough to say that he'll pay the amount if it doesn't go through. The acting manager of course refused. All the while, I'm explaining how this went down, then out of nowhere, he says ok you can go now. Guess he finally figured out how wrong he was. If anything like this ever happens again, I can and will use that location for credit fraud.

One of the many fast food icons located here. McDonalds fails to deliver on two main fronts; accuracy and speed.

First, McDonalds is making great strides to help in these areas and are utilizing automated order taking along with human staff for order taking as well as preparation. You would think this would assist in the speed your order is brought to you, but unfortunately, for this location, it does not. Regardless of the time of day, staff, while friendly, do not move with the haste a fast food restaurant is known for. Add the fact that orders are consistently inaccurate, missing items or having poor quality.

With the errors and overall lack of speed, I'd recommend other locations if you are looking for a McDonalds, or try and of the other food choices within the area.

text:
Wow, I don't really know what to say about this McDonald's.  I've been here quite a few times, and lately I've been less than impressed.  A couple weeks ago, I went through the drive-through for breakfast and was given the wrong food, but I didn't have time to get it fixed (soccer game), so I just dealt with it.  Unfortunately, what I received was one of those Biscuit-based sandwiches and the biscuit was hard as a rock...so bad service AND bad/wrong food at the same time.

This is not what I'm writing in about, though.

This morning, I went to this McDonald's again to grab some breakfast before heading to my soccer game.  The line in the drive-through was pretty long, so I decided to head into the restaurant.  I placed my order, then a large group of college-age people came in and placed their orders (maybe 8 minutes after I placed my order).  The guy ahead of me received his food and it was wrong, so he had to send it back for another try, then the group of college kids began receiving their orders while I was still standing there waiting for my food.  I was less-than-impressed, but I know that sometimes food takes a little longer (especially when lunch is starting and breakfast isn't ready-made anymore)...but once I checked my watch and realized it was literally 15 minutes as the guy finally handed me my bag of food, I became incensed.  As he handed me my food, I said, 'It's been fifteen minutes!" To which he simply stared at me for half a second and walked away. Not even an, "I'm sorry," or "how can I make this better?"

I don't expect the best service in town from a fast-food place, but I expect something...anything that could be construed as trying.  As a person who has spent a lot of his life working in different aspects of the service industry, I know that no manger would approve of this method of handling the situation.  I can't, in good conscience, recommend that anyone use this location when there's another (and another and another) nearby that will likely do a better, more consistent job of providing quality food and service to each customer.

name: Chris Hoffmann
text: I have been a regular since it opened, I even worked there for a while. I like most of the employees. Would give a 4 ☆ at least but the last time I went in the new GM checked me out. I bought beet so he asked for my ID. I have an SD license that doesn't like to come out of my wallet but since my birth date is in the middle most people in South Dakota don't care as long as they see I'm 30. Looked at it for a long time before informing me that he couldn't tell how old I was unless I took it out of my wallet. I told him it was difficult to do but half of his employees could tell him my age. He said that he couldn't sell me beer if he didn't know, which is true, but he would have known if he could read my ID. I managed to get it out, he fumbled with his scanner trying to get it to read, couldn't, so he looked at it for a really long time before handing it back saying that because I used to work there I known how it is. I do know how it is, I also know how to read an ID and not sneer at customers. I guess that's just one of those GM things. I like the store and the staff, the current GM is too dumb to be that condescending. Who works retail and can't read a local ID?

name: P H
text:
Place is slow at 1130pm,.the rest room were clean,they have good soap finally to get dirt and grease off your hands.
Why do the shop men drive the service vehicle from the shop to the fuel desk and then let it idle while they're in the store flirting with the girls or hide in the bathroom or hiding in the office not doing anything for hours at a time. It's so waste of fuel and wear and tear on the engine. And if it was extremely cold why don't you just pull it inside the shop or and plug it in so the engine stays warm you don't have to leave it running for hours and hours it's just wasting Fuel and wear and tear on the engine. I don't know why they don't have a three-wheel bicycle with a large basket for them to bring Parts back and forth from the shop to the fuel desk. They don't need to drive the pickup truck back and forth all the time it's a waste of resources and money.

name: TEXASBLAZE 101
text:
The gas stations there are dysfunctional. I used to go there all the time to fill my car with gas. The first time the machine failed to shut its self off, it spilled a little gas on the side of my car but it was no problem because i was able to get a small refund from the cashire. The second time it failed to automatically shut off i was sitting inside my car because i did not want to stand outside in -15°F with gusting wind of 50mph because understandably that sort of weather can be extremely overwhelming. I noticed it was taking a while to finish up so i checked and the nozzle, still firmly in place as fare as it would go into the filling port was spewing gas all over the side of my car and formed a pool of gasoline under my car as well. I walked inside to ask for a refund and the night manager walked outside to check on the situation. It took her a while to finally asses the situation and i asked her if i may get a refund. She laughed at me and said no. I asked "why not? The last time this happened i got a refund, no problems." She said its not her call and she began to blame me saying it was likely my fault for the malfunction because somehow i must have messed up one of the simplest taskes on earth... stick in a stupid gasoline nossle and fill a tank of fuel. She said the day-time manager would need to make that happen anyways. So she takes my name and number then tells me she would have him call me at 11AM tomorrow morning. I turned back to my car, walking through the lake of gasoline that surrounded my car and drove to the car wash to avoid having my paint eaten away by the contamination of gasoline. The next day it was already 12PM and i had recived zero calls from Loves gas station. I hopped into my car with the gasoline fumes still choking me from the night before and drove to the station to see what was going on. I find the day-manager who i was told will help me out with my refund. I had to chase this guy around the store for about 10 minutes, with him even going as far as to walk outside and around the store in an effort to ditch me. I was already heated by the fact that these people have already begun to waist even more of my time now. I finally catch up to him and had a little chat about the night before. He goes off to say that it was my fault for not standing next to the pump while filling and that no mechanical device is perfect and how they all fail and that my experience with the pump last night was somesort of coincidence. I tell him this wasnt the first time i had this problem and that tis has happened to me here twice now and theres no way its my fault. He continues to say what he had already said like three more times as his words and the entire conversation enveloped around it being all my fault had became of extrem redundancy. I told him, i dont want to waist anymore of my  time (its been 30 minutes or longer by this point) and i was just looking for a refund. In a atempt to totally deny me of any hopes to recieve a refund he tells me that im lucky i dont have to pay money for the cleanup effort that apparently goes behind each one of these spills. i told him i have never seen this happen anywhere else except at this station and ive filled at many different stations in the past before. He interupts me as he has 6 times already saying hes seen it happen countless times at other stations which by this point is so typical to everything he has said since he has been contradicting everything i say and tries to make it look like i dont know what im talking about. He said some of the most goofy stuff i ever heard saying the gas nozzle has many variable degrees of insertion but everyone and there mother knows the gas nozzle will only fit one way. Its not rocket science to know this stuff. finally I had enough of his hot air and was on my way out

I hate the customer service here, i hate their food i hate the over priced hardees with their equaly teribble food they serve and i will never purchase another drop of gas from this sorry POS service station for as long as i live. Thank you for reading.

name: Kristy Woodfield
text: Had a wonderful day in Custer State Park.  We hiked the Big Elk Trail #9 and while the trail was snow covered and icy in parts it was passable in regular hiking shoes if you take your time.  The wildlife road was way better than I expected! I highly recommend taking the time for the drive.

name: Jeannine Szostak
text: I stumbled upon this place by accident. We could have made a whole vacation here and never seen the same place twice. There are three highways that run through here, each as unique as their name. One (Wildlife Loop Road) takes you through prairie dogs and buffalo (technically “American Buffalo” or “bison”), and burros and gazelle and dragonflies and more. Another (Needles Highway) takes you through unique rock formations, which you can climb on and drive through. The third (Iron Mountain Road), also has twisty-turny roads which lead through one lane tunnels, which frame views of Mount Rushmore (if you’re headed the right direction).  There are turnoffs for you to park near all of the tunnels should you want to get out and explore, however there are signs posted where the Buffalo roam to not get out of your vehicle (though people do) because they are wild animals and will charge, no matter how flattering a photo you take of them. There is a lake for swimming and many, many other things to explore - the place is huge. Your admission is also good for a week, so it’s not expensive. Absolutely worth the drive!!

name: Tracey Janisch
text: We did the wildlife loop and also were able to see the needles tunnel. We went out and ventured to do some rock climbing which the kids completely loved. Everywhere you looked it was gorgeous scenery and just breathtaking! All of us enjoyed every minute of the drive and being able to get out and just enjoy the scenery. You could never take enough pictures and you could just sit and stare for hours. The whole experience is great and would go back to do it again!

name: Chanchal
text: Awesome, amazingly natural site! Loved driving through Custer State Park. Very supportive staff. Although we visited amidst Pandemic but full care taken care of. A drive worth enjoyable between many of its beautiful spots like Legion Lake, Needles Highway, Stockade Lake, Sylvan Lake. Trails are worth to hike on.

name: Lex Godfrey
text: One of our favorite places! Awe inspiring scenery and numerous wildlife.

name: Kenneth Hill
text: Nature's way of surprising how a fast paced society isn't anywhere to be found while in this park, picture perfect settings and excellent pullover sites throughout

name: M. McCoy
text: Love this park! Wildlife viewing is awesome here.

name: Sylvia Moya
text: Great morning hike at Sylvan lake. I didn't get to see the burritos like I wanted to, but the hike was awesome. Do it early before it gets very hot and bring plenty of water

name: Sarah Trader
text: Beautiful place to visit. Amazing scenic drives and it's so cool to see the bison up close! Needles highway is fun too, though my young kids were bored quickly. Be prepared to spend a good 90 minutes to 2 hours if you drive the Wildlife Loop and Needles Highway. Some nice views of Mount Rushmore too!

name: azureanthem d
text: Absolutely Gorgeous! This is the prettiest state park I've ever been to. Worth driving 12 hours just for this. If you're visiting Mount Rushmore, you gotta come on over to Custer State Park. Simply incredible!   P. S. You don't have to see the wildlife loop or the needles highway, but you'll be missing out 😀

name: Darren Good
text: Nice area to view nature in the form of wildlife and the land. At this time of year the park is not crowded which makes driving more comfortable.  I this trip seen a couple of Bisons, a few prairie dogs and a coyote.

name: Don Den
text:
Beautiful park. Buffalo in the wild. Up close and personal. Stay IN your car!
Prairie dog colony's are cute. Get out and tske pics there )

name: Glenn Taylor
text: The buffalo roundup is a very special event. Highly recommend the viewing of the roundup as well as the arts festival that follows. The unique artwork on display from the local community as well as the artists who have travel hundreds of miles to show off their skills has definately opened my eyes (and pocketbook) at this one of kind event. Great food and conversation goes well with the live music at the Buffalo Roundup!!

name: Brittany Dukes
text: If you love driving to see the scenery and wildlife come here.

name: quentin holmes
text: This place is a must. Between the lakes and animals it really is an amazing place to visit. South Dakota is amazing and underrated.

name: Ashley Gutowski
text: Amazing park with lots of wildlife and trails. Best to go early to avoid crowds

name: Derrick Grant
text: Custer State Park is a must see if you visit the Rapid City or Black Hills area.  The entrance fee is $20 but it covers 7 consecutive days of visits within the park.  This park is quite vast, so I highly recommend planning a few days to visit the park.  If you enjoy outdoor activities this is the place for you.  There are numerous hiking trails with various levels of difficulties, from the novice short trails to the longer hard to maneuver trails.  There are also several lakes and several places to fish.  Custer State Park is a great place to visit even if you do not want to hike or perform outdoor activities, due to the amazing views and scenery.  This is especially a great place to visit with your family and a great place for outdoor activities to involve your children.  I highly recommend Custer State Park, you will not be disappointed.

name: Laken Brock
text: Small fee for park entrance $20 for up to 7 days (good in any South Dakota state park) or $38 for the year! There are three different driving trails within the park. We took the wildlife loop. Normally the animals are more active around dawn and dusk. We went from 2-6 pm and saw many animals. Several groups of pronghorn, a couple hundred buffalo that came right up to the window, prarie dogs, lots of birds and Turkey. We spent all 4 hours on the road due to looking at the wildlife but plan at least an hour to complete this look. The views alone were stunning.

name: Jon Reed
text: Very nice people when you by your ticket, answered questions for is, great drive to v see Buffalo and good hike today.

name: Guru Ram
text: Custer state park is a must visit place when visiting black hills or Mount Rushmore area. The drive to custer park through iron mountain road is  totally amazing one. Be aware of abundant wildlife in custer state park, especially bison herd. The park roads, visitor centers and public areas are well maintained. We throughly enjoyed Needle highway and wildlife loop road on our visit. The roads are narrower in some places, so drive cautiously.

name: Joseph Stanfill
text: Amazing state park. Save the wildlife loop for a few hours before dusk. Sunday Gulch is an amazing but technical trail. Don't miss a burger at the Blue Bell.

name: Chad Reickard
text: Beautiful large park with so much to do! There are hiking trails and need drives (needle) and fishing and wildlife. There are buffalo, but the park is so big, I recommend visiting the Visitor Center 1st - they know where the buffalo are located. There was some road construction while we were there, so you might miss some stuff or have to drive a ways around. Beautiful park and a must visit in the Black Hills.

name: Rupesh Trivedi
text: Must visit place in SD...very beautiful scenic views across the park

name: Vicki Ware
text: We were hoping to see the buffalo and wild burros and were not disappointed! Was fun! Such a beautiful place!

name: anna pizzolo
text: Amazing! Outstanding and breathe taking sceneries. Wildlife at any corner. It's a must in a lifetime, it's as beautiful as a National Park. It should be advertised more. Very well mantained and many parts are wheel chair accessible.  Rangers are adorable and helpful. It's perfect for many kinds of outdoor activities.

name: Patty Capella
text: Lots of different things to enjoy.  We saw live full size Bison,  deer and antelope. Tame donkeys slowing traffic and reaching into different cars almost like Oatman, Arizona. The donkeys seemed to be tame as some people could actually touch them. Lots of driving up and down hills through small rock tunnels and one vast area of majestic huge boulders and unreal colors. So worth the stop.

name: Bob Dobbins
text: Bison and Big Horns walked right next to the car! Beautiful landscape! The wildlife loop (including the gravel side roads) is a must see for anyone visiting the park.

name: Eric Minor
text: Amazing place filled with Beauty and Wonder

name: Cow Town
text: This state park is always a blast to visit! Has things to do for everyone, lake side fishing/hiking, Buffalo, Restaurants and camping! Not to mention the lovely views you get here!

name: Nyor Mirror
text:
We hit Custer State Park around noon to fill in the afternoon after visiting Rushmore and Crazy Horse. I wished I would have researched this better because you could spend a week here enjoying everything Custer has to offer.

Encompassing 71,000 acres in the Black Hills, Custer State Park is home to abundant wildlife and adventure; camping, hiking, biking, swimming, fishing, or relaxing, there’s something here for everyone.

We did Needles Highway, wildlife loop, and Kayaked on Sylvan Lake. We later referred to it as the Yellowstone of South Dakota.

$20 entrance fee good for a week. We stayed in a Rapid City Airbnb and enjoyed the town’s proximity to the attractions and amenities. I definitely recommend and will return.

name: Vanessa Arruda
text: Love everything about it the camping, lakes, scenic trails, animals but mostly Needles Hwy ❤

name: Ian Allen
text: One of the highlights of our trip to the Black Hills! The wildlife loop road is beautiful all on its own but having the opportunity to see a herd of bison makes it all the more special! I recommend coming early to beat crowds—the beat route I think is to enter from 16A (after seeing Rushmore perhaps) to experience the Iron Mountain road, do the wildlife loop, and then finish on 87 (Needles Highway). This was an incredible drive that took up our whole morning and we kept noticing all the traffic was going the opposite way—we kind of had the road to ourselves! Highly, highly recommend!

name: Victoria Nowlin
text: Probably one of the most beautiful to see.  Allow a couple of days.   Needles hwy is a must and then do the other side of the park another day

name: Adriana Perez
text: It's a nice park with beautiful scenery but you have to go prepared with your own gear and even your own chairs.  I didn't see any seating areas and very few places where you can actually enjoy some shade.  Entrance fee is $20 and it's valid for a week.  We didn't go with any camping plans or even our own kayak, so it was just an ok experience for us.  Lots of great photo spots.

name: Dennis Rose
text: A huge park with over a thousand bison, many elk, donkeys which you can feed and scratch, deer, antelope, coyotes, prairie dogs and occasional bighorn sheep.  Delightful every time, especially when the bison lick salt off your vehicle and may be two feet away!

name: Alexander Witt
text: I use to take reservations for this campground via phone for a company that I was employed for. I did not realize how incredible this place was. Took my motorcycle through here and enjoyed every second. Hills, curves and turns everywhere and great views that go miles and miles in every direction. What is great is when you go through here, you end up at Iron Mountain Rd. and Mt. Rushmore. Incredible roads and views. Will be back. Superior.

name: Rachael Huisman
text: Beautiful park! We loved traveling Needles highway and seeing all the wildlife. Would recommend planning at least a whole day to explore this park

name: Bruce Z
text: Great hiking and good fishing in the lakes. Just be sure to respect the Bison and other wildlife. We had a loner come visit us while fishing at Legion Lake.

name: Samuel Everist
text: The wife and I ventured into this beautiful park while searching for hikers that would amaze. We hiked Lover's Leap and also Sylvan Lake's Sunday Gulch. These were the best trails we've hiked ever. Plus, this gem of a park is absolutely stunning. Worth the drive through at least if you're not a hiker.

name: larry cooper
text:
Custer State Park is one of America's finest parks. It ranks with some of the best national parks. It is large and many varied. It has great wildlife viewing opportunities, some of the best in the country for antelope, bison, wild turkey and prairie dogs.
The Needles Highway scenery is superb. The Iron Mountain Highway is very different but equally alluring. The vistas from Mount Coolidge are great.
If you like to hike, the opportunities are numerous.
The lodges are really nice and quite different from one another, thereby offering very different experiences.

name: Erik Kessel
text: Always enjoy our trips to Custer. Wildlife loop is pretty tame in early fall but still sone good scenery and of course the Burroughs were around... Bring apples and carrots!

name: Tami Archer
text: My favorite place. Try the coffee shop in Custer called Jane's coffee its amazing. The park is clean and beautiful. Also if you want carrots foot the donkeys the little grocery store in Custer is great!

name: See Lee
text: Beautiful!  Had to pay $20 to drive through Needles Highway.  The top was breathtaking.

name: Andrew Weisz
text: Fantastic experience! Go during the fall. It is mindblowing!!!!

name: Rae Rhoads
text: Wildlife loop drive is awe-inspiring. The buffalo "jam" is the coolest traffic jam to be caught in and these magnificent beasts are so much fun to watch up close. Great way to spend a gorgeous afternoon.

name: Ferretti Farmer
text:
Custer State Park was a lot of fun for the family. I would highly recommend two things if you decide to visit...
1) Take Iron Mountain Rd to get in. It's a blast with tight tunnels (no RVs) but I made it just fine with an F250.
2) Stop at the visitors center to see a map where the buffalo have been spotted that day.
The park is beautiful. The whole family loved it.

name: Tony Verchio
text: This is the crown Jewel of the Black Hills. The scenery and the wild life are definitely worth the trip. The hiking is great with many trails to choose from and trails for all levels of hiker.

name: A F
text: A beautiful park with many options for the family. Hiking, swimming, scenic drives. You can’t go wrong.

name: D Cooper
text: Hit the Wildlife Loop Road for some amazing buffalo encounters...Beautiful creatures!

name: Leah Kent
text: Beautiful and serene. We were there for a family wedding and it was absolutely perfect. Only complaint were that the beds in the cabins at the State Game Lodge were very bouncy yet much too hard for comfort.

name: Celeste Ruppelt
text:
Custer City is inside the Custer State Park. Crazy Horse is there.
It's a beautiful drive through the Park, coming up to Crazy Horse. Crazy Horse is still under construction and preparation for blasting was underway. When it is finished, the figure will be 563 feet tall and 641 feet long The 9-story face of Crazy Horse is completed.
In the evenings, at dark, (Memorial Day until the second Monday in October) a laser light show entitled 'Legends in Light' is presented. The views are best from a distance, but for an extra charge, over and above admission,there are bus tours available that will take one to the foot of the mountain.
The Visitor Center features exhibits, a movie, and made to scale models that will explain the carving process over the last 65 years.

name: Irish
text: Custer State Park is beautiful! Please don't pet the buffalo. They are wild and can hurt people. Stay in your vehicles. Wildlife loop where there's donkeys, prairie dogs, buffalo, mountain goats...etc. Peaceful and tranquil camping grounds, Mount Rushmore, and Crazy horse too!! Needles highway is pin turn curves and narrow tunnels.

name: Clara Hanson
text: This place is breathtakingly beautiful. I've never seen anything more beautiful. The narrow winding road leading up was scary but it was hard to keep your eyes on the road because of the towering rock formations. I would love to live there.

name: Traveling Man
text: Best park in this side of the state. Great views, wildlife, and peak at Mount Rushmore.  Wildlife loop is so fun with the burros. They love carrots and itching themselves on your mirrors. :/ Pronghorn and massive amounts of buffalo.

name: Troy Molde
text: Had a blast here.  Its a huge park, took us all day.  We started at rushmore  that took 45 min. Then went to crazy horse. Then went to keystone and checked out the shops, then drove custer park the rest of the day.  We stopped at the visitor center, i recommend watching the movie.  It was a full day. It was my wife, my 16 year old, my 11 year old and my 9 year old.  They had a blast. We walked around sylvan lake, it was so pretty.

name: Zoraida Arbelo
text: One of the absolute best parks I've been to!

name: Tom Crumlish
text: Wow. The scenery was spectacular and the wildlife was simply breathtaking! We went early and came upon a huge herd of bison which was nothing short of amazing. It was more than worth the trip!!

name: Keith Knobloch
text: I love Custer State Park...we enjoy every trip there.  This time we went to Sylvan Lake and hiked Black Elk Peak from there.  Unfortunately it was a summer Saturday, so difficult to find a place to park, a table to eat, and space at the beach after our hike.  I'd recommend hitting it on a weekday or off-season if your schedule allows.  Also, if you are from SD and visit other state parks, it's worth noting that you can't buy a one-day pass for $6 at Custer SP, they only do the 7-day pass for $20.  Plenty to do though, so well worth the money and the time finding a parking spot!  Highly recommend also: Sunday Gulch Trail, Poet's Table, and the Wildlife Loop.

name: Lizza G
text: Can I say enough? This place is an absolutely great experience, inside and out!

name: Erik Hannigan
text: Absolutely amazing as always. We drove through the wildlife loop and we got stuck in a buffalo jam, which was super neat! The gift shops and restaurants are fairly reasonable for prices and good food. I would highly recommend the needles highway as well. It was a blast to drive through and had some one of a kind views.

name: Daddy4G W
text: Favorite place in SD! Drive through and we had Bison in the road and everywhere, it was amazing! We also seen Pronghorns, Burros, Prairie Dogs, Whitetail, and of course many different birds! I would highly recommend visiting Custer Park!

name: Bill Mason
text: Excellent views!  Fed the donkeys and saw some bison herds.  Gotta go up to the top of Mt Coolidge Lookout.   UNBELIEVABLE VIEWS!  Make sure to pack a binoculars.   You can see Crazy Horse and Mt Rushmore with binos on a clear day.  When you look at Crazy Horse he is looking right at you!  So awesome when you can find him.  It's a really long ways away and it takes a good set of binoculars to see him.

name: Brent Bloomingdale
text: Very awesome park. We enjoyed the drive thru the park and the wildlife loop was totally amazing. We got to see donkeys, deer, buffalo, prairie dogs among other animals. Nice leisure drive and amazing scenery. I would recommend checking it out. My 5 yr old loves checking out the wild donkeys. There is a cost to get into the park but we'll worth it.

name: Robert Bowden
text: We had a fantastic time! The scenic views are spectacular and amazing wildlife is all around. Already planning our next visit back to Custer State Park! Wish we could have stayed longer.

name: Luke Peters
text: I loved Sylvan Lake and Needles Highway. The Wildlife Loop was okay, but perhaps it might have been better had we seen bison a bit more closely. We saw herds from a distance of 500 yards.

name: Ryan M Finch
text: Wow. A very great stop and not a waste of time at all.

name: Jennifer Olson
text: Beautiful and alot of interesting wildlife

name: scott valdez

name: David Clark
text:
The best buffalo herd is outside Custer. Off the "wildlife loop" in Custer State Park take road 6. This will lead you into a portion of Wind Cave National Park not connected to the rest. About a mile or two down the road is the best buffalo experience in the area.
Custer State Park itself is amazing, but the wildlife spotting can be hit or miss because of its immense size. This park offers the best views in the Black Hills as there are many overlooks on highway 16A and especially 87 which travel through this park. Mount Coolidge provides the best view, but the gate closes at 5. After 5 expect a couple mile walk, but the best place to watch the sun go down. Rushmore, Crazy Horse and the Badlands can be seen with the viewing glass on top of this mountain. After dark the lights of Crazy Horse can be seen clearly.

name: Julie Phillips
text: Loved this park so much, we bought a week pass for $20 and visited multiple days. It was off season, late April, so we could stop almost any time we wanted to take pictures or look at animals. Any time of day there were plenty of animals, deer everywhere! Multiple short tunnels and at one of them is a sign showing how the rocks actually look like a needle with an eye. At one point, a bus driver took a turn too tight and got stuck with the belly of the bus hung on the curb. Police let us slowly pass in the ditch so we we're not held up for long. The bus should never have been back there... This is one of my husband's all time favorite drives.

name: Clark Zealand
text: When trip planning, I read that Custer State Park is the next best place to see bison and other wildlife, outside of Yellow National Park, and it certainly did not disappoint. Within minutes of being in the park we saw Pronghorn and many beautiful birds we do not get to see on the east coast. As we travelled further into the park, we started to see more and more bison but that was the extent of our wildlife sightings on the first day. However, the second day entering the state park, we hit the wildlife jackpot. We saw no fewer than three massive herds of bison, all of which included several calves. One herd was causing a ‘buffalo-jam’ and hence, we sat in traffic for almost 20 minutes and just enjoyed watching the bison be bison! We drove around the entire park, including the famous needles highway and other scenic roads and then checked out the visitor center. The visitor center is very impressive and includes information that has relevance for both kids and adults. The staff were friendly and very helpful. Overall, this is an incredible place and I strongly recommend taking the time to visit! A trip to the Rapid City area is not complete with a visit to Custer State Park!

We went in mid April and there was still some snow on the ground, which made the hike more difficult than it needed to be. The other thing to note is that you need to pay an entrance fee to drive into the park since it is a state forest. To me this felt fine, as the money goes directly to maintaining this gorgeous forest.

name: Wallace Gutzmer
text: I always love driving through Custer State Park when in the Black Hills. You're very likely to see buffalo, antelope, and donkeys (bring a bag of carrots!) as well as wild turkeys, and prairie dogs. And if you're lucky you may even see elk and bighorn sheep. If you're very lucky--like I was last week-- your vehicle will actually be briefly surrounded by a passing buffalo herd; awe-inspiring. Just don't get out; buffalo are faster than a horse and can be very dangerous (take pictures from INSIDE you vehicle)! And you can spend as much- or little - time as you want driving through the various areas of the park as you like. Also, there is an excellent visitor center, restaurants, Coolidge Lodge, campgrounds, guided tours... plenty of choices for a day of adventure in the Southern Hills.

name: Randy Hill
text:
Although the recent tragic forest fire  decimated a good portion of the Park and there was some loss of wildlife as in every forest fire in tragic loss we find renewed life and new beginnings.
The loss of old growth Timber (Pine, Fir and even Elm, Ash and Oak) has a way of giving it's own unique version of rebirth.....the heat from the fire causes the pine cones to open and drop their seeds and the abundance of Wildlife that lives on those seeds will quickly spread the seeds every where they travel.
Of course with the death of light limiting trees overhead the grasses and wild flowers underneath will now really go crazy presenting a unique chance or opportunity to witness what mother nature can truly do.
To those who don't remember the Black Hills Area before the Bark Beetles destroyed thousands of acres of timber or the devastating fires of several years ago now....
Those areas are now teaming with life....first comes the grasses, wildflowers and brush. They in turn provide the early protection that seedling pines and fir trees need as they get established again....there is a great abundance of both species of trees (Pine and Fir )

Post Fire UPDATE ;
I had a question about the Miners Pack Donkeys asking about how they fared during the fire....sadly a couple did die from their wounds from the fire but the majority survived with only slight to moderate Burns and are healthy and back roaming their Same areas. A word or 2 about them....THEY ARE WILD and you need to respect them as such....just because they will eat it of your hand if they feel threatened the will respond.
If you want to feed them take Carrots, Apples  they love them and are a good source of vitamins for them....please no corn chips or bread .... processed foods .....their not built to handle that type food and will harm them in the long run.....Carrots, Apples, Cabbage, lettuce things like this are just fine and they can digest them ....we always take a mixed bag of certified weed free alfalfa cubes, carrots and Apples to feed to them when we go visit them so enjoy but be responsible about it please and thank you.

Time for a 2020 update;

The Park is recovering nicely from the Forest fire. It's so very cool to see why sometimes a fire can have a silver lining to it's dark cloud of ash and smoke.
New life is everywhere, the native grasses and wild flowers are on full display this summer and if your brave enough and take a short hike into burnt areas and look closely there are honestly hundreds of thousands of sapling seedling Pine, Spruce and some Fir trees sprouting under foot so at this rate the hills in the Park that are now dotted by dead burnt snags will be covered once again by Pines and in the Creek bottoms Fir and Spruce will once again be growing tall and straight.

Please keep in mind the Park is a very special place and way more than a vacation destination with it's lakes, streams, Camping and lodges and Cabins to visit....It's amazing Variety of true Western Wildlife is on full display for all to see.
It's full of history and truly has a magic all of its own, You can come into the park and you can actually feel the tension, the worry of every day life, the stress we are placed under, some of us 24/7/365 ...start to leave you almost the very minute after you enter the park, sure there are some who are so disconnected from the world around them that they wouldn't notice the magic even if it jumped up and bit 'em in the Butt ! They however are not to whom I am writing this.
The Park is full of places and things that just naturally seem to have a profound effect on those of us who are aware of the natural world around us.
My Wife and I call it "Green Therapy" and the best thing about it is it's free !!!!! All you have to do is get up around 5 A.M. , grab a cup of your favorite morning brew and head out to some quiet peaceful spot then just sit and watch the Sun rise, That feeling you experience of peace and calm that comes over you....is the Magic of Custer State Park...."Green Therapy" we call it.

name: Lauren Kopriva
text: I usually have great food here with good portions and it's a great atmosphere. Always busy. We went here two nights in a row becuase we had family in town. The first night we all ordered something with fish since its lent. Someone at my table got the wrong dish with meat in it. No big deal, they offered to fix it and make it right. We decided to come back the next night. Server was very nice, but it took over an hour to get our food. The kid's food came out way before ours and the chicken nuggets were raw. They offered to fix it. Our food came about 50 min later and my food was cold. They did make it right by comping the meal and bringing us some free drinks to make up for it. Very willing to fix it.  Issues are back in the kitchen that need sorted out. Maybe new cooks being trained?

name: Cory
text: Very good food very slow kitchen the past few times i have been in there from getting there to leaving was just over 2.5 hours.... we did order pretty quickly too.. food was worth the wait

name: Jeff Smith
text: This is one the best hidden gems in the hills! My wife and I went here based off of some of the reviews when we were trying to find somewhere new this past weekend. Hands-down this is the best chicken fried steak I have ever had, and the portions are just absolutely huge. I took about half of my lunch home and my wife took about half of hers home. Other than the fantastic meals the wedge salad is some of the best I’ve had. Everything is really well done and you definitely get more for your money here than at other places in the area.

name: Alecia H
text: Portions are always more than generous and the prices are great for what you get. Food is delicious, servers are friendly.

name: raven shelton
text: The food was excellent! The server was super friendly. Our order did end up a little messed up though and It all came out at once (appitizer and meal) and I had to ask for my salad. Over all it was pretty good.

name: Greg Egemo
text: Service was quick, fun ad awesome. Chelsy " bunker" rocks!!. Food was fantastic, prices are good. Happy experience. We shall return.

text: Excellent! Chelsea was wonderful!  She took great care of us and came back often to see if we needed anything.  We both had the queen ribeye and we agreed it was the best steak we have had in a long time.  The steaks are hand cut fresh daily.  They also have a great happy hour.

text: Amazing food, great atmosphere. Lovely date night.

text: Amazing food!  You can't go wrong here.   If anything there are too many choices!   Perfectly cooked and happy family!

text: Great atmosphere! Food was very tasty and delicious 👌. The only thing we had a issue with, it took almost 40 minutes for our food to be served. It was not busy at the time we were there. Overall, very good place!

name: Wendy Peacock
text: OMGOSH! Hands down some of the best food I've ever had! I have to admit, when I found out that we were going to have to wait over a half hour just to be seated, I really considered going somewhere else. But, the wait was TOTALLY worth it! My husband had the walleye tacos and I had the stacked nachos w/BBQ pulled pork. Both were out of this world!  I also had the tomato- mozzarella salad and it was super fresh! I HIGHLY recommend!

name: shelli j
text: Amazing food and service! Will definitely be back!

name: Terry Masters
text: The food was awesome, the artichoke spinach appetizer and chips was too notch. Group of 4 very satisfied customers. With plenty of leftovers for the next day.

text:
Food is exceptional, and my wife's a chef... So we have a picky pallet... We know what good is.
Friendly, clean, and like I said... Great food!

name: Sandy Wellman
text: Very good food and the service is great.

name: Melissa Gaines
text: We love coming here! Their beef dishes are top notch. My favorite is the Bloody Mary's that I personally think are the best in Spearfish! They also have delicious buffalo wings that have been hickory smoked and are delicious, today was just introduced to chicken fried bacon my new favorite!

name: Mike Wynia
text: Wow is all I can say from start to finish was amazing!! We had a table of seven and the place was packed on a Thursday night !! Food  was amazing came out hot and fresh and fast !! Huge portions !! Deff worth the price ... Will deff come back !! Ty and keep up the amazing work !!

name: Ray Kinard
text: Rarely have I found a place that has (1) delicious food (steak is tdf), (2) spectacular selection of whiskeys, and (3) great service from the moment you walk in the door all under one roof. This is the place for steak and whiskey.

name: Elizabeth
text: So good. Great service. Highly recommend the ribs!

name: Ron Smith
text: The Steerfish always has great lunch specials, a diversified drink and food menu, pleasant wait staff and nice atmosphere!   Today our table ordered the smoked prime rib dip, chopped huckleberry salad, a spinach salad with salmon, and a wedge salad with chopped/grilled chicken.  We were all pleased with our choices.  We always enjoy eating here and have a hard time narrowing down what  we would like to eat!  It is a wonderful place to meet friends for lunch or dinner.

name: Trevor Fisher
text: Delicious food good prices and friendly staff

name: Bryan Myers
text: Honestly had a great meal, great drinks and a very friendly staff.  If we were staying longer, we would definitely go back here.

text: Really nice place with pleasant people and atmosphere. Food is delicious. I had steak wit asparagus, mushrooms rice and sauce. It was to die for

name: Danette Eggleston
text: Very good! Great service, great food, hardly a wait at all to get some of the best food ever! The manager on duty was very good. He stopped by to see if everything was to our liking and I noticed how he checked out our plated food to make sure it was as it should be presented. For the quality of the food, the taste and the service, the price for our very pleasant dinner was, great! Definitely will be back.

name: Natalie Johnson
text: The service, atmosphere,  and food is fabulous.   They offer several beer brews.  They have really good steaks.  I had the steak tips which was not one I'd order again nor the Reuben sandwich.  The stuffed mushrooms are crazy good.  I would recommend this place for all purposes and ages.

Family friendly, bar seating and tables

name: Susan Hall-Martin
text: My steak was done to perfection! The wait staff was friendly and the manager stopped by to say hello. I love this place for my steak fix!!

name: lesa krajewski
text: The ribeye was excellent. My husband likes medium well and I like medium rare. Both Cuts were delicious.

name: Jordan Arndt
text: Waitress was prompt on refills and requests. Food was hot and absolutely mouth-watering delicious. Had the Devils Tower burger, and couldn't stop eating. Pulled pork topping the burger was sweet, and savory with the best medium cooked burger I've had in a long time. It was a big burger as well. Had the smashed fries. Were very delicious, with lots of seasoning, but a little too spicy for my preference. Good food nonetheless. Definitely recommend this place to anybody. Does have steakhouse pricing so be prepared for that. Awesome food! Awesome service! Awesome atmosphere!

name: Jennifer Peterson
text: Took the kids out for a treat today and we had a nice lunch. We learned a lot abt the different menu items and had a tableside guacamole tray get made infront of us at our table , which the kids didn't know what table side was and so they thought this was pretty cool. It was a lil pricey ($7.00 for kids mac n cheese)and the service was so so but the food was local and made in new and interesting ways (ranch w feta cheese) and the building was one of the original settled mercantile locations in Spearfish so there's some historical value. Portions were quite rich and large and I liked that they served the kids fresh fruit too.

name: Gail Biers
text: Our 2nd time here and can't wait to go back!!   Big menu,  so many great choices, great food!

name: Michael Kedik
text: Nice place with LOTS of choices. Service was attentive and fairly fast. I was there during lunchtime and it was not crazy busy. There is a lot of construction nearby which I'm sure is affecting overall number of customers. Give it a try; you will not be disappointed.

name: Colton Clark
text: Service was mediocre at best as was the food

name: Dylan Finn
text: Best restaurant in Spearfish

name: Brian Bartholomew
text: The food and atmosphere were a solid 4.5 but the service was pretty disappointing.  Everytime we asked our waitress a question, she acted like she couldn't care less.  Prices were a bit steep but quality was high so I really can't complain too much about that.  Other than the issue with service, everything was pretty good.

name: Richard Stainbrook
text: Great service and food. You will not walk away hungry.

name: Carole
text: Excellent happy hour deals. Can't beat the half price appetizers. Smoked chicken wings with dry rub are the best according to my husband. The smoked trout tacos were also good. Great service from Ramie. We will be back.

name: Carl Hoffmann
text: Great food, ribs were excellent!

name: Ted Hosselkus
text: Good atmosphere & food.  Have been here several times.  Average entree is about $16 with steaks costing around $27.  Service was very good.  Bar side is significantly louder.  Good beer selection.  Good kids menu.

name: Nick Baker
text: Great lunch menu, fast service, amazing hospitality. I got in, sat at the bar, ordered based off of the recommendation given to me by the bartender, and ate within 30 minutes. Probably one of my best lunch experiences in Spearfish.

name: Tessa Allen
text: Awesome food and atmosphere! They have happy hour from 4-6 everyday I believe and the apps menu is HUGE and the portions are HUGE. I just fed 2 adults and 2 kids for $25! Great quality and tons of variety, you really can't ask for more!

name: Chris Edward
text: Great family place. Good food.

name: Ralph Massarczyk
text: Very good selection of western and smoked food, also liked the vegetarian options. Good service

name: Steve & Mar ia
text: We  had an amazing Server..I am sorry I do not remember her name. It was a very busy night and she did not miss a beat.  There was 9 of us celebrating 2 birthday's. Reservation was under Jones

name: Jane Johns
text:
This is not a 5 star restaurant (i.e. not white linen).  That said, I reserve 5 stars for great service and great food for the price point of the restaurant.

Steerfish Steak and Smoke has an extensive menu.  I ordered the walleye and my partner had a steak.  The walleye was a very generous portion and was very good.  My partner stated that his steak was cooked correctly and had great flavor.

They served us corn muffins with our meal and the cinnamon/honey butter was really yummy (I inquired about the butter, they make it themselves).

The only thing I would critique is that the restaurant is noisy.  However, that is likely due to the fact that they were super busy; a good sign that the locals love eating there too.

This restaurant is an excellent value for the money.

name: Deezul
text: Incredible food

text: Absolutely amazing food! And the staff was excellent as well! Highly recommend this restaurant!

text: Well... the drinks were good. Everything was good except the steaks. Steaks were burnt. Black crispy burnt. Yuck. Service was extremely slow as well. Wont be back.

text: Came for drinks and desserts and all was amazing.  Our waitress, Hannah, was amazing and very attentive.  We kept her running and she seemed happy to serve us.  We will be back!

text: Excellent, tasty food! Our server, Binker, was awesome! Love, love, love this place! We'll be back! I had the Mountain Oyster appetizer, I have to say,  they had better flavor than the ones I cook at home. I wish I had your batter recipe, it allowed the flavor of the 'oyster' to come through.

name: John Strand
text: Was not all that great.  Asked for no cheese on my green chili nor on my salad.  Got cheese on both.  Asked for salmon on the salad, got chicken...  The chicken was very dry and burnt. The most burnt pieces were carefully covered under the spinach in the salad.  It also took forever.  I really want this place to rock... Every time I go there stuff like this happens.

name: Callie Ackerman-Jasper
text: Huge menu, fun entrees, lots of types of beer and alcohol.

name: chris weeks
text: Great food, great service, great atmosphere. Prices were pretty steep but it's what I expect to pay for a place like this. My one criticism is that their menu uses unique names for every section and every menu item. In order to have any idea what you're looking at you have to read the description on everything. It's like you need an answer key to decode the thing. Maybe that's a bit harsh, but if I have to read the description on 4 menu items to realize I'm in the sandwich section, you're doing something wrong. All said, I will be back again.

text: A little loud, but still the best place for a ribeye in town

text: Great food great service

text: I ordered the Guacamole Burger. Nice size burger but absolutely no seasoning.  The smashed had too much seasoning. The restaurant was very warm and noisy.

name: Larry Jeffries
text: Absolutely marvelous as usual. I highly recommend. I ordered crab-stuffed mushrooms which I have ordered three times in the past. Again they are marvelous.

name: Dan Halloran
text: Amazing steaks and sides

name: Mary Duncan
text: Very nice place. Very clean and excellent food. Great waiters all of them hustling. Great selection on the menu. A little spendy but again excellent!

name: DL Bradford
text: The food was not great. Too many competing flavors for our taste.  Did not feel well after dinner and all night.

name: Dustin Floyd
text: I'll be honest: We weren't expecting much from a place with such a ridiculous name. But we'd heard good things from friends, so we gave it a try for lunch, and we weren't disappointed. Food was incredibly good, with well-cooked meats and strong flavors. Smoked meat is what they do, but there are a handful of good-looking vegetarian and salad options on the menu. We didn't have any drinks or desserts, but the menus looked promising. Pricing was very reasonable. Staff was very friendly and took great care of us. Decor and ambiance were amazing: the historic stone-block building used to be a general dry goods store (among many other things), and the vintage fixtures and exposed beams gave the place a really fun vibe. We'll absolutely come back!

name: ron svatos
text: Absolutely amazing food. Worth the price

name: Brent Babcock
text: Great food and great service!!

name: Nathan Peters
text: This was a great Steakhouse in downtown Spearfish. Very friendly staff. Great food. A bit loud for my liking though. Not due to music and such, but rather to the general atmosphere noise of people talking and plates clinking, etc. Parking is very tight for this restaurant so I would plan on coming early to find a parking spot as you may have to walk a block or two. However downtown Main Street is right there as well. I also would recommend that you call ahead to reserve seating as this is a very popular restaurant.

name: Kelsey Stephens
text: We're locals and this is the spot we take company and go for special occasions. However that will be changing. Service is terrible, wait 15 minutes for a beer, asked for waters multiple times never got any. It has been worse each time we come back. How can a steakhouse be out of pork when that is half their menu?  Zero gluten free options Much better places in town, with better service and less noise.

name: Ellie
text:
Food was very good! We had the prime rib dip, sirloin steak tips on rice, and a sirloin steak. Everything was fresh and well plated. If you need any extra reason to go, the corn muffins served when you arrive make it worth a visit!

One downside of the visit was a 50 minute wait for our food after ordering with no explanation as to why. In previous meals at this establishment we did not expireinece such a long wait, so it may have been a side effect of the holiday travelers.

name: Anne Simmons
text: Friendly staff and generous portions. Good food!

name: Gerri Lynn Owens
text: Excellent!!!! I do mean excellent atmosphere, food and service!!!  Our first time there but it won't be our last!!!  I have already shared our experience with family and friends...

name: James Vande Hey
text: The food is always 5/5. Most times the service is amazing however im only giving steerfish 4/5 because probably every third or fourth time i go in the service is horrendous and even if there are no other customers the service is poor and slow. At one time my spouse and i went for dinner, there were two other tables and my wife was given the wrong meal but we never had the opportunity to let anyone know as no one ever came to check on us. Most of the time the service is good and i do continue to return, but if i have more bad experiences i will probably stop coming in.
