The Arnold was sour and bitter like the machines had not been cleaned properly.
My brother told them about that we all have experienced flat to bad tasting drinks so not that big of deal.
My meal was really good so was our friend's
But the Steak tips and eggs my brother got and keep in mind that place prides themselves on thier steak tips!
Tips were cold like they just came out of refrigerator cold.
Waitress was great and apologized but its the cook who needs to apologize and needs better training!
What was not divulged during our conversation with the manager on duty is we were both cooks him in the NAVY for the Admiral of his ship.
I was a cook at 2 different steak house.
So we know food handling and proper cooking techniques cold food like that will eventually get someone fired and business closed !

She came back with one piece of cake cut in three tiny pieces with whipped cream on three plates. The pieces were seriously no BIGGER than two inch pieces. Really. We again, not the first time we've stayed away for a year or more because of a bad experience, will NOT be back for a long while.

text: The Bridal Veil Falls is a great and beautiful waterfall. Because this place is located near Spearfish Canyon, it is a nice drive to it! name: Jeannine Szostak
text: Every moment of every day is so eerily similar yet so incredibly different. The area is so remote and expressive that you feel like you’ve gone to a different planet. Some of the trails are very easy, others, not so much. You can see a lot from the parking lot but you can’t really get a feel for it unless you surround yourself with the rock formations. Make sure to come back around sunset (which is earlier due to the rocks) and get some cool photos. Bring a lot of water if you’re going exploring, and consider something like a Chilly Pad. Definitely worth exploring for multiple days.

name: Joshua MacGregor
text: Beautiful park in Western South Dakota.  One of the most unstated and underrated ones that I know of.  Big Horn Sheep can be frequently seen here.  Not crowded.  Close to the town of Wall, SD where there are plenty of amenities.  Skip Crazy Horse Memorial and spend less here and get way more!

name: Chanchal
text: It's amazing. One of its kind. Driving through this was fun. There are places you can find prairie dogs, big horn sheep, bisons etc. There are so many scenic points to click pictures and take a look at rocky mountains, land formations, steep canyons. We were there on a sunny day so would recommend travel with energy drinks, water, sunscreen, hat. Do stop your vehicle at various overlook points, it's beautiful ; The Fossil Exhibit Trail, Pinnacles Overlook, Yellow Mounds Overlook, White River Valley, Panorama Point etc.

You will see bison, pairie dogs, birds and even snakes.  It is vast so driving around it is probably the best idea.
Aside from nice scenery and lots of social distancing, there isn't much else to see at the Badlands so if you're looking for entertainment, this isn't for you.

name: Makayla Preuss
text: This place is so beautiful and there's so much to see. I'd recommend to have at least a full day to see it all. I'll definitely be going back!

name: Sylvia Moya
text:
Magical scenery.  I felt so tiny and insignificant seeing the vast, dramatic landscape and rock formations. Truly spectacular. We traveled in an RV and when it became dark, i felt unsafe to continue driving. The roads are not lit, so ve mindful when traveling and trying to reach a destination. We stepped at one of the overlook areas and being in pitch darkness os just as amazing. You definitely must experience this. Vest part was scaring the kids at night.  ;)

Not sure why I was charged $30 for my vehicle when the website says $25

name: Davidson Koay
text: Beautiful place with magnificent lookout. If you decide to go on Castle Trail, round trip is about 12 miles, you will be able to pass Saddle Pass Trail as well. Make sure to bring plenty of water because it very hot during the summer time.

name: Jason Arnold
text: Such an awesome place so much to see you may need 2 days to really enjoy the park. Lots great scenery.

name: Dinesh Shrestha
text: The badlands national park is breathtaking and magnificent.  I was amazed to see this unbelievable landscapes within a few hundred miles from the place where I live. The visitor center is very informative and helpful. The maps and brochures they have us were very useful. The badlands has a number of foot trails, camping sites, and road trip routes. We had a very limited time to spend in the park however we chose to take  an one hour driving route around the park that lead us to magnificent landscapes in the park. This route has a lot of scenic view stops. They signs and direction were helpful. We got chance to see prairie dogs and mountain goats. We walked through one of the footrails. I will definitely come for a hiking and camping next time.

name: Red Faux
text: A very beautiful place to stop with many places within it that you'll just have to take pictures. Parents.... watch your children. There are many places that are not fenced and seriously unsafe. This is also part of the beauty as you can touch, walk into the natural areas. Some decent places to stop and eat, buy trinkets and piddle. Decently clean in most places.

name: Laken Brock
text: Beautiful formations, lots of overlooks to pull over and see the landscapes (I didn't feel comfortable letting my little ones out of the car though as there were many places without guardrails). Not as much wildlife activity as Custer state park, but we did see pronghorn and biscon. There was a $30 entrance fee which is separate from the south dakota state park weekly or annual fee. It gets very hot here and the road grade can get intense. I was glad that we parked our travel trailer and did not try to pull it though the badlands.

name: Glenn Zior
text: Awesome place with lots of interesting views. Not too busy. Well worth a visit.

name: Ferretti Farmer
text: A must see! Beautiful. Our family loved it. We were lucky enough to see a lot of wildlife as well (including big Horn sheep). This is a National Park everyone should put on their bucket list

name: Ольга Демидова
text: One of the most beautiful places to visit in the USA. Spectacular views and a lot of wildlife (we saw a bighorn sheep). A lot to think about erosion. Easy access. Lots of trails. Not too crowded. Your entrance ticket is available for 7 days.

name: Greg Prince
text: No words are good enough to explain the feelings you experience while here, pictures try but fall far short also!  What a beautiful piece of our America.

name: Kendall Larson
text: This is a very high quality national park. Most people that come to South Dakota come for Mt. Rushmore and Custer state park, but the badlands is also an amazing stop. It stands out from anything I’ve ever seen in my travels, and it keeps drawing me back for another visit. Even the badlands in Teddy Roosevelt National Park in North Dakota don’t compare. A must see if you’re ever in South Dakota.

name: Bethany
text: So beautiful seen some Buffalo was so cool!!! We will be back!!

name: Blaxon Bourbon
text: Beautiful place. I definitely recommend you take a day or two to just go out in the wilderness and wander. There are a few unmarked trails that take you to truly remote and untouched areas. Only do this if you have a gps, know orienteering, or some combination.

name: Michelle Glaser
text: Awesome place and what a beautiful place to see.

name: Joanna Pahlow
text: Great park very interesting. Do the notch trail hike.

name: ralph hartsoe
text: Beautiful, different from any landscape I'd ever seen before.  Riding Motorcycles through, made it even better..  highly recommend to drive through and see this natural beauty of the USA

name: Martin Webb
text: Always a new look.  Peaceful.

name: M. Anastasia Busckova
text: June is a great time to visit.   The temperature is comfortable and everything is so green.  Pronghorn, buffalo and Prairie Dogs!

name: Michael West
text: Absolutely amazing. If you are in the area make you take the time visit.

name: Eric Salas
text: The Badlands National Park is one of the main attractions in South Dakota. Via I90, visitors coming from or going to Mouth Rushmore usually stop by to be amazed of its rugged terrains. Born out of volcanoes 30 millions years ago, the Badlands is a natural wonder that can be appreciated most by driving along a zigzag loop that takes you to its base.

name: Calcorax Productions
text: Beautiful, rugged nature. Do yourself a favor and get off the tourist loop and hike some trails. BRING WATER look out for snek!

name: CR R
text: Beautiful to ride to. Great info station and awesome view points to park at. Very cool fossils

name: Tim Braley
text: It was a beautiful day to visit and plenty of wildlife including, big horn sheep, prairie dogs, and bison not crowded and we'll worth the drive....

name: Twisted Oak Photography
text: This is amazing!! You doubt realize how small you really are till you come here.

name: Meg Buchanan
text: Hot but awesome. Definitely go in fall!

name: Julie Phillips
text: Beautiful with lots of animals. Gorgeous view at sunset and dusk, with the colors shining off the rocks. Visited multiple days and saw animals at all times of the day. Highly recommend the Badlands!

name: K B
text: if you are able to go for a walk.....I hope you do. I saw a bald eagle, a golden eagle. several hawks and a couple gazillion prairie dogs...in a couple hours. Buffalo are relatively easy to find, at least if you are willing to ask a couple knowledgeable folks. Bighorn sheep can...can...be found but may be a little more hit or miss.  When you DO find them....voila. What a beautiful habitat to observe them in. If you are unfamiliar with the Badlands area, it is possible you will spend a lot more time than you expected because of the incredible hold that it can impart on you and yours.

name: michael sharp
text: Cool views all the way around including walking trails and Rocky Mountain Sheep.  Also cool views of the Black Hills.  There was no social distancing here despite a few people wearing masks.

name: RV Allen Jr
text: Oh my gosh the most amazing place on earth

name: Daniel Hoey
text: We caught it when it was not so beastly hot. Lovely place. So green during the summer of 2019...we very much recommend visiting.

name: Kristen Schell
text: So many awesome hiking trails for all types of hikers. The trails are all marked so you won’t get lost. A beautiful place to visit. Must see!

name: John Livaditis
text: Beautiful land. Climbing out here is about as fun as it gets. Saddle Pass Trail is a must.

name: Tony Verchio
text: I have lived near hear for a long time and this year the park is the most beautiful ever. With our wet year all the colors in the park pop and it was a joy to visit. The visitor center as a very good 20 minute movie playing on a loop that tells you the history of the park and about the geological formations and wildlife. There are hiking trails and scenic overlooks in abundance. Definitely worth a stop on travel through western South Dakota.

name: Tom Rydz
text: It is OK. Same scenery throughout with little change. Best walk is near visitor center, cliff edge. Not worth spending a night. Cedar Cabins are inside the park but AC did not work and it took 2 days to fix. Food is bad and it is fly infested. Windows don't open or stay open, service bad. Check in is 4. Not 355. Not 359..4. They just don't care. Try calling the desk direct (not the reservation number, the office). They put you on hold and leave you...never come back. Simply not worth the stay in so.many ways. Just do the drive through off I90. Go in one side, out the other and be on your way.

name: Tiffani Bussie
text: Beautiful. Breath taking. Great hiking. Some paved areas for people who are not able to walk on rugged trails.

name: D Cooper
text: Wow!!! Lots of wildlife and observation points to take in the beautiful scenery.

name: Alex Pellegrineschi
text: Beautiful park with several panoramas view points, activities for kids, and great camping areas. Depending on your interests you can visit this park in few hours or days. I strongly recommend the night sky program or any stargazing activity.

name: John Massie
text: I feel like this is one of the hidden gems of South Dakota. Everyone that comes to visit me wants to see the Black Hills and My Rushmore and while they're both equally awesome in their own right, the Badlands is just as awesome. The park changes with every road and turn you take. It's amazing how you can go just a half mile down a road and the whole park looks completely different!

name: Ourperfectlyimperfectlife
text: What can I say, this is an amazing place. There is nothing like the South Dakota badlands. It is beautiful in the day time and at sunset as well as during thunderstorms and of course at night. We love taking the back way on Sage Creek road where you can often see wildlife.

name: Jennifer Lundberg
text: Such an interesting landscape! The whole family ages 3 to 80 loved getting out and walking the trails and climbing around. Would highly recommend to anyone.

name: Brad Barker
text:
A beautiful national park that deserves more than just a drive through visit. Take time to get out of your car and walk on some of the trails. Do be careful of wildlife and stay 100 yards back.

Pets are allowed in the park but must be on a 6’ leash and are not allowed on any trails in the park (dirt or boardwalk). Pets should also be kept away from wildlife-especially at prairie dog towns since the fleas carry plague.

name: HerbnKathyRV
text: Wonderful scenic drive takes a couple hours if you stop along the way at the overlooks.  Amazing landscape

name: Mike From Michigan
text: Beautiful canyons on the left. Herds of bison on the right. Not much else. $35 to enter the park.

name: Ian Allen
text: An incredible landscape, accessible for pretty much anybody. Whether you want to do a simple drive, or set out and do some hiking, this park has something for everyone. While the formations are beautiful, they were enhanced by the fields of yellow wildflowers that gave the land a contradictory look—on the one hand lush and on the other somewhat lunar. Definitely recommend planning an early morning visit as this place can become unbearably hot during mid day. We ended up coming twice, once just to do the loop road through the park en route to Rapid City, and another time to get out and do some of the shorter hikes.

name: Martha Roberts
text: Beautiful scenery, awesome wildlife, terrific views at sunset.

name: Donna J
text: Beautiful scenery and wildlife!  A must see!  One of GOD'S  many wonderful creations

name: Max Kaftanati
text: Plenty of amenities, lots of great views to take pictures, as well as plenty of wild animals to see. Recommend going there late Spring all the way into the Fall.

name: Randy Sessions
text: Scenery was spectacular

name: Rachael Huisman
text: Absolutely amazing! We spent the entire day here, and could have easily extended it in to 2 days if I would have planned it better. The landscape is breathtaking. My kids loved exploring, and my 6 year old participated in the the Jr Ranger program. Make sure you inquire about this at one of the visitors centers if you have kids.

name: Ben Roman
text: Beautiful, unique geology and some wildlife scenery, hadn't been for a few years during rally. Park raised their rates for bikes from $10 couple years ago to $25!! A bit of BS, but is what it is.

name: Doug Schwartz
text: It was a great trip through the Park.I have lived in SD for 21 years . and we have never been here. It is an amazing creation and makes Us realize What amazing things We have in our State

name: Sol Sukut
text: Make time to stop at several of the view points. Also according to the Ranger you can climb & hike where you want, so let the kids stretch their legs.  As for actual trails there are a couple short wheelchair/stroller accessible ones plus a couple multi-milers.  There are several rest rooms along the 30 mile loop as well as a few picnic spots.

name: Melissa Laskey
text: Absolutely breath taking views! Saw many mountain goats and prairie dogs! Can spend hours in this park!

name: M G
text: Loved it. Beautiful. Smells so nice after the rain.

name: Phil Trivilino
text: Great place. Wondrous natural rock and Earth formations.

name: Jeff
text:
Must see. Indescribable. But I’m gonna attempt to describe it anyway…

No, upon further reflection, it truly is indescribable. Go see it. No matter the cost.

We visited it on two separate days, and are still in awe.

name: Marty billman
text: Loved it.  Get there early in day. The rocks heat up quick.  Wear a hat and drink lots of water

name: Brandon Powell
text: $20 admission is absolutely worth it! Be sure to drive all the ways to the Roberts prairie dog it’s a good little drive but so worth seeing the prairie dogs! Walked right up to the babies.

name: Eric J
text: Awesome place to spend a couple of days. Out of this world landscape with lots of animals.

name: Mike Bailey
text: Great vistas, wildlife and clouds.

name: Justin Warner
text: Cannot recommend this place enough. Easy access, you can see so much beautiful from your car, but also rad, rewarding trails that would be fun for an advanced hiker.

name: Liz JA
text: Love this place! I would loved to be able to spend long periods of time here in the Badlands. The barren landscape. The rock layers that can be seen are just too beautiful for words or pictures to describe. I just think it is too bad that there are so many people there so that I can't be alone in solitude to contemplate...or just not think. And yes, I know, I add to the people problem too.

name: Troy Molde
text: Pretty amazing scenery.  You can hike a trail thats about .75 miles. We saw buffalo, sheep   and prairie dogs.  Its 25 dollars to get in and the long trail took us about 1.5 hours. We're pretty fast people.

name: Daddy4G W
text: It is a sight to see that can not be explained in a review. It is definitely worth the visit. But once you seen it you really dont need to visit again.

name: Levi Mosier
text: Cool formations worth driving through

name: Jetlover X
text: Simply a wonderful national park with unbelievable views and great sceneries. A must see. Highly recommended!

name: jennifer johnson
text: It's a little redundant but totally worth the drive.  We saw bison, big horn sheep amd tons of prairie dogs.  Some of the views were absolutely stunning.

name: ellen b
text:
HOME since spending many summers as a kid here,it is hime and you cant miss views the Badlands are so beautuful allow ti.e for kids to run & fully enjoy climbing all the butted.  The views never get old for me. I DO wish the would put p
Back the cedar pass overlook though and do a bit more roadwork!.

name: Andrew Goodrich
text: Amazing to travel through!

name: Gus Panella
text: Inspirational views and clean air. Great place to escape the rat race.

name: Tracey Janisch
text: Truly nothing to saw other then breath taking especially when you come from flat land

name: Bon Manhkong
text: This place is magical! No words to describe the natural beauty!

name: Kelly Ghee
text: Scenic drive. $20 to get in. Lots of places to stop for photos along the way and a nice walkway with interesting information about the history at the end. A must do when visiting The Black Hills.

name: BobKaren Brown
text: Stark natural beauty. Uncrowded. Lots of wildlife. Clean air.

name: Jeremy Warnken
text: This place is awesome you will see big horn sheep, buffalo, Perry  dogs and deer. The gift shop next to the welcome center has a Great restaurant

name: Michelle Taylor
text: The views are incredible worth the trip!

name: Hanoch Raviv
text: Great park to visit - tip- try to enter the park from the west side through the gravel road- check on google maps for the “prairie dog” place and just drive on the rim road

name: Lee Keller - 360
text: Another fantastic park that you should not miss.

name: Kristin Castenschiold
text: Beautiful scenery, come early and stay late to see it in all it's glory. Food was decent and when we went in September it was quiet with lots of parking!

name: J
text: Badlands National Park is badass. One of my favorite national parks and I've been to quite a few you can explore for months and never see it all.

name: Trinity
text: Visitor center is smaller than expected. Film was informative and a chance to relax.  The girls enjoyed the gift shop.  We enjoyed the door and window trails.

name: Leah Moody
text: This was a great family trip! We had so much fun climbing and hiking the trails.

name: Bhanu Petla
text: Geological wonder! Very quiet and scenic mountains formed as a result of wisdom of soil by the elements of nature. A must see attraction.

name: Robin Bramlett
text: Awesome experience!

name: Wendy Peacock
text: So beautiful! We spent the whole day here--even in the 94° heat! Beautiful and very informative visitors center. I want to take my 5 year old grandson with us next year! He will LOVE it! Just be sure to have lots of water!

name: Nadia P
text: This is a unique and beautiful place!

name: Melanie aka Lanieiniowa
text: Liked the park, very pretty even though it was raining.  Fees to get in are like $20 and we drove around a loop then headed on our way. Nice visitors center, lots of places to pull over and take pictures. I think the rainy day made the colours even prettier.

name: Gayle Cinnamon
text: Amazing! So beautiful.  You pay to enter and drive the "loop". Many pull offs, a visitor center and hiking areas. Get has before going and pack lots to drink. Not many stops.

name: Nancy Crocker
text: Very scenic. The Park Service Rangers were extremely informative, we were able to fill up our water tank at the facuet near the visitor center.

name: Lori Corn
text: Pictures in books and websites don't do this national park justice! Truly unique every path you explore. We went in June 2019 after they had a lot of rain and the yellow flowers blanketing the prairie were in full bloom. Paths easy to hike! Bring water, snacks and sunscreen and enjoy getting lost in the unique structures in the park. Saw a family of bighorn sheep while we were there. Best kept secret of all the national parks!

name: Terry Bloom
text: Always enjoy the Badlands and Wall !

name: Luke Wiley
text: This is great place to get out and play! Fun and beautiful. Great views and awe inspiring formations.

name: Steven Price
text: Nice trails to get out and explore the area.  Very good informative and educational signs explaining what you're looking at.

name: Dave Den Adel
text:
Do you want a lunar experience without going to the moon ??? Than head to the Badlands of South Dakota !! Badlands is Lakota for Badlands and South Dakota is English for South Dakota. The Badlands are like the moon in every way except for the oxygen, grass, trees, buffalo and ten dollar entrance fee. In fact, I wouldn’t be surprised if the moon landing wasn’t filmed here, at night. Either formed by millions of years of wind erosion or created 10,000 years ago by God, the park is a beautiful drive  worth getting off I-90 for. Be sure to hit Wall Drug after your lunar adventure...
🌛🌜🌔🛰🛰🛸🚀

name: Charlie Dango
text: Beautiful park. Great views from road that winds throughout as well as from many scenic lookout points. Trail system is well marked. Bring water as trails provide no shade. Buffalo and Big Horn Sheep can be seen in and around the park.

name: mark gloww
text: Beautiful place!

name: Anupa D.
text: A long drive through gorgeous landscape. The geology and geological features of this place are amazing. I weren't aware that clambering off trail and onto the rocks/hills etc were totally okay at this park (which is quite unlike any other National Park) and I was unhappy that people were doing this. They have a visitors center at just one end of the park, so you won't know until you get there! Lots of bison, deer (pronghorn and mule), prairie dogs, bighorn sheep, cliff swallows and other birds and animals to be found all over the park. The spur road off the west entrance is a must do short drive.

name: Joe Joe
text: Beautiful scenary well worth the $30.00.. Seen it in the snow barely covering it was nice as well. Someday see it with out snow. Sone places you can walk. Wild life consists of buffalos, prairie dogs, deer, longhorn sheep, some of these arnt where we live N.W. Illinois.

name: Sandra L Ledbetter
text: Thankful for the chance to see this great land of ours

name: Michelle Gilmore
text: Had a fantastic time in the badlands. With our family

name: Angie Sutton
text: AMAZING drive! A "must do" on your trip. Lots a spots time climb a little and take photos.

name: Jim Smith
text: Wish we had more time.  We did see the new herd of free range  bison grazing

name: igofastr6
text: Best at sunrise and sunset.

name: Dragon Steamwerx
text: Incredible views

name: Shane Wigginton
text: Absolutely beautiful. A must see.

name: Alyssa Love
text: GREAT views, can be dangerous in extreme heat, trails are very mixed, great for starter hikers and more experienced ones as well.  Beautiful place, interesting gift shops, and a cute diner.

name: Patty cavlovich
text: I love this place.it is so beautiful and seen alot of animals

name: Chad Reickard
text: DO NOT SKIP THIS VISIT. Our favorite part was the ground hogs! They are so cute! You can walk out among the burrows, and if you get lucky they will pop out right next to you. The babies are adorable and the dogs "bark" and wag their widdle tails. The ground formations of the badlands are amazing to look at and in some areas you can hike down into the dunes. It gets hot so bring plenty of water and some snacks.

name: J May
text:
Absolutely beautiful! We drove the loop during the day and got a great view of the Badlands. There were a few buffalo at the entrance and some prairie dogs throughout.

The next morning we got up for a sunrise timelapse. Amazing color in the early morning. On the way out of the park we saw a herd of big horn sheep!

name: Mike Morgan
text: Great hiking and exploring for all levels. Brilliant colors at sunset/sunrise. Wildlife galore.

name: Stephen CARLSON
text: Great place to visit wonderful rocks wonderful pine tree smell fantastic place

name: Anu Chitrangana
text: This place feels like a different planet.

name: Dee Real
text: As soon as I saw the area, it reminded me of so many movies, like "Red Planet", "Starship Troopers", so I Googled it, and sure enough movies were made here, " Dances with wolves",  "Thunderheart," "Armageddon," "Starship Troopers", "National Treasure: Book of Secrets", just to name a few!!!

name: Terry Wittgren
text: This is a great scenic ride on a bike or a great trip in a car the whole family will enjoy the scenes wildlife and the walks love this place.

name: Steve Watkins
text: Wonderful day at the park! 17F no wind and no one around.

name: Markus Maurer
text: Was a bit disappointed. There are better national parks

name: Cynthia Niswonger
text: A dream come true to visit this amazing place.  It surpassed my expectations.  We drove the road from the North to the South thru the Badlands.  Many places to pull over and snap photos.  This kids enjoyed climbing and exploring.  Beautiful sights at every turn.

name: JuanTool's Do Work
text: Great place,very awesome to see.

name: Deborah Barron Brown
text: Super incredible.  I am sorry we could only spend a day there.  We spent the night overlooking the Badlands.  Popular easy trails are well marked.  We have an RV and pull a car.  We were able to drive through the whole park, park at various stopping points without ever having to take the car off. We went in the middle of June the weather was in low 70s and it wasn't terribly crowded (there definitely were people).  We will come back someday and spend a lot more time.

name: Ernest Go
text: Appreciation to nature's wonders! The Badlands is a must see destination if traveling to South Dakota.

name: Laurel Gehrke
text: Fabulous scenery. Cute little prairie dogs. Bison seen in distance.

name: Tammie Crane
text: Absolutely beautiful!!! I dispersed camped on the south rim for a week. Just an amazing all natural place.

name: Marianela Lozada
text: Beautiful 😍

name: Megan Smith
text: I like that boulder. That's a nice boulder.

name: Silhouette Shop
text: Beautiful. We saw goats and prairie  dogs. Many of our group enjoyed climbing some of the rocks.

name: Ryan Medici
text:
This place is REALLY turning into a tourist trap. They've put in tiny bridges, ramps and sidewalks to make it easy for anyone to get around in the more popular places to stop. Which you can take as a negative or positive, I'll let you decide.
I did some dispersed camping, just make sure you're out of site from the main roads and half mile from trails. Bring lots of water!

name: Jasen Kwasniewski
text: Great vacation spot, you will never run out of stuff to do here

name: Jenifer McIntosh
text: Stunning!  Wildlife amazing!  A must see ✌

name: exer cise
text: Wide open spaces, nature at it's best! Bison,long horn sheep, antelope and prairie dogs...yep they are there!

name: Shawn Uyeda
text: Photos of the Badlands are awesome.... but actually being here and seeing it with your own eyes is truly amazing, especially in the morning. Luckily all the wildlife were cooperating the day we visited and were out and about.

name: Kathryn Tuggle
text: NOTE: Do NOT take Sage Creek Road in an effort to see more of the park than 240 will allow unless you have a big truck and four wheel drive. Sage Creek is NOT paved and is very rough! Taking 240 will allow you to see all the scenic parts of the Badlands on a nice smooth road! Overall this gorgeous park was both more and less than I was expecting... less green (Not many trees at all) and more beautiful rock formations and sweeping views of the landscape. Driving through on 240 and stopping regularly takes about three hours. There are scenic pull-offs about every 20-30 minutes and bathrooms about every 45 minutes. Take your own water and I’d recommend taking your own toilet paper as the bathrooms weren’t always stocked! Also be on the lookout for bison, deer, and great horned sheep!

name: Kelli M
text: Beautiful park. The shorter trails were quite full but we enjoyed it anyways and loved driving the loop. Would love to spend more time here. It was very clean with ample parking.

name: Michael Ballash
text: The landscapes are fantastic and the wildlife is abundant.

name: Lynn N.
text: Love love love. Will be back.

name: Mike C
text: Loved the hiking here.

name: Beau Cox
text: Awesome. Another one of Our Creator's beautiful works. God Bless America !!

name: David Clark
text: Very hot and dry in summer months so bring plenty of water. Signage could be better as you're left wondering if you're looking at the correct thing. Such as the "door and window" or "castle" sites. Based on that I'd recommend buying a book about the Badlands from the visitors center. This national park is amazing and is highly recommended. Plan for a half day or preferably more.

name: Nicole P
text: So cool and you just have to drive through it in real life-pictures do not do it justice. We went on a cool March day and saw hundreds of prairie dogs, sheep, buffalo, ect. Not too many cars/people so never felt rushed or held up at the many lookouts. If you do the whole loop-half is dirt road, half is paved. Fun!

name: Shane Brons
text: Amazing scenery and great hiking!

name: Jason Semans
text: Beautiful to see. Take time to stop and look. Don't rush.

name: Heather B
text: This is the most beautiful place on earth!! Great adventure!

name: Dennis Fuerst
text: Badlands...extremely scenic and surreal!

name: H B
text: Love this place. Make sure you have good shoes and plenty of water if you plan on hiking trails.

name: Matt Armstead
text: An amazing change in scenery at the West end of South Dakota

name: Wendi
text: Beautiful place, visitor center was closed. Nice fun drive to view the beautiful  area.

name: Brian Impson
text: Breathtaking vistas.

name: Chris Ruda
text: Just amazing landscape and it is great that you can walk around and see so much.

name: David Hallenberger
text: Great scenery saw some bighorn sheep some bison and prairie dogs

name: Jeff Kaser
text: Your time and have a nice leisurely drive to the Badlands. Take some back roads and see different views. Stop at the visitor center and enjoy some local food. Shop at the store for authentic made jewelry by the locals

name: Rimpi Singh
text: Perfect for a day trip.

name: heath price
text: Awesome views. There are many paths and trails to follow. Just bring a good map and gps so you dont get lost

name: lonnie Richie
text: Hertz according to what you like, if you like open free places you won't find any more open for free....

name: Crystal Wolfe
text: Beautiful in person! Pics do no justice! A must see!

name: Jonathan Byrd
text: Had a wonderful visit.  Be sure to take route 44 on way to rapid city when done with th badlands.  The scenery is great.

name: Thomas Crawford
text: This place is Awesome. Can't take enough pictures.

name: Sean Romanjenko
text: Very hot but oddly beautiful

name: S S
text: Awesome park!

name: Kenny Richard
text: Incredible place to visit with extraordinary views and beautiful scenery. I viewed several mountain sheep at the first pull off after entering the wall exit. There are numerous designated pull off areas with grand views, and several had walking paths to allow visitors to search the area on foot. There I'd diverse landscaping and fascinating Rock formations. Some of the roads can be very windy and precarious so use caution and drive slow. A must see place to visit when in South Dakota.

name: Joseph Cook
text: Good place to see.

name: Sadat K
text:
Mini Grand-canyon! There are about 12 lookouts.  1st  , 2nd and 3rd , close to visitor center, being top picks. I saw all 12 as didn’t wanted to miss anything. Spring is best time as summer could get very hot. If you are driving from MN and going to SD enter via ‘Ben Reifel visitor center’ and do the 240 loop. And if traveling from SD to MN do the other way around. There are walking trails, few fossil hunt trails, though I didn’t see much of fossil, but walk is not bad. Some trails are can go from easy to expert level. Please be cautious around small plants and holes as this place is known to  have rattle snake.

If you are not up for hiking, the park is easy to drive through, and takes roughly 30 - 45 minutes to drive through with no stopping.  Lots of look out points, and places to park and watch the wild life.  Wildlife includes Bison, Ferrets, Deer, Prong Horn, Big Horn Sheep, Prairie Dogs (they have plague, stay away from them), and other things I am surely missing.  Over all, it's a cool place to visit with unique landscapes.  Problem is, it is in the middle of nowhere, with very little infrastructure supporting it, making it a very "out-of-the-way" stop for a lot of visitors.  Bring enough food and water for your group, and enjoy the hiking and scenery.

Never walk to the edge of a Butte, it may give away under you.  There is so much history concerning this national park. You can see fossils, antelope, bison, prairie dogs, Jack rabbits, mule deer, wild sheep. But, remember, "never walk close to this animal,,!"  They may seem tame and friendly, not. They are born and raised in the Badlands National Park and do their own thing. Stay back, take pictures, read all signs and be safe. We welcome all visitors to the park. There is a visitors center with much information. Concerning how the Badlands  came to be.  My thoughts as well as my older sister who was here visiting from the East coast believe and feel much spirituality from this land.
So, if you're planning a trip to Badlands National Park, read everything you can find about their formation, what, how when, what else was here???? Very exciting info and vacation of learning, fun and leisure.

text:
This place is breathtaking. It's very well kept. I didn't see much trash and all the viewpoints we stopped at were very well maintained.

We went on 5 of the trails. The Fossil Exhibit Trail really wasn't much of a trail, but it was pretty neat seeing fossils of creatures in the area. The Saddle Pass Trail made me pretty nervous with my 3 kids (10, 8, & 5 y/o), but they made it pretty well and the view was definitely worth it. I did have a close encounter with a rattlesnake. I didn't get bit, but be super careful because they are really out there. We also found a couple of fossils on the trail! We took pics and reported them, but the big one had already been reported. The Cliff Shelf Nature Trail wasn't as impressive, but it was a very easy trail that had board walks and stairs for a good chunk of it. The Window Trail was super short, but the view was great. I think my favorite was the Door Trail. It was a rugged hike, but wasn't bad at all. You're surrounded in the majesty of the Badlands. I also wasn't constantly worried one of my kids were going to fall off a cliff. That's always a bonus.

The visitor center was nice, but way too crowded. We got to see how they process fossils and saw pictures on the wall of people who found fossils. Unfortunately we won't be on it...

The Badlands are a definite must see if you're in the Rapid City area. The beauty and mystery are too great to pass up.

name: Clark Zealand
text: Badlands National Park is a beautifully rugged place to visit and simply take in all that is offered in a location like nowhere else on the planet. As soon as you enter the park, you get an immediate sense of why this place is called the Badlands! While some interpretation brings it to life, I can’t imagine what natives and Europeans really had to do when attempting to travel through this landscape. And since the landscape is affected so dramatically by rain, it’s changing all the time; it’s just too bad that the average tourist doesn’t respect this and stay on durable surfaces built for them. It was amazing to see how many tourists just think they can walk anywhere, even with all the signage asking people not to. The views from all the parking areas in the main driving loop are worth stopping to enjoy as well as the few, short hiking trails. The Visitor Center has a lot of impressive interpretive displays and is always well worth your time. At one of the last vista, we even go to see several of bighorn sheep traversing the steep Cliffside. Overall, this is a great place and I strongly recommend taking the time to visit!

If you love marveling at the wonders of nature, this is a park you're going to truly enjoy. Distant views showcasing the power of mother nature are pretty much available throughout the park and in every direction. There are many places to pull over along the route to stop, take photos, take it all in, or simply to rest.

There are quite a few spots where you can climb some of the formations as well. We were able to spot a good amount of wildlife during our trip. A few things I wish we would have brought along would have been binoculars, extra water (it was August), and a few snacks. You can easily lose track of time here and end up spending several hours. name: Hannah Brown
text:
Badlands National Park is like a mix of Bryce Canyon and portions of northwest Wyoming (in and around Dubois). The erosion both past and continuing has created some breathtaking views and the juxtaposition of colorful hills with rolling prairies is stunning.

We drove through during a severe thunderstorm so photo and hiking opportunities were severely curtailed. However, numerous trails and pullouts abound and one could easily spend the better portion of a day exploring the beauties of Badlands National Park. Look out for Bighorn Sheep scampering up the cliffs!

text:
South Dakota has a wide variety of scenery to offer - the vast majority of the state is covered in beautiful sweeping plains.  The Black Hills are a mountainous contrast to these areas, but the Badlands of South Dakota are an entirely different world of their own.  Compared to the rest of the state, it provides views you would be hard pressed to find outside of perhaps Arizona.  The green rolling plains transform into an almost desert like series of tremendous valleys that would be easy to get lost in!  Very majestic, such wow - worth visiting for anyone traveling through the area.

Afterwards you can recharge at Wall Drug :)

text:
There are lots of places in the United States that can be described as Badlands or Mal Pais. The reasons vary. For Badlands Nat'l Park, the reason is erosion of the high plains of western South Dakota. The "loop road" off of I-90 is the most visited portion. The NPS Visitor Center is located along the loop road. Just outside the park boundary at the southern most portion of the loop road is the very small town of Interior. Interior is worth a quick stop.The eroded landscape of the Park reveals  layers of deposited sediment colored by differing mineral content. The pastel strata are best viewed in the early morning or late afternoon to really appreciate the coloration. Before the area was a national park, wagon loads of fossil large mammal bones were carried out of the area for sale to collectors.
The town of Wall, SD lies at one end of the loop road at its intersection with I-90. Wall is the home of one of the nation's most beloved and enduring tourist traps, Wall Drug,  a must see.

Our family loved the stay here.  We camped at Cedar Pass for two nights. Highlights were the junior ranger program, star gazing with a ranger (fri and sat only), plus hiking the notch and door trails.

For those on a tight schedule, at least visit one or two hikes.  Stop at the pinnacles and yellow mounds over look.  Dont forget the Ben Reifel visitor center either.

If you are camping out west, plan one night in cedar pass.  They have pull through sites, no camp fires but electrcity. It is awesome at night

name: Kasper Bosscher
text:
(Translated by Google) Fantastically beautiful park. Belongs to the list: yellowstone, grand canyon, yosemite and glacier national park.
Well worth it.
Can be combined with mount rushmore and yellowstone.
Located about an hour and a half drive from Mount Rushmore.
You can do the whole park by car, but there are also a few "trails" for a walk.

Ligt op ongeveer anderhalf uur rijden van mount rushmore.

name: Robert Mueller
text:
(Translated by Google) A little off the beaten track, but if you visit Mount Rushmore you should definitely go to this national park, it is only a few miles ... Here you will find a completely different landscape that is simply breathtaking. At $ 20, the entrance fee is quite high compared to other national parks.

(Original)

Hier bietet sich eine komplett andere Landschaft, die einfach atemberaubend ist. Der Eintrittspreis ist mit 20 Dollar im Vergleich zu anderen Nationalparks recht hoch.

name: Ben Beerents
text:
(Translated by Google) One of the many national parks in the US. And what for 1. Well worth a visit.

We drove the route from Wall (first visit Wounded Knee Museum!). We first drove through the park and then back via the national road. Lots of beautiful views. And as usual in an American National Park: excellent parking.

(Original)
Een van de vele nationale parken in de US. En wat voor 1. Een bezoek meer dan waard.

Wij reden de route vanuit Wall (eerst Wounded Knee Museum bezoeken!). We reden eerst door het park en daarna via de rijksweg terug. Veel mooie uitzichten. En zoal gebruikelijk in een Amerikaans National Park: prima parkeergelegenheid.

name: Andrea Credaro
text:
(Translated by Google) Beautiful park famous for its "banded" mountains. In fact, erosion and a particular geological conformation make the soil composed of different minerals capable of giving different coloring which is highlighted on the mountains and hills carved by erosion. Near the park there are few accommodation facilities, so book in advance to find a comfortable solution for sleeping nearby. Inside you will find various trails of various lengths, to better enjoy the park I recommend making someone.

(Original)
Bellissimo parco famoso per le sue montagne a "fasce". Infatti l'erosione e una particolare conformazione geologica fanno si che il terreno sia composto da diversi minerali in grado di dare colorazione differente che viene evidenziata sulle montagne e colline scavate dall'erosione. Nelle vicinanze del parco ci sono poche strutture ricettive, prenotate quindi in anticipo per trovare una soluzione comoda per dormire nelle vicinanze. All'interno troverete vari trail di varie lunghezze, per gustarvi meglio il parco consiglio di farne qualcuno.

name: Elenka
text:

Interesting points with hiking trails are located near Ben Reifel Visitor Center in the south-east of the park. Nice to hike in the evening: there the sun is already lower, is not too hot and it blows strong but warm wind (the review refers to the end of July)

Schöne u.a. kurze (bis 1 km= ca. 20-30  Minuten) Wanderwege, atemberaubende Aussichtspunkte. Nordwestlicher gibt es eher höhere Berge, in der Mitte mehr Grasland. Interessante Punkte mit Wanderwegen befinden sich nähe Ben Reifel Visitor Center im Süd-Osten vom Park. Schön ist es gegen Abend zu wandern: da steht die Sonne schon tiefer, ist nicht allzu heiß und es weht starker aber warmer Wind (die Rezension bezieht sich auf Ende Juli)

name: Rejean Beauchamp
text:
(Translated by Google) An indescribable inevitable.

We crossed this park quickly first motorcycle in the afternoon of July 24, 2017 from the village of Interior and have done it again in the opposite direction the next morning but taking our time this time to to enjoy to the maximum of this unavoidable unspeakable wonder. There are no words to describe our mutual enchantment. The heat was too intense in the afternoon of the 24th and we had just traveled a long distance on a motorcycle. We paid $ 10.00 for a 7 day pass. The cost was $ 20.00 for automobiles. We took a motel to Wall to visit the Badlands and Rushmore the next day. We stopped at several places offering breathtaking panoramic views. We took several pictures that we offer here with our opinion. It would be a sin on your part if you decide not to visit this wonder especially if you are nearby. We strongly recommend to linger on this magical site.

Reviewed October 29, 2017 Salaberry de Valleyfield, Quebec, Canada.
___________________________________________________________

We went back on a motorcycle on August 31, 2019 and enjoyed this park as much as in 2017. We would like to share again some pictures that we took.

Reviewed December 5, 2019 in Salaberry de Valleyfield, Quebec, Canada.

(Original)
Un incontournable indicible.

Nous avons traversé ce parc rapidement une première fois en moto dans l’après-midi du 24 juillet 2017 à partir du village d’Interior et l’avons à nouveau fait dans le sens contraire le lendemain matin mais en prenant notre temps cette fois pour jouir au maximum de cette incontournable merveille indicible.  Il n’y a pas de mots pour décrire notre enchantement mutuel.  La chaleur était trop intense dans l’après-midi du 24 et nous venions de parcourir une longue distance en moto.  Nous avons payé $10.00 pour une passe de 7 jours.   Le coût était de $20.00 pour les automobiles.  Nous avons pris un motel à Wall pour visiter les Badlands et Rushmore le lendemain.  Nous nous sommes arrêtés à plusieurs endroits offrant des vues panoramiques à couper le souffle.  Nous avons pris plusieurs photos que nous vous proposons ici avec notre avis.  Ce serait un péché de votre part si vous décidiez de ne pas visiter cette merveille surtout si vous êtes à proximité.  Nous recommandons très fortement de vous attarder sur ce site féerique.

Avis écrit le 29 octobre 2017 à Salaberry de Valleyfield, Québec, Canada.
___________________________________________________________

Nous y sommes retournés en moto le 31 août 2019 et avons apprécié ce parc tout autant qu'en 2017.  Nous aimerions à nouveau vous partager quelques photos que nous avons prises.

Avis écrit le 5 décembre 2019 à Salaberry de Valleyfield, Québec, Canada.

name: TW U
text: Very neat 1880s town. Examples of buildings that are period specific. Build g materials are accurate.  Out front is a gas station and convenient store for the highway travelers.  Midway is an old round  barn with gift shop and museum which also serves as the entrance to the town. Beside the round barn is a small restaurant in an old train with a kitchen car, dining cars and luggage cars. Very cool.

text: Nice little recreation of the old west. Not too fancy but fun.

text: It's a total tourist trap. $12 a person. I was expecting an actual town with shops and people dressed like the 1880s. It's more of a museum. There were only two people at the saloon dressed up. Some buildings were not even open, just a little view inside. There wasn't a person in the gift shop for us to buy our souvineers, and when she did show up, another co-worker needed her. Didn't even acknowledge us. So we left our stuff on the counter and left. Maybe just enjoy the photos and say you were there.

text: As a huge Dances With Wolves fan, this place did not disappoint. Here you will find really cool movie props and behind the scenes info. The main attraction is the 1880s town (hense the name). There were some pretty cool antiques and interesting buildings to explore. The only negative was that the gentleman doing the wagon rides was telling jokes that were inappropriate for the children. Other than that, this is a fun stop along your journey's way.

text: We needed to stretch ours legs and let the kids run around after being in the car for 8 hours plus. We saw all the bill boards and decided why not. It was a great break during our road trip. It was neat to go through all the old buildings and read about their history.

text: Love this small town little place. Brings me back to old western days I grew up reading about. Neat little diner in an old train offers great food options in the middle of nowhere! Stopped twice within a week, and we will definitely be stopping again!

text: Good prices really cool experience way better then we thought it would

name: Denise
text: If you're a fan of history, this is a great stop for you.  If you're not a fan of history, but your travelling companions are, it's still a neat place to stop.  I fall into the latter category.  While I didn't love this place, it was still pretty cool to see the old buildings and stuff that was used back in the day.  It's set up sort of like a mini town and you can walk into the buildings and see the different tools and instruments and vehicles that were used so many years ago.  There's a cool saloon you can visit too where you can pick a costume to walk around in and really live the experience.  You can also get some small snacks and cold bottled beverages there as well.  For a small fee you can take a wagon ride, pulled by some donkeys as well.  The gift shop is nice, and the display from the Dances with Wolves movie is cool too. It's worth at least visiting once.

name: Kasper Bosscher
text:
Nice stop on the route if doing a routetrip.
Not really worth the drive if you're not passing by.
But if you're driving over the 90 freeway and need a reststop, this is the place to stop.
Fill up with gas, go to the restrooms and go for the 1880 town tour.
There is also a gift shop in the gasstation.
All in all the best reststop on freeway 90.

name: Wendy Burk
text: Neat place but expensive to visit. Very tourist oriented. 12.00 a person in August 2016. Worth stopping by even if you do not go in. Has a neat train diner and gift shop.

name: Thomas Hull
text: neat road side stop  very interesting historical property

name: Tonie Garcia
text: Like traveling back in time. An absolute must if you are traveling through. $12 dollars an adult, a little less for kids but completely worth it. I would eat before hand but there is enough treats to get you through if you don't. There is so much to take in and explore so plan to be there a while. Truly an unique experience.

name: Shawn Schweigert
text: Very interesting! I loved all the old saddles and spurs.  It's great to see the American cowboy lifestyle preserved. I will be back!

name: Gran Jaguar

name: Wade Christiansen
text: Nice little attraction. Buildings and railroad set up as it was in the 1880's. I really enjoyed the Dances with Wolves exhibit upstairs.

name: jasenko mandura
text: Nice

name: Charlie Dango
text: Nice place to stop and streach your legs and see how people lived in frontier times. Lots of good photo ops and a family friendly saloon to get a cold drink.

name: Chris Gibbons
text: Stopped at 1880 Town on a whim as we were driving to Rapid City. It is neat to see some of the memorabilia and old structures. We had fun walking around seeing how things would have been in the late 1800s. The Dances with Wolves memorabilia is neat as well. Not sure if it is worth $12/person though. Made a good first stop for our vacation.

name: Tim Canaday
text:
Didn’t bother with the town.  Couldn’t get past the awful diner food. Three of my family had the cheeseburgers and one had a grilled cheese.  The grilled cheese was good, but the burgers were not tasty.  Fairly run-of-the-mill type taste.  They looked cooked, and were cooked correctly, but somehow didn’t taste cooked.  And how in the world can you mess up chips?  The potato chips were bad as well.   We each tried a different flavor, and even my daughter, who loves chips, didn’t like any of them.

In the end, it’s a quaint place.  And if you like trains or are fascinated with their history, then come for that.  But, skip the meal.

name: Shaun Simmons
text: Kind of expensive for a large family! The restaurant was closed early and there was a  lot to see, with out any kind of guidance. Would not do it again. Not really worth it unless that is your thing.

not all the buildings are decorated/named for what they originally were..

go..pay the admission and help pay to keep them cared for.
maybe a few more generations will be able to see this stuff before it only exists in pictures.

name: Z BRN
text: If you want to feel like you are traveling back in time and having a chance to see how life was in 1880, this is perfect theatrical place to experience that. They have a historical post office, stores, church, bar, houses with old traditional items. Really fascinating place to be!

text:
A great experience to see what a pioneer village used to be like. I took a star away because after the first few buildings, it became redundant. They could move the buildings closer, or have something to offer besides the structure itself.

It is a nice stop with some time to stretch and something to see in a very convenient way when you are on a road trip.

text: I wasnt able to make it inside cuz we locked out keys in our car and by the time we got them out they were closed but he was very helpful and sweet. And even if we didnt get to go inside the service/interaction was amazing.

text: Nice clean place, I love old west history, so I enjoyed this place.  My kids ages 11 and 13 were bored though.

name: David Newman
text:
If you have ever seen the movie " Dances with Wolves" you will enjoy your trip to the 1880 Town. The main museum is full of movie props including the real Buck ridden by Kevin Costner. Although Buck has passed away. You can still find him stuffed and on display.
The Saloon is still "active" with Live music and drinks like soda and water are available for purchase.

name: Journee Ramsey
text: The gas station had my favorite drink which isn't very common. Otherwise attractions were fun for the entire family

name: Jessika Rice
text: I really have mixed feelings about this place. They have a lot of cool artifacts from history and props from a few movies. Also there are tons of building to walk through. The problem is most of the building are falling apart and not in a cute ghost town way but in the someone is going to get hurt and they are going to get sued way. I can see the potential in it and I'm love tourist traps but visitors beware and careful

name: Mariusz Zielezny
text: We saw many they signs along the route to Rapid City and decide to stop. Won't regret. For the first time I feel like traveling in time. This town is a replica on old west town. You feel like in wild wild west. With original bank, store, houses, sheriffs office, church, train station. Everything is original. I just loved that place.

name: Tannia Lovejoy
text: We arrived at 6:45 at it was closed even though it says online open until 8 when asked was told they close early during bike week. They should really advertise that online as we planned our drive home thinking we had plenty of time.

name: Donald Hoffman
text: A great place to visit and really worth the entry fee.

name: Free man
text: Nice little stop when travelling across S Dakota.

name: S. Wilson
text:
An impressive collection of historical buildings and furnishings is on display here. No matter what type of building you're interested in, they probably have it here. From churches to saloons  and hotels, to jails and doctor offices, it's here. Barns? Yes indeed. Don't forget to go upstairs in the main entrance building and check out the items from the movie "Dances with Wolves ".
After checking out the scenery, head over to the diner that's set up in railroad cars. We didn't because of time constraints, but next time for sure! There's plenty of parking available, and a large gas station on site can accommodate large camper trailers and RV's.

name: Deb Lorance

name: Diane Eldridge
text: Local authentic and historical buildings and the accoutrements arranged to let you step back in time. They keep adding to it and making it even more fun!  Love the Dances With Wolves props and even got to visit Cisco (Buck) when he was still alive!

The saloon is a pretty cool thing too, they have live entertainment put on several times daily and it is very fun and family friendly. The guy who headlines the show is Billy Wyatt and he is super talented and an extremely down to earth nice guy. Look him up on google to hear some of his stuff. You will not be sorry.

text: Yes, it is exactly what you expect. Roadside America at its finest. A full setup of a frontier town with equal parts interesting-ness and tourist trap. Lots of souvenirs to buy, but if you just want to see a fairly authentic-looking movie set, you've come to the right place. Hard to not give it a 5-star review: it's like giving someone's grandfather a bad review, you just kinda have to do it for the cuteness/classic-road-trip-stop factor.

name: Kyle V
text: Soggy, rotting, and barely maintained. When we visited, we looked at the dilapidated, largely abandoned buildings  in between broken glass and a small family of probably feral cats that had taken to living in the roped-off kitchen of one of the buildings. Constantly running fans were employed as substitute dehumidifiers in a few of the bigger buildings, though they probably wouldn't have done much for the mold growing in the ripped train seats. The only evidence someone had done maintenance here in decades was the VHS copy of "Dances With Wolves." Avoid unless you need to use the bathroom, because the owners do apparently.

name: Jesse Locklear
text: Easy check-in, nice level spots, and clean bathrooms. We stayed 2 nights and enjoyed how close it was to town and to the National Parks & Mt. Rushmore. They also had cabins and a dog exercise area. The showers need a little more water pressure but everything else was great!!

name: Laken Brock
text: A nice place to stay while you explore the black hills. See Mt. Rushmore, keystone, explore the black hills. Custer state park is only 45 minutes away! The campsite was secluded from the highway and there are many different options from dry camping, to full hookups including cable. There is a communal shower house/laundromat/dish washing station, as well as volleyball and horse shoe pits,  and two playgrounds for the kids. It's quite pricey (75-100/night) for a campsite, but hotels seem to run at least 200/night around here as well. Would recommend staying for 2-3 nights and then moving on to a less expensive area.

I guess all KOAs don't want you in the shower any longer than absolutely necessary (too small or too cold, either way, you're in and out).  The place was huge, and the map was locked in the truck, so I couldn't find the dog walk.  I found grass area next to the propane tank and promptly discovered I wasn't the only one that walked their dog there.  There were 'landmines' everywhere.  When I got my receipt, I discovered that I was charged a pet fee.  Hopefully they use the money to buy some signs, or mark out a second walk area, because no dog is going to walk THAT far outside and hold it.  But I highly suggest that they at least use some of that money to clean up after the dogs of owners that didn't.  Really, I paid a fee to walk my dog through other dogs piles.  EW!

name: Jeannine Szostak
text:
It was fascinating to go through here with my kids and hear them talk about “yeah, in the olden days, people had to...”, realizing that I lived through that era!! 😂😂. It was cool to see the photos of things I grew up surrounded by, that I didn’t realize were related.

I wasn’t aware that there were multiple sites to the place either, but I’m glad that we drove to the silo site as well. And, ironically, one of the magazines highlighted in the museum was from my hometown.

name: Ward Dougherty
text:
What a cool little museum.
This is not a massive structure. It is a small building located just off the interstate. There is pleny of parking. It is dedicated to the Minuteman missile facility that were located nearby. There is a small walk through museum that is very well done highlighting the arms race, why the silos were built and how they worked. It is a neat little museum that anyone and everyone should see to understand what the country went through during those times. There is also a small gift shop. If you are interested, they also have self guided tours of 2 of the delta facilities (missile facilities) nearby. A good historical stop if you are in the area

name: Shannon Tate
text: Absolutely astounding. As it says in it's description, this is the only US memorial dedicated to the Cold War. For those who grew up under the fear and uncertainty of a nuclear attack from overseas, this will being back memories. For those who have never experienced living in the Cold War era, there are lessons to be learned here. Highly recommend visiting the missile sites/ Delta sites.

name: Marc Crawford
text: Lots of cool history at this museum.  If you are not into history, there is not much to see here.

name: Mark Stevens
text: It’s definitely a National Park Service site to visit while you’re in the Badlands National Park area! The visitor center and information looks small, but there’s a lot of information about the missileers and America’s Cold War past. There’s plenty of parking and the NPS rangers and staff are always helpful to provide any information about this and other locations in the area.

name: Deborah Barron Brown
text: Yes the small visitor center is nice but I was really expecting to see a silo.

name: Jason Winget
text: Well down, a quick visit. Tours are not at this site. Short video explains the program.

name: Wendy Burk
text: Stop here on your way to the Badlands. It is at the same exit. Well worth it. A piece of US history we sometimes forget about. If you can get tickets for the control room tour it is well worth it. MUST be there about 8am as only 45 tickets a day given out and go fast. Museum is very interactive.

name: Nick Bell
text: Wow! I never realized how vast our country is in terms of defense. The de-commissioned Silo was eye opening. Today. Now with Supersonic weapons on the horizon these silos are obsolete but so much fun to visit.

name: larry cooper
text: This is a modest historic site allowing the public to get a chance to see what is normally a highly restricted military site

name: R Scott Weaver
text: Powerful and moving review of a terrifying part of our national history. Worth a stop off Interstate 90.

name: Sid C
text: The exhibits at the visitor center brought history to life!  The nuclear weapons history and how these nuclear capable rockets defended our nation during the most tense moments.  Incredible how close we came to nuclear war on several occasions.  The museum did an excellent job of presenting the information and well worth the time to walk through slowly.  The staff was very knowledgeable and had great stories to tell.

name: Jeff Meister
text: Arrived there late and missed the tours but the museum area was quite interesting even though it was not large. If you are passing through it's well worth the visit.

name: Tony C
text: Small but very interesting especially if you lived through the Cold War. Excellent informative movie.

name: David Clark
text: There are three sites for the Minuteman. My GPS did not lead me to the correct place with the address listed. The welcome center is located on the other side of the interstate from the entrance to the Badlands National Park. This welcome center features a very interesting and informative museum which is a must see and is free. The actual missile is a 15 minute drive from the welcome center and is also free. If you want to see the control center that is on a third site and requires tickets you will need to purchase at least 24 hours in advance, but should be purchased a month in advance because they sell out fast. If you have trouble finding the visitors center this address should get you close: 21280 SD-240, Phillip, SD 57567

The staff is where it shines. Ranger Jim was a great host and very knowledgeable (he had worked as a missilier for eleven years). Ranger Jim's first hand experience illuminated the visit, and his stories were fascinating. This visitor's center, and the command center, and the Delta-09 facility are must-see stops.

name: Zach Zingmark
text: We took the 1880 train in late September, round trip from Hill City. This is a very cool experience for adults and for kids. They have a great play area outside of the depot while kids wait for the train. It would be nice to offer food or hot beverages during the off season at the depot or even concessions on the train. Once on board, the seats are comfy, the narrator was great, and the ride was overall very enjoyable. I wish there was more time between the turnaround in Keystone. We barely had enough time to use the restrooms (with a line a mile long) and purchase a snack before leaving. Highly recommend for families with children.

resp.text: Thank you - glad you enjoyed the ride!  During most of the season there is opportunity to book a later return from Keystone and spend more time there before you return to Hill City.

resp.text: Thank you for taking the time to provide this feedback; we're glad that you enjoyed the overall ride! We do have options in the regular season to have the quick 15 minute layover, or the option for multiple hours to walk around either town. I also apologize there was a disturbance in the beginning of your ride. We are a family-friendly destination and sometimes those disturbances do happen. Throughout the season we do have special events with adults only cars, that are 21+ and we serve alcohol throughout! We try to have something for everyone so we hope to see you again in the future!

resp.text: Thanks for your review - glad to have you aboard!!

name: Sarah Trader
text:
The 1880 train was recommended to us by a friend so we gave it a shot. I was a bit disappointed. You essentially ride on the train from Keystone to Hill City and back (if you buy a round trip ticket). The trip is an hour each way, which a layover in between. The train cars are not air-conditioned and we rode it on a hot day, which made it uncomfortable. The view is nice and we did see several deer and pronghorn, which was cool. There is a guide who shares some local info too. The food at the Hill City depot was very good and cheap!

If you're looking for something low key, that allows you to sit for several hours, or if your kids are wanting to ride their first train, it would be good. For us, it wasn't worth the $100+ we paid for 4 people, and the almost 3 hours it took out of our day.

resp.text: We are sorry that you did not fully enjoy our vintage steam railroad.  You are correct that our historically restored, early 1900s passenger cars are not air conditioned, however all of the windows can be opened and closed by the passengers.  We also offer open-sided passenger cars which offer the most airflow through them and are protected with a roof.

The train conductor even took time to visit with my son and take some pictures. Then this year for the first time we rode the Christmas train! It has been on my bucket list for awhile and did not disappoint one bit! It was over the top amazing too! I hope to some day try the adult drinking Christmas train ride too!
