name: Karin Wells
text: IMO the place is pretty overrated.  The hype starts from signs hundreds of miles away, so I kind of expected more.  Maybe I just built it up too much in my head, but it just seemed like an oversized gift shop.  We were going to get lunch, but the lines were long and slow and not everything was open, on a Friday afternoon.  If you're in the area and have some time to kill or just want to take a break from the long drive across SD its probably worth it, but I wouldn't recommend going out of my way.

name: Dee Hanson
text: Employee had to come from a different retail area of store. Clerk was very polite. Dusty displays.

name: Jesse Locklear
text: Fun place to stop, shop, rest, snack, and use the restroom. Honestly you could stay all day!!! Awesome jewelry and boot shopping!! Fresh donuts made on site and free ice water! Lots of parking for cars, rv's, and busses:)

name: Chad K
text:
Proof that billboards work! So long as you have 150 of them along I-90 from Sioux Falls to Wall. lol

Things here start closing up around 4:30 PM (despite signs that they close at 5 or 5:30). So, be here before then. The outdoor area is seasonal, so if you're here in late autumn, winter, or early spring then it may not be open.

It's basically a big store that sells corny Old West and Native American themed souvenirs to tourists.  Stop once to say you've been and to realize why you probably never need to stop here again. Get your "Where the heck is Wall Drug?" bumper sticker and a smashed/pressed/rolled penny. Take a photo sitting on the giant Jackalope.

name: Marc Crawford
text: A cool spot to stop by after driving through the Badlands.  The food is just ok.  Lots of tourist things to buy.  Worth the stop to look around.

name: Marie Rokusek
text: I really enjoy going to Wall Drug-souvenirs galore! Being your wallet because you will buy lots...t-shirts, hats, toys, salt water taffy, fudge, etc. There is fun to be had for all ages! They have a huge roaring dinosaur, a fun splash pad, and great food! Make sure you get either a chocolate or maple frosted doughnut and that free ice water!!! Wall Drug is a great place to stop on the way to the Black Hills!

name: Nate Chatigny
text: Certainly a spectacle on its own right. Worth stopping in, whether you’re headed there as a destination, or just passing through!

name: Ольга Демидова
text: All those billboards on the road make you expect something special. It’s more like an ordinary tourist attraction full of different staff. Its Wild West theme is quite interesting. It’s the only place to eat in the area but it definitely is overestimated.

name: Joy B
text: Best place to stop on your road trip.

name: Liz JA
text: Yes, it is a tourist trap. We still had to stop. Spent way too much on souvenirs, but hey, good place to get gifts to give people. Prices are rather high, but I think that depends on what area of the country you are from. The food was good and I loved the idea of 5 cent coffee! The coffee was good. Coming during covid the 6 foot rabbit was put away with only the jackalope out. I love reading the history of how they got started. Would I stop again...sure I would.

name: Connor Carlbom
text: A required stop for the kitsch factor alone. Be sure to check out all the western art in the cafe and the dinosaur in the backyard. Also don't leave without picking up a couple of donuts!

name: The Fun Stuff
text: It's an awesome store,and after visiting Badlands this store is like an oasis.Good food is there. But coffee is a machine coffee.

name: Celeste Ruppelt
text:
It had been many years since we were last at Wall Drug. It has grown and probably now would take an entire day to see it all. It is still fun and unique to it's purpose. Worth stopping for whether one is on the way to the Black Hills or coming from them. We came for dinner on a rainy evening.
Had Buffalo Burgers that came with a big stack of onion rings. Everything is served hot and fresh. We also had a piece of apple pie ala mode to share. It was excellent but at $6.29, one piece was plenty.
Wall Drug closes at nine, so we didn't have much time to walk around.
There is street parking, which is free, and there is plenty, but it can still get crowded.
Budget what you shall buy, there are many choices.
Be sure to visit the Back Yard. Lots of fun photo ops there. Unfortunately, it was closed by darkness and rain when we hoped to check it out.

name: Deb Knarr
text: Reminded me of Oatman and Williams a little...fun stop. Lots of shops and cafe. Really have 5 cent coffee! Spent a couple hours here... plenty of parking for big rigs.

name: Jeff
text:
Listen, after something like a thousand signs along the road… I don’t know what to expect. And after seeing it, I’m still not sure.

Given that there is a global pandemic, just except that there is no social distancing or attempts at stopping the spread of it. Know that going in. Embrace it if you want, but accept it.

I almost bought a $1200 buffalo pelt… But my wife would’ve killed me.

I waited 12 minutes to see the tyrannosaurus eat some thing, and while it was admittedly pretty cool how it roared and moved and gnashed it’s teeth… It didn’t actually eat anything, or anyone, or even appear to. So I’m a little sad about that.

But you’re in for a treat with the deluxe bathrooms. Way better than regular bathrooms. These are deluxe bathrooms. Be ready. Come ready to go, and you will not be disappointed.

Check out the Wikipedia article before you arrive to get a sense of what you’re in for. Be sure to pay attention to the see also section that mentions Uranus, Missouri which is in many ways a sister to this place. Maybe you want to swing by there too! I don’t think it’s too far away. I mean you made it this far, right?

name: Tina Olszewski
text:
Great place to stop. Lots of fun things to see and do. Many shops with everything you can imagine.

The restaurant was nice and the food was good. They also have a bakery, ice cream shop, candy  and more.

Kids will really enjoy Wall Drug. There are lots of photo opportunities so take your camera.

Some e parts of the attractions are outside so dress appropriately.

name: Wandern Leo
text: Is it a tourist trap? Is it worth the visit? YES!!! Absolutely. Didn’t know about this place in advance, but we’ve been seeing the advertisements along I-90 for at least 100 miles in advance so we decided to stop there. The place is worth a trip in itself. Pretty sure there is nothing you wouldn’t be able to bug there. Very entertaining.

name: Matthew Rokusek
text: It is a tourist trap, but that's not necessarily a bad thing. It is neat to look around.

name: Zach Zingmark
text: Wall Drug is your typical tourist trap, but it is worth a stop. We took our two young kids and there were plenty of things for them to see and do. There are several great opportunities for photos, places to eat, and don't forget to visit the animated dinosaur in the backyard. It may be cliche, but its worth a stop on your way to or from Rapid.

name: Laurel Carlson
text: Great place!  Great breakfast!

name: michael sharp
text: There was proper social distancing and all of the employees and most visitors were wearing masks.  I had a chocolate doughnut which was good.  Things are slightly overpriced but not terrible.  All the money helps the city of Wall South Dakota including the high school which is very nice from the outside especially the football field and stadium.  There's more tourists the=an locals that are in Wall on any given day.

name: Chris Spencer
text: Mostly just a tourist trap. If you want shopping they pretty much have everything.  It is fun to just browse around and look at everything.  I got bored pretty fast though.

name: Adriana Middleton
text: The “Homemade” ice cream did NOT taste homemade. The 5¢ coffee was excellent, there wasn’t a lot of room to move around and the restrooms were hard to find. There was not a lot of social distancing going on. It was so crowded we couldn’t get a picture with the saloon girls.

name: Marci Glines
text: Fun place to stop on the way to the Black Hills! Lots to see and do. Bathrooms could be alittle cleaner but other than that great place to visit!

name: Nyor Mirror
text:
My son and I stopped here after touring the badlands like thousands of other tourists do.

Pros: We got our free water and some neat souvenirs.

Cons: the handmade ice cream and milkshakes they bragged about for miles on billboards was closed. The original drug store that peeked my interest was closed (limited hours M-F 8:30-5). The cafe had a huge line calling out orders. No social distancing being practiced.

It’s pretty much a large Spencer’s with a chapel in it. Cool to get something to say you were there no real reason to go back.

name: Dave B
text: An iconic place to stop in South Dakota. The fresh made donuts in the cafe are a must. It’s kind of a maze getting through all the shops so don’t lose your kids. The main hallway with all the wooden statues and animal heads are a great place for everyone to take in all the craziness.

name: D Cooper
text: Good enough spot to grab a souvenir t-shirt or other trinket. Social distancing and mask use was minimal.

name: Jeff Meister
text: What can you say about Wall Drug that hasn't been said before... it's wacky fun!! Had lunch there and found that it was very good, my wife loved the home made pie. There is a lot to take in, stay awhile and roam the premises. Visit the back, find the Jackalope and take a ride and don't forget the bumper sticker and free ice water!

name: Krista Beerman
text: Good nostalgia. The cafe is expensive for what you get. I totally appreciated the history that is honored throughout.

name: Ryan Tellberg
text: Wall drug certainly is a staple of south Dakota and is worth a stop if you are passing through. It certainly gives off the old west vibe there are plenty of places to go shopping and lots of restraunts and also neat things for kids to do.

name: Lower48 Traveling
text: Passed by many times so finally got a chance to stop in...it’s okay place glad we stopped

name: Jeff Winn
text:
Fun store and area with something for everyone and good food.
The hype built up by the dozens of billboards along the highway made the whole experience hilarious yet very worth it.

name: M Rennie
text: What else ya gonna do crossing SD? Totally worth a stop for whatever you need or desire. Wall Drug.

name: Nadia P
text: This is an interesting place. Lots and lots of shopping opportunities from native American jewelry to Western apparel and everything in between. Tons of souvenirs. They also have a cafe, but the food was just ok.

name: Bill Baughman
text:
We enjoined seeing all of the signs as we drove across the state. It was a interesting rest stop on our road trip to Yellowstone from Dunbar PA.
There was a lot to see here. The food here looked very good but it was so busy and we didn't have the time to wait that long to eat.
But we did find several souvenirs to take home and we got our Free Ice Water.....
We'll stop again someday when we have more time  and look it over a lot better....

name: TW U
text: Everything you would expect from a tourist destination.  Cheap trinkets for a high price and expensive gifts for even higher prices. But well worth a visit as this place is definitely historic.

name: Hunter Tyler
text: Very unique and cool place with many sweet gift shops and restaurants. Definitely a must when visiting South Dakota.

name: Jim Petykowski
text: An American icon tourist stop on the way to the Black Hills or The Badlands.  There are hundreds of signs on the way thru South Dakota directing you to this place. They have everything you need including a full sized restaurant and tons of items for sale. They are famous for free water and homemade donuts.

name: Justin Reeg
text:
We were relatively excited to check this place out.  Frankly, just a bunch of overpriced tourist-trap souvenirs overall.  The bookstore was decent and had some good-looking books on sale.  There was NO SOCIAL DISTANCING at all.  Most people didn't wear masks and crowded around each other... "shocking" to see the COVID rates going up in this area since our visit a couple weeks ago.

Post-COVID, it's worth a stop, but only if you're in the area.

name: Sodak Girl
text: Tourist trap from hell , don't reccomened, also seems disrespectful to indigenous tribes

name: Deborah Causey
text: We had a blast!! There is so much to see and interact with. We aren't kids anymore, but we sure acted like it here. I even rode a jackalope!! Great prices on souvenirs and lots of photo opportunities. Great place for a rest from the car and to stretch your legs AND grab a bite to eat.

name: Jetlover X
text: You see signs over 50 miles before the place. We stopped there and it was not so special as we thought. But we all now: marketing works. Staff is ok. Stores approximately offer all the same stuff. It is more a tourist trap.

name: Tonya Gilbert
text: So many things to do.

name: Nathan Cadieux
text: Finally found Wall Drug. Lots of shops with cool touristy items and some very good food, doughnuts, and ice cream. The 5 cent coffee is good, and there is lots for kids to do in the summer.

name: Katie Bergh
text: THE BEST DONUTS. We stop every time we come through just for the donuts (get chocolate).

name: Loriahn Bass
text: What an amazingly fun stop! I had no idea it was tucked off I 90.  Loved exploring and checking out all the little shops and novelties

name: Dave Den Adel
text: Their donuts are to die for. I bet you can't just eat one !! I ate 3 in 1 sitting. But I have issues. And donuts fill the cracks of a broken heart. 💔💔💔🍩🍩🍩

name: Debra Reddy
text: Drove an hour and a half in the wrong direction to spend a few hours here. Worst decision ever. After shopping for a while for over-priced items that we didn't really need, we decided to sit down at a cafe to have a snack and drink. We ordered 2 slices of pepperoni pizza and were told there were 3 slices available. After we paid we sat down to wait. Then some employees came in and were given those 3 slices and we were told we had to wait 10 minutes for another pepperoni pizza to be made. Completely ridiculous. I will never waste my time here again.

name: D Shoogs
text:
Famous WALL DRUG STORE.
Food in the cafe was alright, it was way over priced bar food. Backyard was pretty cool.

name: David Cy
text: Quirky cool place to stop as you are driving from rapid city to sioux falls or vice versa. Neat historical photos as well as a touristy stop to grab a bite to eat. Must stop here if you are also going to the badlands.

name: Wade Christiansen
text:
If you're not from here, or South Dakota, then there is much to see. I had to come and see and that was enough. If you like wall to wall foreign stuff to spend your money on, then this is for you.
Please don't get me wrong. There is history in Wall Drug and some interesting things to capture your attention for a time, but for me, once is enough

name: Lynn N.
text: Loved loved loved. A must stop & see.

name: Lori Corn
text: A must stop if you are on I90 going by the town of Wall. Could have spent 2 hours in there looking at all the unique merchandise. Very friendly staff at each store we stopped at. Bought some great authentic leather belts at one store and buffalo jerky at another.

name: Victoria Nowlin
text: Big disappointment after all the hype.   Tourist trap

name: Kate Rogers Serenity Spa
text: We went on the off season and I had huge expectations...it had been 20 some years since I had been and it was definitely not what I remembered. Everyone we ran into that worked there was friendly and helpful. Very touristy attraction site with lots of construction and places closed.

name: ThatJacobPowell
text: Cool 1800’s themed shopping center. Must see stop in Wall.

name: Kristi Newcomb
text:
I love to shop! It's just fun looking for something different.  I found cool books and some really good lotion. But really believe the other reviews about the food.
Restaurants look dirty and the food is horrendous and way overpriced.

name: Cathy Hale
text: Interesting place to see! They have tons of merchandise, good photo opportunities, food, and it's not very expensive!

name: Liza Timmers
text: It’s a tourist trap but fun none the less. Lots of shops and food. Crazy amount of people stop here. It’s pretty much a must do at least once just to say you went, lol.

name: Joel Wallen
text: The donuts are really good, most other things are overpriced

name: Dart Mall
text: Wall Drug is a nice place to stop after a long drive across the great state of South Dakota. Free ice water and it's delicious fill up a jug before you leave! Food is delicious and the doughnuts(coffee is cheap too) are to die for made fresh all day. Plenty of things to look at and buy. Been visiting this place since I was a kid.

name: Laura DeSimone
text: It was much better years ago but still one of those must add places to your cross-country list if you are driving that route

name: Trinity
text: My family loved it!  It is so worth the stop. We saw plenty of signs along the way and we figured why not.  You can easily spend a day here and there is something for everyone.  Thank you for an unexpected and fun family experience we will never forget .

name: Joshua A
text: I've got to say that when you read signs for an attraction as much as 300+ miles away, your expectations climb, and well, I can't exactly say this place is much more than a glorified flea market with higher prices. Don't get me wrong, it IS interesting to walk around and check everything out and there ARE some quality, unique items available for purchase, but all in all I don't think I would ever return. It's kind of one of those things that you go do because you hear about it and once you've done it, you've DONE IT.

name: Tony C
text: Interesting back story but really not worth a stop unless you are in the neighborhood

name: Paul Nygren
text: Gotta see it once...thats enough

name: Stephen Smith
text: Cool store...or western town mall. Lots of cool old western artwork and photographs, souvenirs, etc. A bit of a tourist trap, as top be expected,  but a fun experience nonetheless.

name: Sabrina Bourg
text: Omg! This place was amazing!! much better than I expected!

name: Stephen CARLSON
text: Amazing fantastic place to go to

name: Mark Deavult
text: Wall Drug ... for you East Coast peeps, the “On The Border” of the Plains. It’s the Kardashian of the tourism world, famous only for being famous, which makes people visit to see it ... because it’s famous.

name: Jude Fernando
text: A good quick stop for a few photos. Definitely a tourist trap but worth the stop for some quick photos and quick food.

name: Kristin Castenschiold
text: Fun to stop by for breakfast and spend a while walking around. Food was good and very touristy!

name: Anon Trew
text: Good place to spend 2 to 3 hours.

name: Red Faux
text: Food is just not good here. The cake donuts are the only thing I would spend money on. How can you mess up a hot dog or burger? Low, low quality food and ingredients.

name: Nicholas Miller
text:
Always a stop for us to and from the Black Hills and it never gets old.  There is always something cool to find and purchase.  Food is really good and the Free Ice Water is always cold.

EDIT 08OCT2017 - Stopped in for a slice of apple pie on our way to the hills and its still amazing.

name: Free man
text: Someone recommended we not stop, but I'm glad we did.  Worth the time - lots to see.  Tourist trap maybe, but still a good time if seeing as much of this country is your goal.  Good place to stop and eat on a trip across S. Dakota.

name: Robert Lerner
text: Historic, lots of worthwhile items to purchase as well as souvenirs

name: Josh Maximovich
text: My family and I had a great time here! Take the time and get off the highway and drive over and see this place. There are so many stores inside this Wall Drug. It just keeps going and going and going. Pretty much anything you can think of buying on a trip you will find here. I'm giving it a five because everything we bought here was quality made!

name: A Layton
text: Adorable place to visit. From the food to the stores to the fun picture opportunities out back. Everything is fun.

name: Dustin Garness
text: We've been here countless times and it continues to be a fun place to take any guests we have visiting us. Honestly, the whole place is a big tourist trap, but it has lots of endearing character and quirks that keep it interesting. The food in the Cafe is over priced, especially since it's just normal diner food.

name: Madame LaBrie
text: Shoppers dream! Well worth a detour if you are looking for souvenirs

name: baljinder singh
text:
Lol - my kids were all hyped up and it was a conversation laughter piece with all the signs leading to it from Sioux Falls. So we had to stop by here when we got the chance.
It’s a nice little rest stop with little shops built inside the market. The 5c coffee is pretty good quality.
Prices seemed fair and lot of of eating options available within. Expect to spend around 45 mins even if stopping here for a rest break.

name: David Smith
text: Typical tourist trap.  Cheap nik-naks and t-shirts.  Worth the stop if you have time to kill but would not go out of my way.

name: Amanda
text: This is an American Classic and a must-stop on the drive to Rapid City! The atmosphere is fun and family oriented! I journied here with my family as a small child and now 35 years later am bringing my own family. Shopping is great. Prices rock and people are friendly! Get some pie and 5 cent coffee!

name: Chris Gibbons
text: Not worth the hype in my opinion. We never tried the food so I cant comment on that but it is basically an overgrown gift shop design to trap tourists. Definitely would not go back.

name: Angel E
text: It was so much fun to show my children Wall Drug. Yes, cheesy souvenirs, but great memories to store away so they can bring their children someday. Wish we would have eaten at the cafe, it smelled great! Thanks Wall Drug for being open all year!

name: Scott Glenn
text: It's a great place to visit clean and warm and friendly people it's a lot to see

name: Erik Hicks
text: Trust all those billboards - this is definitely a place you must experience.  Well-stocked gift shops, plenty of great decor, really good food, and friendly people.  It's a fun unique place to go!

name: Abby Staggers
text: Love the home made ice cream!

name: Terry Hedgespeth
text: food was good

name: Noah Darnell
text: Definitely a must-stop for the classic-road-trip factor. However, it is an enormous tourist trap. So, just don't be surprised if that's what you take from it. That being said, it is a good place to stop on your way elsewhere. Great lunch options nearby.

name: Sid C
text:
A very large "tourist trap" but in a good way.  There are many type of stores or gift shops plus an ice cream parlor, restaurant.  It's gaudy but everything is clean, people friendly and your basics for restaurant.

This is a good diversion if you have a little time.

name: Thomas Walker
text: Great things to see and do in great food

name: boars den logging
text: Really cool place lots of great deals and lot great things to see!

name: Joan Wollschlager
text:
Fun place to shop with your family on vacation. Must see attraction an hour east of the Black Hills!
Multiple shops and restaurants.

name: Austin Howell
text: Most of the stores sell trinkets that you'd find on eBay. Nothing was really appealing. They literally sold some random gargoyle action figures/figurines in their memorabilia shop to give you an idea. Why? They have a huge roadsign game that falls way short in person.

name: Frank S
text: Very interesting place to visit lots of things for the kids to do

name: rolf baier
text: Tourist trap

name: Scott Olslund
text: Great tourist stop, especially for those just passing through. There are a lot of cool shops within Wall Drug and most of the people that work here are super friendly and nice. The cafe here to is excellent and their donuts are great!

name: kaybee dubya
text: You just cannot make the trip to mt. Rushmore on I-90 without a stop at the "historic" wall drug. If you worry about not being able to find it the road signs WILL make sure you don't miss it. This is a place you will remember and tell stories about. Fantastic place for just about any kind of souvenir you may want.

name: Brian Schwinderman
text: I take many trips to SD a year and can't help myself when I pass by, I just have to stop in!  I love this place.  Even better when it is tourist season.  It's fun to see all the families faces as they check it out for the first time.  It is a must see!

name: Jesse Ault
text: For all of the hype, it was a bit of a letdown. As far as tourist traps go, it's worth a visit. We didn't stop on our first trip to SD. There are so many more interesting things to see, but I didn't want to pass up the opportunity this time. If you have kids, prepare them by either telling them you aren't going to buy anything or giving them a set amount of money to spend. Also, we often find some really great places to eat when we're traveling, and while we only got ice cream while we were here, I can tell you that this isn't one of them.

name: Eric Salas
text: The place is a cute little tourist road stop, especially when you are on your way to the Black Hills, with all kinds of crazy gift stores along its short stretch. It is also close to the South Dakota Badlands, so making a side trip to The Wall is, sort of, given.

name: Matt Kruse
text: If you prepare yourself for the fact that it'll be an ungodly amount of people, a multitude of things that you most likely will not buy, and that there's a good chance you won't get seating for a meal, then you'll be ready to enjoy this place. The chocolate donuts really are great. And, if you have a child who loves stuffed animals, they have a very good selection of reasonably priced prairie themed stuffed animals. The best thing you can do though is either come right when they open in the summer, or better yet, come during the off season when it's a downright peaceful experience.

name: Natalie Acheson
text: We love to visit here on our way through at least once a year!  Always fun to catch up with our favorite dinosaur or ride the giant jackalope or play in the water fountains.  We always have fun looking in all the various shops and finding something exciting to keep the road trip fun.  Worth a stop for sure!!

name: Darlene Poppe
text: Great place.  Lots of things to see and do for all ages.  Was looking for a painting of a truck that says Mitchell, 2 people in front of a campfire and two horses behind them.  Sadly we were not able to find it.

name: Anna P
text: The stores are just on the average and expensive. Excellent donuts. Excellent bookstore. Charming building and lamps. Of historical interest are the  objects, pictures and paintings on the walls.

name: D.J. Truesdale
text: Visited years ago & thought it was amazing! But just visited a few weeks ago and was disappointed. Food is about as bland as it can get while prices are on the high side. Definitely worth stopping in Wall if visiting the Badlands!

name: Tabitha Moe
text: There is a lot of variety here. This place is huge. It's always a "must" to stop for me. Great food, ice cream, donuts and fudge. They have a huge art collection, chapel, arcade, gold panning, interactive water fountain, clothing stores, gifts, jewelry, toys, book store, oh.... And a drug store too. :) It has a bunch of fun and kitschy photo opps that always make me grab for my phone or camera.

name: Hannah Brown
text: Tourist, tourist, tourist. That said, it is a fun little stop with a variety of shops and galleries lining Main Street. Wall Drug itself has two parts: one being your mainstream gift shop with mass-made (foreign-made) products and merchandise; the other being an indoor replica of an old-time small-town main street with specialized shops for jewelry, books, leather goods, galleries & prints, pottery, candy, and more. A lot of the goods are made locally, or at least by individual artists from around the country. If you have the time, it's worth the stop if only to say that you did it.

name: cj
text: Wall to Wall people! See what I did there? It is a fun little break from the nothingness that is I-90 across South Dakota. It is definitely a crowded little place, however. I am not a fan of crowds but had a pretty good time here. We got a box of their "famous" donuts and they were quite tasty. My son has a common name but spelled in a  unique way and we were able to find him a key chain with it spelled how he spells it so that made him quite happy. For the most part, the stores sold the typical tourist stuff you find in any roadside tourist trap like this. I didn't really find anything unique that I could not live without. I'd recommend at least stopping to check it out. If anything, it gets you off the highway for a little bit.

text: My family has been stopping here for years. Yes it is touristy, yes most of the stuff is overpriced made in China junk, but there is a certain route 66 style, road side family attraction charm to this place. Being a history buff, I love their bookstore. I also like pocket knives, and their camping store has a pretty good selection of knives ($5 to $250). The backyard has an area with fountains that are synched to music that kids are allowed to play in. If you have not been to Wall drug, it is worth a look. If nothing else, it is a nice little oasis on the interstate to stretch your legs.

text: This place shines bright in all its tourist trap glory.  If you like such places, this place is a 'must do' if visiting the area or just passing through.  Plan to grab a bite because the tasty, old school cafeteria has over 500 seats busted into a few themed dining areas.  Then, after eating, walk it off by shopping the endless array of gifts, souvenirs, books, pottery, etc; or enjoy the dozens of photo ops in the 'backyard' featuring Mount Rushmore, trains, dinosaurs, a sprayground, and much much more.  (Oh yeah, there really is a drug store in there!)  So glad I stopped when passing through the area.

text:
Have you ever realized how many presidents there are? Well if you walk along this route, you definitely will. Here’s a suggestion that we came up with. From a distance, try to guess what President you’re approaching. It’s a lot of fun! When in doubt say Taft or Coolidge.

Plenty of opportunities for selfies with the Presidents. They have their whole bodies, and also various items that are appropriate to the presidency… Making them much better than the four faces on mount Rushmore.

Also, just a wonderful chance to walk past all the awesome businesses and restaurants that line the area.

name: Jennifer Peterson
text: This incredibly unique place has some thing for almost everyone centrally located in Keystone across from Museums coffee shops sightseeing and gas stations. Just get out your credit card and do this already because you know you want to and the memories are unforgettable we got pictures at the top of the hill. little kids four and up can participate in most rides with parental assistance. We didn’t eat here it we did every attraction except for the giant zip line tour (next time)  Gift shop and places to eat as well as restrooms clean and super friendly staff that are helpful and safe. Pristine views fun things to do at every turn as close to an actual amusement park as you’re going to get in the Black Hills & South Dakota . We had so much fun we went back the next day for more. Don’t forget sunscreen extra water, hats!

resp.text:
Jennifer-- we love that we can offer attractions that can suit all ages, even the littles ones can enjoy a relaxing ride up on the Chairlift! We also appreciate the awesome feedback about our facility and our staff.

The views of Mount Rushmore at the top while enjoying lunch or dinner makes it even better! I am hopeful you guys will be able to return the following season to experience our Pinnacle Zip line Tour! The tour consists of 5 Zip-line's that range from 400-1500 ft. long with heights up to 400 ft! We have our awesome tour guides that make the 2 hours even more memorable spent on the tour. Thanks again for the review!

name: Ourperfectlyimperfectlife
text: What a great way to spend the day to please both young and old adrenaline junkies. This place has it all! Beautiful view from the top of the chairlift along with grill and Cafe. Thrilling rides, including the Alpine Slide (you control the speed) and the tubing hill (VERY fast). The 800 ft zip line and the tree course were the big winners in our group of 6 (ranging in age from 9 to 51). We bought the Ultimate combination packet for the 4 kids and it was a great deal considering the individual prices of the various activities.  We will be back!!

resp.text: Thank you for taking your time to leave such a great review! We offer attractions for all ages, even littles ones are able to take a ride up the chairlift to see the beautiful view of Mount Rushmore. You save nearly 50% by purchasing the Ultimate Package-- we try our best to make it affordable for everyone! We appreciate your thorough review, and hope you guys will be able to return the following season!

name: Glenn Zior
text: A good variety of things to do. I found the aerial park to be challenging. After they show you how to clip in and off they send you on your way. Better not get scared because there is only one bail out point halfway through each course. I made it halfway through the medium difficulty. Looks like very few people even try the medium difficulty after making it through the easy course. It takes both balance and upper body strength. Alpine slide goes as fast as you dare. Tube slide and zip line are also fun. Lines flowed smoothly and all equipment was in working order.

name: Isaac
text: Very fun, helpful staff. This place has a very large and inticrate rope course and many zip lines. Kids need to be over 50 pounds so we took the younger ones on the luge slide.

name: tom callies
text: Very fun, beautiful scenery. Great guides with sense of humor.   Will definitely do it again.   May seem pricey but when you think about all the expenses involved with the zipline setup, cables, framing, platforms, equipment, insurance, utilities, fuel and employees, it's reasonable for 2 hrs. Great job guys!

name: Sodak Girl
text: This was such a cool place ! The alpine slide and the 800ft zipline were a blast !! The staff seemed very educated and friendly to us the whole time. Prices were kind if expensive when you go as a large group. However it was a great experience! Someday we will come back and try the zipline tour.

resp.text: Glad hear you enjoyed your time on our attractions. We offer discounted package to do our best to make it affordable for everyone. Thank you for your time leaving a review! We hope to see your group return for the Pinnacle Zip line Tour, it is a great experience!

text: The park is fun but a bit expensive if you have multiple children. All of the staff members where pleasant. The ticket booth wait was long bc there weren't any signs showing the prices for each ride. We had to wait until we reached an attendant before we saw the prices. This seemed to slow the line down. The restuarant is nice but they need help in the kitchen. BBQing the burgers to order is fine but the register is severely outdated and it took us about 15 minutes to place an order behind 2 people bc they didnt have enough workers to take orders and make drunks. So, it was about 45 minutes before we ate anything. Also, they should offer smaller burgers for children.

resp.text: Glad to hear the good feedback about our staff! We provide pricing in the waiver tent where you begin first. Thanks for giving us the feedback, we will try our best to be sure to pull people in the tent before getting to the ticket window. Hope you were able to still enjoy your food!

Suzanne,

text: Fun, Fun, Fun!!! Went on the tramway up to the top. Ate lunch at the restaurant at the top (delicious burgers and friendly staff).  Rode the slide back down which was a riot!! name: Eric Severson
text: Took my 6 year old on the alpine slide. I guess I was not fully aware how easy the sleds tip after some rushed instructions. We were having fun until we were almost to the bottom. We ended up flipping upside down, and skidding for quite a while. If we were provided with any type of glove,we would have been fine,but once I had to put my hand down to shield my son, all I could smell was burning flesh. I ended up with burns on my hands and legs almost down to the muscle(where my skin was oozing clear plasma). I admit, I was in control of the sled, and video taping(there is a sign in the front of the business with a father and son doing the same thing),so I was at fault for crashing. The part that bothered me about the alpine slide the most was that when we got off all bloody, and my son crying from pain,the employees just snatched the sled out of my hand and stacked it like nothing had happened. The same thing when we had to exit through the gift shop. Luckily we were within walking distance of our hotel where their front desk clerk immediately went and got us some 1st aid. Just a little compassion would have meant at least a couple more stars with my review.
